jobs.title: Senior Full-Stack Engineer
jobs.summary:
Jobbbler Demo Systems maintains a demo job catalog built to showcase the product's own workflow screens, and this senior engineering seat sits with the team that owns the search and matching views, where candidates and hiring managers spend most of their time in the product.

You take ownership of that surface end to end: a TypeScript and React frontend backed by a Node.js and PostgreSQL API, with the latitude to rewrite a slow query path rather than patch around it. A recent change pushed the two-hundred-result search render from twelve seconds to under one by moving filtering into the database, and the next piece applies that fix to the salary-range and location filters. Expect to design accessible list and detail views too, plus instrumentation that flags a slowdown early.

Required: production experience with TypeScript and React on the frontend, and with Node.js and PostgreSQL on the backend, including comfort writing and tuning non-trivial SQL queries rather than only calling an ORM. The seat is set at five to eight years of professional engineering experience. Prior exposure to accessibility auditing is useful but not required — a design partner covers that when it comes up, and the team will bring you up to speed.

The team works fully remote across the UK and Germany and ships small pull requests rather than long-lived branches, pairing on anything that touches the search index. You would report to the engineering lead for search and matching, who reviews architecture calls but leaves day-to-day implementation to you. The location-filter rewrite and keyboard navigation across the results grid are already scoped for the first quarter.

jobs.title: Product Design Lead
jobs.summary:
Inside Jobbbler's demo product, the assistive agent activity views were reading as loading spinners rather than a search actually happening, and a first-time viewer squinting at that screen during a demo recording is what pushed this design lead role onto the roadmap.

As design lead you set the interaction direction for that surface, turning research findings into flows that make an AI-assisted job search feel legible instead of magical. Day to day means running generative and evaluative sessions with people watching the demo cold, extending the shared design system with new patterns for agent status and progress, and pairing with engineers in Berlin to get prototypes into working code before the next recording. The next problem is a progress view for when an agent hits a captcha or login wall mid-search.

Required: fluency in Figma across exploration and production files, hands-on user research experience running both generative and evaluative sessions, and a track record extending a shared design system rather than working around it. The scope here sits at lead level: you set direction across a surface rather than accumulate a set number of years, though several years leading design work is the realistic floor. Deep coding ability is not required — engineers own implementation once a prototype holds up.

The role is hybrid out of Berlin, in the studio a few days a week for critique sessions that get genuinely argumentative before landing on a direction. You report to the head of product design, who expects decisions defended with research evidence rather than taste alone. The rest of the week is yours to arrange around research sessions and engineering pairing.

jobs.title: Technical Talent Partner
jobs.summary:
Running Jobbbler's internal demo organization day to day falls to just a five-person team, and hiring for that team now needs a dedicated recruiter rather than whichever engineer happens to have a free afternoon between sprints to sit in on interviews.

You design interview loops for software engineering and product roles, calibrate scorecards with hiring managers until they agree on what a strong answer looks like, and build sourcing plans that reach candidates outside the referral networks leaned on so far. A second focus is talent analytics: tracking pass-through rates by stage and pointing to where a loop introduces friction. Interview panels stay deliberately small, with a single structured debrief replacing the free-for-all discussion candidates describe from other processes.

Required: hands-on technical sourcing experience, comfort designing interview loops and calibrating scorecards with engineering hiring managers, and enough fluency with talent analytics to point to a specific stage rather than a vague impression. This seat calls for around six to eight years of recruiting experience, including some of it spent leading process changes rather than only running requisitions. Experience recruiting specifically for design roles is not required.

The position is onsite in London on a fixed-term contract, working alongside the small internal team that keeps the rest of the demo organization running. You report to the head of people operations for the length of the contract. Expect your first two weeks spent shadowing the existing loop before you are handed a live requisition to redesign on your own.

jobs.title: Principal Platform Engineer
jobs.summary:
Kubernetes clusters, Terraform modules, and a set of Go services stand between an internal team at Northstar Cloudworks and a new AWS environment they can provision themselves, and this principal role sets technical direction for that stack across every region the platform serves.

You decide when to introduce a new abstraction into the control plane versus extending what already exists, weigh multi-region capacity plans against real provisioning-time targets, and mentor senior engineers who are already deep in the codebase but need someone thinking two steps further out. Recent work cut average environment provisioning time and shrunk the blast radius of the last two outages, and the next stretch does the same for cross-region failover, which still requires a human to flip the switch today.

Required: deep hands-on Kubernetes experience, production Go services, and genuine infrastructure-as-code discipline in Terraform rather than borrowed modules nobody has read closely. Principal scope here means eight-plus years of infrastructure experience, most of it spent setting technical direction rather than only executing someone else's design. Direct AWS certification is not required — what matters is production judgment, not a badge.

Based anywhere in Europe or Canada, the role only pulls you into a room quarterly, for in-person planning weeks. You report to the VP of infrastructure and otherwise set your own priorities within the quarter's plan. Interviews spend real time walking through a past architecture decision you made and would make differently today.

jobs.title: Cloud Reliability Engineer
jobs.summary:
Overnight pages traced back to the same under-provisioned host pool went off three separate times in one quarter, and that pattern is what got capacity forecasting reprioritized on Northstar's small SRE team. This senior role owns both that forecasting work and the observability behind it.

You extend Prometheus dashboards and alerting so on-call engineers catch degradation before customers do, lead postmortems that turn incidents into concrete changes rather than vague action items, and build capacity plans from historical Linux host metrics instead of reacting to seasonal spikes after they hit. The forecasting model built from this work is expected to catch the next seasonal spike three weeks out instead of three days.

Required: real production experience running Linux systems at scale, fluency in Prometheus or an equivalent metrics stack, and a calm, structured approach to incident command under pressure at odd hours. Candidates should bring five to eight years of SRE or operations experience under their belt, with genuine on-call ownership rather than a rotation you only watch. Kubernetes experience is a plus but not required, since these host pools run mostly on bare Linux today.

The team gathers at the Toronto office twice a week and rotates a shared on-call schedule the rest of the time. You report to the SRE team lead and carry on-call on the same rotation as everyone else on the team. Interviews focus on walking through a past incident you handled end to end rather than an abstract whiteboard exercise.

jobs.title: Developer Support Engineer
jobs.summary:
Developers integrating with Northstar's infrastructure platform tend to hit the same handful of API and configuration snags, and closing the loop between answering those tickets and fixing the documentation that caused them is the whole point of this mid-level role.

You triage incoming support requests, reproduce integration problems in Python against the platform's own APIs, and write technical responses clear enough that a developer can act on them without a follow-up call. Part of the job runs the other direction too: shipping small documentation fixes and sample code yourself so the same question stops recurring within a sprint or two of first showing up, rather than filing a ticket against someone else's backlog.

Required: working Python skills for reproducing integration bugs, direct experience consuming or supporting APIs, and technical writing clear enough that a developer can self-serve from it. This is a mid-level seat, around three to five years of hands-on support or engineering experience. Prior experience with Northstar's specific stack is not required — the onboarding period is built around learning it from the ticket queue.

Based from Dublin or remote within Europe, the support queue is covered as a team rather than assigned to one person. You report to the support team lead and coordinate coverage with teammates across time zones within Europe. Resolution time gets tracked, but so does how often a documentation fix quietly eliminates a ticket type that used to show up weekly.

jobs.title: Staff Data Scientist
jobs.summary:
Copper Finch's forecasting models are accurate more often than not, yet a model a stakeholder cannot explain in plain language gets ignored at the next planning meeting no matter how good its numbers are, and closing that trust gap is what this staff role is built around.

You build and maintain explainable forecasting models in Python, backed by SQL pipelines pulling from the workspace's shared metrics tables, and design experiments checking whether a new model actually changes a decision for the better instead of just looking better on a dashboard. Because the role sits at staff level, you set technical direction for forecasting across multiple product teams instead of only shipping your own models one at a time.

Required: deep experience in applied forecasting, strong SQL for exploring genuinely messy production data, and a track record designing experiments that hold up under scrutiny from a skeptical stakeholder. Staff scope here means eight-plus years of applied data science experience. Deep learning experience is not required — the forecasting work here runs on simpler, more explainable model classes on purpose.

The team syncs over a couple of overlapping hours each week rather than fixed hours, fully remote and open globally. You report to the head of data science and set your own working hours around that sync window. Model reviews favor a written explanation of assumptions over a slide deck, and the next one on the calendar covers why the churn model's confidence interval widened last quarter.

jobs.title: Machine Learning Engineer
jobs.summary:
Customer data drifts constantly underneath Copper Finch's business intelligence product, and a model that scores well in a notebook and then quietly degrades in production is the specific failure this senior seat was created to catch before a customer notices.

You productionize model evaluation by wiring MLflow into the deployment path so every model version carries traceable metrics before it ships, and build feature store pipelines in Python, packaged with Docker, so data scientists reuse validated features instead of recomputing them per project. Engineers here get evaluated on how few surprises their pipelines produce once a model reaches customers, not on how clever the architecture looks in a design document nobody outside the team ever reads.

Required: comfort with MLflow or a comparable experiment tracking tool, real experience taking a model from notebook to production, and Docker fluency for packaging feature pipelines end to end. This senior seat calls for five to eight years of machine learning engineering experience, most of it spent productionizing other people's models. Deep statistical theory is not required — the emphasis here is shipping and monitoring, not model research.

Three days a week land at the Amsterdam office alongside the data science team, with the rest worked remotely. You report to the ML engineering lead, who reviews pipeline designs before they touch production data. The next pipeline on deck handles a churn model whose input distribution has already shifted twice this year.

jobs.title: Analytics Engineering Intern
jobs.summary:
Copper Finch's internal dashboards run on shared data models that a small analytics engineering team maintains, and this internship gives an early-career analyst a real seat on that team rather than a side project that gets built once and then nobody will touch again.

You help write and test SQL transformations in dbt, checking that new models match the definitions the business actually uses before a number reaches someone's dashboard. Data quality work fills out the rest of it: building simple checks that catch a broken pipeline before an analyst notices a chart looks wrong and starts asking questions in a shared channel, and pairing with a mentor on the team to review every model before it merges.

Required: some SQL experience, genuine curiosity about dbt or a similar transformation tool, and comfort using Git on a shared codebase you did not build yourself. This is an entry-level seat — no professional experience is required, though coursework or a personal project touching SQL counts for a lot toward how you are evaluated. Prior production dbt experience is not required; that is what the internship is designed to teach.

The internship runs onsite from the Montreal office so you can pair directly with the analytics engineers who own the models you will be touching. You report to the analytics engineering lead for the length of the internship, with a short check-in most weeks. You will leave with a concrete portfolio of dbt models and data quality checks that actually shipped to production.

jobs.title: Senior Product Manager
jobs.summary:
Blue Lantern greenlit this senior product management role after a roadmap built purely on internal opinion, with no customer conversation behind it, underperformed hard at launch, and leadership wanted a standing owner to make sure that exact mistake never repeats.

You run discovery interviews with existing customers to validate problems before committing engineering time, then translate what you learn into a roadmap the team can actually execute against rather than one that just reads well in a slide. Expect to work daily with engineering and design leads to sequence work, and with leadership to defend tradeoffs using usage analytics instead of opinion whenever a decision gets seriously contested in the room.

Required: a history of owning a roadmap from customer conversation through shipped feature, comfort reading product analytics without a dedicated analyst on call, and direct experience running discovery interviews yourself rather than delegating them. The role sits at five to eight years of product management experience. Experience in B2B collaboration tools specifically is not required, though it does shorten the ramp-up over the first month or two.

The product trio is co-located at the Paris office two days a week, with the rest of the week flexible. You report to the VP of product and present roadmap changes at a monthly review alongside your engineering and design counterparts. That review walks through what changed in customer behavior since the last one and what that shift means for the next sprint.

jobs.title: UX Researcher
jobs.summary:
Two competing redesigns of the same onboarding flow, backed by nothing but each team's gut feeling, convinced Blue Lantern's leadership to fund a dedicated research contract instead of letting the next design disagreement play out exactly the same way it just did.

You plan and run generative interviews to uncover unmet needs, then follow up with usability testing once a design is ready to validate, synthesizing findings into something a product team can act on without reading a lengthy report first. Research operations rounds things out: recruiting participants, maintaining a shared repository of past findings, and making sure earlier research does not get re-litigated from scratch every time someone forgets it exists.

Required: comfort running generative and evaluative studies independently, strong synthesis skills, and enough operational rigor to keep a research pipeline moving without support staff behind you. This is a mid-level engagement, roughly three to five years of applied UX research experience. Prior experience specifically with collaboration or productivity software is not required, though it helps you read the domain faster.

Candidates anywhere in Europe can take this on fully remotely, on a contract that renews rather than ending on a fixed date. You report to the head of research operations for the length of the engagement. Findings ship as short recorded walkthroughs rather than lengthy written reports, since teams here rarely have time to read the latter before their next planning meeting.

jobs.title: Design Systems Engineer
jobs.summary:
Blue Lantern's shared React component library has quietly accumulated three different button implementations across three product teams, and untangling that kind of drift while keeping accessibility intact is the daily reality behind this freelance lead role.

You build and maintain component tooling in React and CSS, extend the Storybook setup so every component ships with documented states and props, and run accessibility checks that catch contrast and keyboard-navigation problems before a component ever reaches a product team. Carrying lead scope also means setting conventions for how new components get proposed and reviewed across teams that do not currently talk to each other much about this.

Required: strong React and CSS fundamentals, hands-on accessibility auditing experience, and comfort maintaining Storybook as a living source of truth rather than a neglected side project. The scope here is lead-level: setting conventions other teams follow, not a specific year count, though several years of production component work is the realistic floor. Visual design skill is not required — a separate design team owns that layer.

The engagement is freelance with flexible hours, based from Lisbon or remote within Europe, billed hourly against agreed milestones. You report to the engineering director sponsoring the initiative and coordinate directly with the teams consuming the library. Component changes now ship behind a documented deprecation path, which is the first thing you will be asked to formalize.

jobs.title: Application Security Engineer
jobs.summary:
Payment-handling code shipped last year with a threat model nobody had actually reviewed, and ParcelSignal's security team now embeds directly with the engineers who build its logistics platform, rather than sitting apart as a late-stage gate, specifically to avoid a repeat.

In this senior role you run threat modeling sessions before major features are built, not after, helping product engineers see failure modes they would otherwise miss until a customer finds them first. You own the SAST tooling running against a primarily Java codebase, tuning rules so findings stay actionable instead of drowning teams in noise, and conduct focused security reviews on the riskiest parts of the platform, including payment and address-handling code specifically.

Required: hands-on Java experience, real threat modeling practice, and the communication skill to make a finding land as help rather than criticism in a review thread. The role is set at five to eight years of application security or software engineering experience with a security focus. A background in compliance auditing is not required — this is a hands-on engineering role, not a paperwork one.

The security team meets synchronously twice a week and otherwise works async, fully remote for candidates in the United States or Canada. You report to the head of application security. Progress gets tracked by how early in the development cycle an issue gets caught, and the next push is moving that catch point from code review back to the design doc.

jobs.title: Security Operations Analyst
jobs.summary:
ParcelSignal's security operations center pulls signals from a dozen different log sources across the logistics platform, and making sense of all of it before individual alerts turn into real incidents is the daily work behind this mid-level analyst role on a growing team.

You investigate alerts inside the SIEM, correlating signals across logging sources to separate genuine threats from noise, and write and refine detection rules so the same false positive stops reappearing every week without anyone touching it by hand. When something real does happen, you follow and help improve the incident response playbooks, documenting what worked and what did not so the next analyst on shift benefits from what you learned instead of relearning it live.

Required: hands-on SIEM experience, comfort scripting investigative tooling in Python, and the patience to document findings clearly in the middle of an active shift. This is a mid-level seat, roughly three to five years of security operations experience. Prior experience specifically in logistics or shipping is not required — the threat intelligence work happening alongside you will bring you up to speed on that context quickly.

Shifts are set at the Austin operations center, on the same pattern as the rest of the security team rather than a flexible schedule. You report to the SOC shift lead. New analysts spend their first weeks shadowing a senior teammate on live alerts before taking primary ownership of a full shift on their own, typically within the first month or so.

jobs.title: Privacy Engineering Manager
jobs.summary:
Personal data collection went unchecked in a data model ParcelSignal shipped two releases ago, and catching that kind of gap earlier, well before an audit ever surfaces it, is now the entire mandate behind this manager role and the small team built around it.

You lead privacy-by-design reviews on new features, working with product and engineering leads early enough to change a data model before it ships rather than patch it after. Data governance is the other half of the job: maintaining a clear inventory of what personal data the platform collects, why, and how long it is retained. You also run structured risk assessments on new integrations and vendors, and as a people manager you grow one or two privacy engineers on your team.

Required: hands-on privacy engineering experience, comfort using formal risk assessment frameworks, and prior experience leading a small team rather than only individual contributor work. This seat calls for around six to nine years of overall experience, including some time spent managing others directly. A legal background is not required — the legal team handles interpretation; this role handles engineering follow-through.

Three days a week bring in-person reviews at the Stockholm office; the rest of the week is yours to arrange. You report to the VP of security and privacy, and manage one to two privacy engineers directly. The team's current stretch goal is catching every privacy gap during design review, well before a last-minute escalation lands on someone's desk.

jobs.title: Site Reliability Engineer
jobs.summary:
Juniper Grid secured real budget for this senior reliability seat after a regional outage traced back to an under-provisioned cluster, since its energy infrastructure platform moves the data pipelines that grid operators actually rely on for real-time decisions in the field.

You operate and harden the Kubernetes clusters running those pipelines, building Grafana dashboards that surface degradation before it becomes an outage rather than after operators start calling in. You also maintain the Terraform modules used to provision new infrastructure, keeping environments consistent across every region the platform serves, and carry a share of on-call, running blameless postmortems that turn recurring pain points into permanent fixes.

Required: real production Kubernetes experience, working knowledge of Grafana or a comparable observability stack, and the calm judgment on-call work demands at three in the morning. Five to eight years of infrastructure or SRE experience is the benchmark here, most of it carrying a live pager. Deep Terraform module authorship is useful but not required — reading and extending existing modules covers most of the work.

Twice a week the team gathers at the Warsaw office, and on-call runs through a shared rotation with clear escalation paths the rest of the time. You report to the infrastructure engineering manager. Engineers here are expected to leave every incident with at least one concrete follow-up action, and the outage mentioned above already has three assigned.

jobs.title: Network Automation Engineer
jobs.summary:
Manual network changes living in one engineer's head, undocumented anywhere else, caused Juniper Grid's last two major outages, and replacing them with Ansible playbooks wired into a CI/CD pipeline is the entire point of this lead contract role right now.

You design and build the playbooks that codify network changes, and wire them into a pipeline so changes get tested before they ever touch production hardware. Alongside the automation work, you write Python tooling that validates network state against intent, catching drift before it causes an incident rather than after. As the lead on this initiative, you set standards for how new automation gets reviewed and bring the networking team along rather than automating around them.

Required: strong networking fundamentals, hands-on Ansible experience, and comfort building CI/CD pipelines for infrastructure rather than only application code. The scope here is lead-level: setting the standard other engineers follow, not a fixed year count, though several solid years of prior networking experience are assumed going in. Prior experience specifically with this vendor's hardware is not required.

This is a fixed-term contract based onsite at the Denver office, working closely with the operations team whose manual processes you are replacing. You report to the networking operations manager for the length of the contract. Rollouts are staged deliberately, starting on non-critical segments of the network before any playbook touches core infrastructure.

jobs.title: Infrastructure Program Director
jobs.summary:
Two infrastructure teams at Juniper Grid discovered last year that they were both blocked on the same vendor delivery, three weeks after it started costing them time, and preventing that kind of silent dependency now falls to this part-time director role.

You track cross-team infrastructure initiatives end to end, surfacing where one team's timeline quietly depends on another's and forcing that dependency into the open before it causes a slip. Risk management fills out the rest of the role: maintaining a live register of infrastructure risks and making sure the right leader owns mitigation for each one. You also manage relationships with external vendors supplying hardware and managed services, holding them accountable to commitments operations teams depend on downstream.

Required: real program management experience across infrastructure or operations organizations, comfort with formal risk management practice, and the credibility to hold vendors and internal teams to the same standard. Director scope here is about breadth of accountability across teams, not a specific year count, though this is not a first program management role. Deep technical hands-on infrastructure experience is not required — the role coordinates, rather than builds.

The role is part-time at twenty-five hours a week, with flexible scheduling, open to candidates globally, structured around a standing weekly program review. You report to the head of infrastructure operations. The first assignment is untangling that exact vendor dependency mentioned above before it quietly delays either team's roadmap for the quarter.

jobs.title: Senior QA Automation Engineer
jobs.summary:
Three separate partner integrations broke in the same release last quarter, and only one of them had automated coverage that caught the break before a partner noticed it first; closing that same gap across the rest of the suite is now this senior QA role's entire job.

You write and maintain end-to-end test suites in Playwright and TypeScript, covering the checkout and integration flows partners depend on most heavily, and build API-level tests that exercise the integration layer directly, catching contract breaks earlier than a full browser test ever would. You also own the CI/CD pipeline running this suite, keeping it fast and reliable enough that engineers trust a red build instead of rerunning it two or three times and hoping it eventually passes.

Required: strong TypeScript skills, hands-on Playwright experience, and a track record of keeping a large test suite maintainable rather than letting it slowly rot into something nobody trusts anymore. The role is set at five to eight years of QA or software engineering experience. Experience specifically with partner or marketplace integrations is not required, though it does help you ramp up faster.

The quality team syncs a few times a week and otherwise works independently; candidates anywhere in Europe can apply, fully remote, full-time. You report to the QA engineering lead, who reviews the suite's overall health weekly. Flaky tests get fixed or deleted within the sprint they are found rather than left ignored indefinitely.

jobs.title: Quality Engineering Manager
jobs.summary:
Orbit Orchard's engineering organization has grown much faster than its quality practice could keep pace with, and the resulting confusion over who actually owns testing on any given feature is the specific problem now landing on this manager role to resolve for good.

You define how testing responsibility splits between dedicated QA engineers and feature teams, then coach engineers on both sides until that split actually works in practice rather than only on paper. Test architecture takes up a good share of the job too: deciding where automated coverage belongs in the stack and retiring redundant tests that slow builds without catching real bugs anymore. You also own release management, deciding what quality bar a release must clear and holding that line even under schedule pressure.

Required: hands-on test architecture experience, proven coaching ability, and enough backbone to say a release is not ready when the data supports it. This seat calls for around six to nine years of quality engineering experience, including some time spent managing others directly. Experience with a specific test framework beyond the basics is not required — the team already has conventions in place.

Three days a week bring the team together at the Vancouver office, with async coverage the rest of the time. You report to the VP of engineering and manage a small team of QA engineers directly. You also represent quality tradeoffs in cross-functional planning meetings alongside product and engineering leads.

jobs.title: Performance Test Specialist
jobs.summary:
Peak traffic on Orbit Orchard's high-volume marketplace platform exposed a bottleneck last quarter that no test caught until customers started noticing slow checkouts, and this freelance role exists specifically to find the next one before that happens again.

You design and run load and stress tests using k6, scripting realistic traffic patterns in JavaScript that mirror how the marketplace actually gets used during peak periods rather than an idealized average day. Once a test run completes, you dig into the resulting metrics to identify which specific service or query is the limiting factor, rather than reporting a vague slowdown and moving on. You also work with engineering teams to validate that a proposed fix actually improves the numbers before it ships to production.

Required: hands-on k6 experience, comfort scripting in JavaScript, and the analytical patience to trace a performance regression back to its root cause rather than its first symptom. This is a mid-level engagement, roughly three to five years of performance testing or backend engineering experience. Deep infrastructure provisioning experience is not required — a separate platform team already handles that layer.

The engagement runs onsite from the Prague office, tied to specific testing campaigns around major releases. You report to the quality engineering manager for the length of each campaign. Every finding ships with a reproducible test script, so a fix can be verified against the exact load profile that exposed the problem.

jobs.title: Developer Advocate
jobs.summary:
Developers joining Lattice's collaboration network tend to trip on the exact same integration step early on, and turning that recurring friction into clear technical education instead of another support ticket is the entire point of this senior advocate role.

You write tutorials and sample applications in JavaScript that show real integration patterns rather than toy examples nobody uses, and speak at developer conferences and meetups to explain how the platform gets used in practice. Community building runs through the role too: showing up in forums and community channels consistently enough that developers trust you to answer. You also work closely with the product team, turning developer confusion into concrete product and documentation gaps rather than a vague complaint that goes nowhere.

Required: strong technical writing skills, genuine comfort speaking publicly, and enough hands-on JavaScript experience to build credible sample projects rather than borrowed ones. The role sits at roughly five to eight years of developer relations or software engineering experience. Prior conference speaking experience is useful but not required — coaching on that is part of onboarding here for whoever joins.

Travel to a handful of conferences a year is built into this fully remote, globally open, full-time role. You report to the head of developer relations. A community-reported issue turning into a shipped fix within the same quarter is the outcome the role is actually built to produce, more often than not.

jobs.title: Open Source Program Manager
jobs.summary:
Two Lattice maintainers quietly burned out and stopped responding within the same month last year, and neither the community nor the internal team noticed until contributions on their repositories had already stalled; keeping that from happening again is what this manager role is meant to do.

You coordinate maintainers across several repositories, making sure contribution guidelines and review expectations stay consistent instead of varying by whichever maintainer happens to respond first that week. Program management is a big piece of it: running a predictable release cadence across projects and tracking maintainer workload so burnout gets caught early. You also own governance decisions and round things out with community operations, from moderating discussion spaces to organizing periodic contributor calls.

Required: real open source program experience, comfort designing governance structures, and the interpersonal skill to manage volunteers who cannot simply be assigned work. This seat calls for around six to nine years of relevant experience, including some time spent managing programs or people directly. Deep hands-on coding ability is not required — the maintainers own the code; this role owns the process around it.

New York anchors the role three days a week; maintainers scattered across time zones account for the rest. You report to the head of developer relations directly. Contributor calls and release cadence reviews happen on a predictable schedule, which is itself part of what this role was created to establish.

jobs.title: Documentation Engineer
jobs.summary:
Lattice's API platform ships new endpoints faster than its reference docs can keep up, and an endpoint that shipped with documentation still wrong three weeks later is roughly how long stale docs tend to survive without one dedicated owner watching the gap.

You write and maintain reference documentation directly against the API surface, in Markdown, structured so a developer can find an answer without reading unrelated sections first just to locate one parameter. Information architecture takes up real time too: reorganizing navigation and cross-linking as the API grows, rather than letting new pages pile up wherever they were easiest to add. You also build small working examples that demonstrate each endpoint in context.

Required: hands-on API experience, strong Markdown-based writing skills, and an eye for information architecture rather than just clean prose. This is a mid-level seat, roughly three to five years of technical writing or documentation engineering experience, ideally including some API documentation specifically. Prior experience with this specific platform is not required — the first weeks are built around learning it from the inside.

The role is part-time at twenty hours a week. Based from Helsinki or remote within Europe, it coordinates asynchronously with the rest of the developer relations team. You report to the head of developer relations, and every documentation change now ships in the same pull request as the API change that prompted it, reviewed together rather than separately.

jobs.title: Senior Solutions Engineer
jobs.summary:
Eighteen months ago, a prospect's engineering team walked out of a generic product demo with more questions than they came in with, and that specific failure convinced Beaconline to build this senior solutions role around real technical evaluations instead of one-size-fits-all decks.

You run discovery calls that dig into a prospect's existing systems and workflows, surfacing integration questions that would otherwise only appear after purchase, and design a solution architecture tailored to what you actually learn rather than a template. Hands-on proof-of-concept work fills the rest of it: building working integrations against the platform's APIs so a prospect's engineers see real data flowing instead of a slide describing it. You also deliver technical presentations across audiences from individual engineers to executives.

Required: genuine API fluency, strong discovery instincts, and the presentation range to adjust technical depth without losing accuracy in either direction. The role is set at five to eight years of solutions engineering or software engineering experience, most of it spent in front of technical prospects. Deep sales methodology training is not required — an assigned account executive owns that half of every deal.

You work closely with an assigned account executive on every deal, fully remote for candidates in the United States or Canada. You report to the solutions engineering manager. The proof-of-concept environments built during the sales cycle get handed directly to the implementation team once a deal closes, so what ships here has to hold up well past the demo.

jobs.title: Technical Account Manager
jobs.summary:
Beaconline's workflow automation product frequently sits half-configured a month after signing, and this manager role exists inside customer engineering to close that adoption gap before it turns into churn. The team owns the post-sale relationship for a portfolio of accounts, turning stated goals into a concrete adoption plan rather than a generic onboarding checklist.

Building a structured adoption roadmap for each account comes first, translating stated goals into specific configuration and workflow changes rather than generic template advice. Querying usage data in SQL is a weekly habit, meant to catch stalled adoption before the customer raises a complaint. When a blocker turns out to be a product gap rather than a training issue, you run the cross-functional fix, and translate what the platform's logs show into terms a stakeholder can act on.

Required: five to eight years in a customer-facing technical role such as account management or customer success, with genuine SQL fluency for self-serve analysis. Project management skill matters too: running a cross-functional effort and holding stakeholders to a deadline. Direct people-management experience is not required, since the seat carries no direct reports; the technical communication skill that matters most is translating logs into terms an account executive can repeat with confidence.

Two to three days a week are spent at the Chicago office with the rest of customer engineering, the remainder flexible. Account health is reviewed every quarter directly against usage data pulled from the platform, in a session the assigned account executive also attends. Supervision here comes from the customer engineering director, on a standard full-time schedule.

jobs.title: Customer Support Systems Administrator
jobs.summary:
Support agents inside Beaconline lose real time every week to manual steps buried inside tools they already use daily, and finding that friction rather than adding another workaround on top of it is what this mid-level role is for. It sits inside customer engineering, administering the Zendesk instance the entire support org runs on.

Day to day, you build workflow automations that route and prioritize tickets by customer impact instead of arrival order in the queue, and write SQL queries against support data for dashboards that show leadership where response times are slipping before it becomes customer-facing. You also maintain the integrations between Zendesk and internal systems, keeping agent-facing context accurate as those systems change, and sit with agents to see where automation actually helps.

Required: three to five years administering a ticketing platform such as Zendesk in a production support environment, plus solid SQL for building reporting from a blank slate rather than a template someone else built. You should be able to read a support workflow and see where a rule would help before an agent asks for one. Deep front-end development experience is not required; this is a systems and data role, not a product engineering one.

This one is based onsite at the Madrid office, full time, alongside the rest of the support team every day. New automations roll out to a small pilot group before going live for everyone, catching unintended side effects early rather than at scale. The role reports to the support operations manager.

jobs.title: Technical Recruiter
jobs.summary:
Talent Kernel Labs builds hiring workflow software, which means its own recruiting process gets watched more closely than most, and a candidate's public complaint about an inconsistent interview loop last year is a real part of why this senior role now owns recruiting for product and engineering.

Full-cycle technical recruiting is the core of the job, from sourcing plans that reach engineers who are not actively job hunting through closing offers against candidates weighing other options. Candidate experience matters too: every applicant should leave with an accurate impression of the company, since a bad experience undermines the product being sold. Hiring analytics rounds out the role, tracking time-to-fill and pass-through rates to find where the funnel is broken, and you partner with hiring managers on scoping.

Required: five to eight years of full-cycle technical recruiting, including direct sourcing experience for hard-to-fill engineering roles rather than relying only on inbound applicants. You should be able to read a funnel report and know which stage actually needs attention first. Recruiting for non-technical functions is not part of this role, which stays scoped specifically to product and engineering hiring.

Coordination happens across a few overlapping working hours each day with hiring managers and the rest of a small talent team, fully remote for candidates based anywhere in Europe, with no fixed office to report into and no travel expected. The position reports to the head of talent, who reviews pipeline health with the team each week.

jobs.title: Recruiting Operations Specialist
jobs.summary:
Every recruiter's smooth-looking interview loop at Talent Kernel Labs sits on top of an operations function that keeps the underlying system consistent, fair and measurable, and a recent audit finding two requisitions with mismatched approval records is exactly the kind of gap this mid-level role exists to close.

You administer the applicant tracking system, configuring workflows and permissions so recruiters and hiring managers see the information they need at each stage. Process design takes up a good share of the work too: documenting the steps every requisition follows, from approval through offer, so quality does not depend on which recruiter owns a search that week. You also own recruiting reporting, building dashboards that track funnel health and pipeline diversity, and keep compliance current.

Required: three to five years of hands-on ATS administration on a platform such as Greenhouse or Lever, plus process design experience turning an informal habit into a documented, repeatable step. Comfort with reporting tools and a working knowledge of compliance requirements around interview documentation both matter here. Prior recruiting quota or sourcing experience is not required, since this role supports recruiters rather than carrying its own req load.

Boston anchors this one two to three days a week, with the rest worked from wherever suits, on a standard full-time schedule. The first concrete project is closing the mismatched-approval-record gap the recent audit surfaced, then documenting the fix so it does not quietly reopen next quarter. Recruiting operations' head is this role's manager.

jobs.title: Candidate Experience Designer
jobs.summary:
Candidate experience at Talent Kernel Labs has been left to whoever had time between reqs, and an exit survey this spring described the company's own recruiting product more accurately than its marketing did. That uncomfortable moment is why this senior contract role now owns researching and redesigning the candidate-facing moments nobody else has time for.

You conduct user research directly with recent candidates, hired and rejected, to understand where communication felt unclear or a status update arrived too late to matter. From that research you build journey maps tracing a candidate's path from application through decision, pinpointing where trust is won or lost rather than describing the process in the abstract. Using a service design lens, you propose concrete changes to messaging, timing and interface a product team can implement.

Required: five to eight years of service design or UX research experience, with real skill at journey mapping and a portfolio that includes qualitative research synthesized into a shipped design change rather than a slide deck. Recruiting-specific background is a plus, not a prerequisite, since the research skill transfers and the domain gets picked up quickly. You do not need prior in-house recruiting experience to do this work well.

The engagement is a flexible contract open to candidates based in Toronto or remote across North America, structured around specific milestones rather than fixed weekly hours. There is no set office schedule to keep. The contract runs through recruiting operations, which reviews deliverables at each milestone.

jobs.title: Revenue Operations Analyst
jobs.summary:
RelayForge's sales pipeline lost a deal's real status for the third quarter running last year, marked as closing when it had actually slipped, with no field updated to explain why. This mid-level role exists to fix that data-trust problem at the source rather than paper over it with a better-looking dashboard.

You maintain and improve the Salesforce data model the whole revenue organization reports from, closing gaps that let deals slip through stages without the fields needed to forecast accurately. Forecasting is a core part of the job: building SQL-based models that combine historical close rates with current pipeline data to give leadership a number they can plan around rather than a rep's optimistic guess. You also build data visualizations that make pipeline health legible at a glance.

Required: three to five years working directly in Salesforce as an administrator or analyst, with SQL skills strong enough to build a forecasting model from raw pipeline data rather than a pivot table, plus comfort building the data visualization that makes that model usable to a skeptical sales leader. Formal data-science training is not required; this role runs on SQL and Salesforce fluency, not machine learning.

San Francisco is home base three days a week for this one, with the balance worked remotely on a standard full-time schedule. Because RelayForge sells operations intelligence software itself, there is a real internal expectation that its own reporting practice sets a credible example. The director of revenue operations is who this analyst answers to.

jobs.title: Technical Operations Lead
jobs.summary:
Release trains at RelayForge carry a rotating cast of engineering teams into the same weekly window, and until a release two Fridays ago took checkout down for forty minutes, nobody owned coordinating whose changes actually belonged in which window. This lead role now does, sitting inside technical operations.

You own release management end to end, deciding the criteria a release must meet before it ships and coordinating the handful of teams whose work lands in any given window regardless of who asked first. When something goes wrong, you lead the incident directly to resolution and then run the retrospective that turns it into a permanent fix rather than a patch everyone forgets. Automation is a real part of the work too: finding the manual steps that keep causing near-misses and removing them.

Required: a genuine track record in release management and incident management at a growing company, not a first attempt at either, plus real comfort building automation rather than adding another manual checklist step. Leadership matters just as much as the technical depth: you set priorities for a small group of operations engineers and unblock their work rather than doing all of it personally. Prior experience with RelayForge's specific tech stack is not required, since the process discipline transfers.

Seattle is the daily base: onsite, full time, five days a week, alongside the operations engineers you lead. The pager rotates through the team rather than sitting permanently with any one person, including this role. Reporting is to the VP of engineering, with real latitude over how release windows are run.

jobs.title: Sales Engineer
jobs.summary:
Deals at RelayForge stall when a prospect's integration question outruns what an account executive can answer alone, and a six-figure deal that sat stuck for two weeks over a single API question is exactly the kind of stall this senior role exists to prevent. It sits alongside the sales team, paired with account executives across regions.

Technical discovery calls come first, digging into a prospect's existing operations stack to identify integration points and edge cases a generic product demo would never surface. From that discovery, you design and deliver solution demonstrations against the platform's APIs, building live examples that answer a prospect's actual integration question rather than a rehearsed scenario. You also maintain accurate technical notes inside the CRM so account executives and customer success inherit the same understanding.

Required: five to eight years in a pre-sales or solution engineering role working directly with APIs, plus discovery instincts sharp enough to ask a credible technical question on the first call rather than the third. Comfort keeping a CRM current under deal pressure matters as much as the demo itself. Deep experience in any one specific vertical is not required, since deals here span industries with genuinely different operational needs.

Time zones stay flexible since the role is paired with account executives across regions rather than tied to a single one; work is fully remote and open globally. Travel to a customer site happens occasionally but is not the default way deals get worked. Sales engineering's head is the manager on record for this role.

jobs.title: Frontend Engineering Director
jobs.summary:
TidalFrame's real-time collaboration scene dropped to eleven frames per second on a mid-range laptop during a demo a few releases back, and that specific moment is why frontend architecture and performance became a genuine competitive constraint here rather than a nice-to-have. This director role now owns both, reporting into engineering leadership.

Architectural calls come first: determining whether the React codebase stays maintainable as the product adds demanding real-time features, weighing new abstractions against the cost of teaching the team to use them well. Web performance work runs through nearly everything: setting performance budgets and deciding which experiences are too heavy to ship as designed. You also grow a group of engineering managers and senior engineers while staying technical enough to review the decisions that matter most.

Required: deep, current React experience plus a genuine track record improving web performance at scale and making architecture calls that stuck, since this role is expected to defend specific tradeoffs rather than set direction in the abstract. People leadership scope matters just as much as the technical depth: you should have led engineering managers before, not only individual engineers. A background in native mobile development is not required; the surface here is entirely the web client.

Three days a week the leadership team convenes at the Los Angeles office for planning and architecture review, with the rest worked flexibly. This director answers to the VP of engineering and represents frontend engineering in cross-functional planning so performance constraints shape the roadmap early. Direct reports include engineering managers and senior individual contributors.

jobs.title: Senior Product Researcher
jobs.summary:
Two participants in TidalFrame's recent usability session described the identical collaboration feature in opposite terms, one calling it seamless and the other confusing, and reconciling contradictions like that is the daily work behind this senior research role. It sits inside the product organization, embedded with the team building TidalFrame's immersive collaboration product.

Mixed-method research anchors the role, combining structured interviews with behavioral data from inside the product, since collaboration habits in an immersive environment often do not match what participants say in an interview alone. Prototyping speculative workflows matters too: building rough concepts that let the team test a future direction with real users before engineering commits meaningful time. Synthesis is where the role earns its keep, turning feedback into strategy recommendations a manager can act on.

Required: five to eight years of mixed-method research experience, with hands-on prototyping ability strong enough to build a rough interactive concept without waiting on a designer, and the synthesis skill to turn both into a product strategy recommendation someone can act on. Formal training in immersive or spatial design is not required, since the research methods transfer across product categories.

Research is reviewed in a standing session leadership is expected to actually attend, on a fully remote schedule open to candidates in Europe or the United States. Working hours flex around that one recurring session rather than a fixed daily block. The position reports to the head of product research.

jobs.title: Chief Technology Officer
jobs.summary:
TidalFrame's platform is expanding into AI-assisted features fast enough that technology strategy and responsible AI practice can no longer be treated as separate conversations, and a feature that launched last quarter without a documented fairness review, caught only after the fact, is exactly the kind of gap this executive role exists to close.

Multi-year technology strategy comes first: deciding where to invest in new architecture versus consolidate what exists, with credibility across the organization so the strategy survives quarterly board pressure. AI governance is a defined mandate rather than an afterthought: establishing how AI-assisted features get evaluated for risk and fairness before launch, with real authority to delay a launch when it matters. Security sits alongside AI governance as a first-class responsibility, and you build the executive leadership team beneath you.

Required: a genuine track record setting technology strategy at scale, including direct experience standing up an AI governance practice and making security tradeoffs at the architecture level rather than delegating them entirely. Executive-level scope is the bar here rather than a specific year count: you should have run a technology organization through a period of real strategic change before. Deep personal expertise in every domain the org covers is not required, since the executive leadership team you build carries that depth collectively.

The role is flexible, based from London with global reach across the organization, and travel to meet regional teams and the board happens on an as-needed basis rather than a fixed schedule. The CTO reports to the CEO and sits on the executive leadership team. No fixed office attendance is expected.

jobs.title: Software Engineering Intern, Climate Data Platform
jobs.summary:
Wrenfield's data platform team maintains the ingestion pipelines that pull satellite imagery, weather-station readings and industrial sensor feeds into the risk models insurers and utilities rely on daily. This internship places you directly on that team for the length of the program, working alongside two mentor engineers rather than in a separate training track.

You build small services in Python that validate and normalize incoming sensor batches, write SQL transformations against the climate data warehouse, and add test coverage to ingestion jobs that currently rely on manual spot-checks. You also shadow the on-call rotation for a few shifts to see how the team investigates a pipeline failure when a weather-station feed goes quiet. The wider data platform group is about a dozen engineers, and roughly half of past interns have received a full-time offer.

Required: coursework or personal-project fundamentals in Python and SQL; no prior professional experience is expected for this internship. Familiarity with Git and basic REST APIs helps you get moving faster in the first weeks, and Docker exposure is a bonus rather than a prerequisite. Interviews consist of a short take-home exercise and a conversation about how you approached it, not a live whiteboard session.

This is a fixed-term internship based hybrid out of the Berlin office, with the specific in-office days set by the mentor engineers you pair with. Genuine curiosity tends to matter more than a polished resume for this one. The internship reports to a mentor engineer on the data platform team, with the wider team available for questions.

jobs.title: Junior Backend Engineer, Risk Scoring APIs
jobs.summary:
Underwriters pricing climate risk on individual properties and portfolios depend on dashboards backed by internal APIs that Wrenfield's risk-scoring backend team keeps expanding, and this junior role is a deliberate first step into professional backend work rather than one assuming prior production experience.

New API endpoints in Python come first, alongside fixing bugs surfaced through the support queue when an underwriter reports a score that looks wrong and keeping documentation current as the data model evolves. A mentor engineer reviews your pull requests closely for the first several months, and the team runs a short weekly pairing session for engineers early in their career. The risk-scoring team has roughly doubled in headcount over the past year as more insurance customers came on board.

Required: a foundation in Python, PostgreSQL and basic REST APIs from coursework, a bootcamp or personal projects, plus a habit of asking questions rather than guessing when something is unclear. Zero years of professional experience is fine for this opening; it exists specifically for engineers early in their career. Prior exposure to Git and Docker is useful during onboarding but is taught on the job rather than assumed going in.

This role is based onsite at the Berlin office, full time, working alongside the rest of the backend team every day. Code review is treated as a teaching tool, and the team is genuinely patient with engineers still building judgment about what production code should look like. The role reports to the risk-scoring backend lead.

jobs.title: Associate Software Engineer, Data Source Integrations
jobs.summary:
Insurers, utilities and agricultural customers keep asking Wrenfield to add new external data sources to its climate risk platform, and the integrations squad is the small team that turns each request into a working connector. This associate role focuses on building and maintaining individual integrations against satellite providers, weather services and sensor networks.

Typical weeks involve writing Node.js services that pull and normalize data from a partner's API, adding retry and error-handling logic for feeds that are not always reliable, and verifying output against known-good historical readings before a connector goes live. You work closely with a senior engineer who reviews your pull requests daily during your first few months and more loosely once you have shipped a couple of connectors independently. The backlog includes about a dozen requested data sources.

Required: some exposure to JavaScript, ideally including Node.js, plus comfort with REST APIs and basic Git fluency for a normal pull-request workflow. No set number of years is expected for this associate-level opening. Deep PostgreSQL tuning knowledge is not required going in, since most of what a specific integration needs gets picked up while building it, and the team's shared runbook of past gotchas fills in the rest.

Amsterdam anchors this one on a hybrid schedule, full time, with specific in-office days set by the integrations team. The runbook of gotchas from past integrations is usually the first thing a new associate engineer actually reads. The role reports to the senior engineer leading the integrations squad.

jobs.title: Backend Engineer, Portfolio Risk Aggregation
jobs.summary:
Every night, a set of batch pipelines aggregates fresh weather and sensor readings across thousands of insured property portfolios so underwriters have an updated risk picture by morning, and this role owns that pipeline end to end. It sits inside the reporting subsystem of Wrenfield's data platform organization.

Extending the batch jobs written in Go as new risk factors are added is the center of the role, alongside tuning PostgreSQL queries that have started to show latency as the dataset outgrows its original design and coordinating with the product team on new report types that ship roughly once a quarter. The role also includes rotating on-call coverage for the reporting subsystem, shared across six engineers rather than the whole platform. A recent migration off a cron scheduler onto a workflow engine is still being finished.

Required: three to five years writing Go in production, with PostgreSQL experience deep enough to diagnose a slow query rather than just write one, and comfort with gRPC for the service calls this pipeline depends on. Docker experience for local development and deploys is assumed, and enough familiarity with Kafka to reason about ordering and replay after a partial failure is expected. Prior experience specifically in insurance or climate data is not required.

Most collaboration happens asynchronously across European time zones, with a single weekly sync kept deliberately short, on a fully remote, full-time schedule. The team treats a clean postmortem as more valuable than assigning blame after an incident. The role reports to the engineering lead for the data platform's reporting subsystem.

jobs.title: Backend Engineer, Subscription Billing (Part-Time)
jobs.summary:
Wrenfield bills customers on a mix of seat-based and usage-based plans depending on how much climate data they pull from the platform, and this part-time role maintains the billing layer that reconciles subscription events between internal systems and the external payment processor.

In a typical week you review reconciliation discrepancies flagged by an automated nightly job, patch edge cases in the Go services that handle processor webhooks, and pair briefly with the finance team to confirm expected behavior before a fix ships. Because billing edge cases are unforgiving of guesswork, tests accompany every fix rather than getting added later if time allows. The scope stays deliberately narrow to the billing layer rather than expanding into the wider payments roadmap.

Required: three to five years writing Go and PostgreSQL in production, plus prior hands-on exposure to REST APIs and a payments platform such as the Stripe API, since billing edge cases punish guesswork quickly. Testing is not optional here: you should be comfortable writing a test for a reconciliation edge case before shipping the fix. Ownership of the broader finance or accounting systems is not required; the role stays scoped to the billing layer.

The position is structured around roughly twenty hours a week with flexible scheduling across time zones, fully remote, which suits someone balancing this against other commitments such as a second contract or study. The role reports to a senior engineer who scopes the weekly priorities directly. No on-call rotation comes with this seat.

jobs.title: Full-Stack Engineer, Underwriter Dashboards
jobs.summary:
Underwriters and risk analysts explore Wrenfield's climate data through a set of customer-facing dashboards, and this role joins the small team responsible for them, splitting time between a React frontend and the GraphQL services behind it, in close partnership with the design team.

Recent projects have included rebuilding a flood-exposure heatmap component that was struggling with larger portfolios and adding CSV export support that several enterprise accounts had requested for months. The team ships in small increments behind feature flags and expects engineers to write their own end-to-end tests rather than relying on a separate QA function. Three product designers and two backend engineers sit alongside this team, and the role moves comfortably between all three groups.

Required: three to five years of React and TypeScript experience in production, plus enough Node.js and PostgreSQL comfort to reason about the GraphQL schema and the queries behind it, since the two sides of this role are genuinely intertwined. You should be able to take a component from a rough design through a shipped, tested feature on your own. A background in data visualization libraries specifically is not required, since the charting needs here are modest.

Standups are asynchronous most days, with a single video call midweek reserved for anything that benefits from a live conversation, on a fully remote, full-time schedule across Europe. Candidates in Amsterdam, elsewhere in the Netherlands, or Poland are all a good fit for the working hours this team keeps. The role reports to the engineering lead for underwriter-facing products.

jobs.title: Software Engineer, Climate Data Warehouse
jobs.summary:
Raw satellite, weather-station and sensor readings become useful only after they pass through the transformation layer this role maintains, turning them into the modeled tables analysts and customers ultimately query. The warehouse currently serves several hundred modeled tables and keeps growing as the risk methodology adds new factors.

You write and maintain dbt models as new risk factors are introduced, troubleshoot Airflow DAG failures that occasionally wake up the on-call engineer when an upstream feed changes shape without notice, and collaborate with a data analyst embedded in the team to validate new metrics before they reach production. Schema changes get whiteboarded together in person rather than argued over in a pull request. Naming conventions and documentation carry more weight here than at a smaller warehouse, given the table count.

Required: three to five years of SQL and a modern transformation tool such as dbt in production, plus enough Python to script around the edges of a pipeline rather than depend entirely on someone else's tooling. Comfort with Airflow or a comparable orchestrator is expected, though not a specific vendor certification. Snowflake experience specifically is preferred but not required, since the SQL and modeling skills transfer across warehouses.

The team spends two days a week together at the Berlin office and works independently the rest of the time, on a full-time schedule. The team treats a data quality incident that reaches a customer-visible report seriously, running a short retrospective focused on process rather than individual fault. The role reports to the data platform's warehouse lead.

jobs.title: Senior Backend Engineer, Sensor Event Platform
jobs.summary:
Billions of sensor and satellite readings flow through Wrenfield's event platform every day, and this senior role is responsible for keeping that pipeline reliable as data volume climbs faster than the original architecture anticipated. The team has grown from three to six engineers over the past eighteen months.

Redesigning a partitioning scheme that is starting to bottleneck under current load comes first, alongside mentoring two mid-level engineers through their first significant architectural change and representing the event platform in cross-team reviews when other teams propose changes touching shared infrastructure. This senior hire is also expected to help formalize on-call practices that have so far been fairly informal. Design documents circulate for written feedback before any significant change starts.

Required: five to eight years operating a high-throughput streaming system in production, with Go, Kafka and PostgreSQL experience at meaningful scale, plus enough Kubernetes and gRPC fluency to reason about how the pieces talk to each other under load. What matters most is the judgment to know when a redesign is worth the disruption and when it is not, over familiarity with any specific vendor. Prior experience specifically with climate or insurance data is not required.

The team works fully asynchronously across European time zones with a light weekly sync, fully remote, on a full-time schedule. The team considers a three-week architecture review normal for a change of this scale rather than a sign the process is too slow. The role reports to the staff engineer overseeing data platform architecture.

jobs.title: Senior Backend Engineer, Risk API Gateway (Contract)
jobs.summary:
Wrenfield needs a senior contractor for roughly six months to lead a rewrite of the API gateway that fronts every customer-facing climate risk endpoint the company exposes. Dozens of enterprise customers have built internal tooling directly against the current gateway's quirks over the years, which is what makes this rewrite delicate rather than a simple technical upgrade.

The work involves designing a phased migration plan that avoids downtime for existing integrations, implementing the new routing and rate-limiting logic in Go, and documenting the rollout clearly enough that the permanent platform team can maintain it once the contract ends. You also run a deprecation timeline past a handful of the largest customers directly, since several will need to update their own client code. Progress is reviewed every two weeks against a plan agreed with the engineering director.

Required: five to eight years of Go experience with API design and API gateway patterns specifically, plus enough gRPC, PostgreSQL and Kubernetes fluency to reason about what the gateway routes to, since this is a scoped rewrite rather than a role to learn the domain on. Strong written communication matters just as much as the code, since most collaboration happens asynchronously with a distributed team. A commitment beyond the six-month engagement is not expected.

This is a six-month contract engagement, fully remote, structured around every-two-week progress reviews rather than daily oversight. Contractors who have done a similar gateway migration before tend to do best in this kind of scoped, deadline-driven work. The engagement reports to the engineering director for its duration.

jobs.title: Freelance Senior Engineer, Climate Data Export Tooling
jobs.summary:
Enterprise customers want their raw climate and weather data out of Wrenfield's platform and into their own warehouses rather than depending on the built-in dashboards alone, and this freelance engagement covers the design and build of a self-service export tool that gets them there.

You scope the initial architecture with the product manager, implement the export jobs in Python against the existing data lake, and hand off a working prototype with clear documentation by the end of the engagement window. Several large customers have specifically asked for this capability during renewal conversations, so there is real business pressure behind getting a usable version out rather than a polished but late one. The role suits someone comfortable owning a project end to end with minimal day-to-day oversight.

Required: five to eight years of Python and SQL experience, plus prior work building data export or ETL tooling with AWS S3, Airflow and PostgreSQL against a large dataset, ideally at a scale comparable to Wrenfield's petabyte-class data lake. You should be able to scope your own architecture rather than wait for one handed to you. Ongoing maintenance after handoff is not part of this engagement, which ends once the prototype and documentation ship.

Scheduling is flexible provided the milestones land on time, fully remote, with no fixed weekly hours attached to this freelance engagement. Check-ins happen roughly every two weeks with the product manager rather than through a standing daily process. The engagement reports to the product manager sponsoring the export tool.

jobs.title: Staff Engineer, Data Platform Architecture
jobs.summary:
Wrenfield's data platform organization grew quickly without much shared architectural review as the company added new data sources and customer segments, and this staff role sets technical direction across the three teams that now make it up, roughly thirty engineers today.

Concretely that means writing design documents for cross-team initiatives such as the move to a shared event schema across ingestion and modeling, chairing a monthly architecture forum where teams surface decisions that affect more than their own codebase, and stepping into a team's codebase when a hard problem needs a second set of eyes. You also own the relationship with infrastructure on anything touching shared Kubernetes capacity, since data platform workloads are among the heaviest consumers on the cluster.

Required: eight or more years of experience with distributed systems and data infrastructure at scale, including hands-on depth in Go, Kafka and PostgreSQL, with the communication skill to influence teams you do not directly manage mattering as much as the technical depth itself. Interviews focus heavily on a past system design decision you can walk through in detail, tradeoffs included, rather than an abstract prompt. Direct people-management experience is not required, since this role carries no direct reports of its own.

Candidates based anywhere in Europe are a fit for this fully remote role, with much of the data platform organization anchored around Berlin's working hours. Reporting for this staff role goes to the VP of engineering, full time. Success looks like better decisions happening earlier rather than any single deliverable shipped this quarter.

jobs.title: Principal Engineer, Climate Data Infrastructure
jobs.summary:
Wrenfield is hiring a principal engineer to own the long-term technical roadmap for its climate data infrastructure, spanning ingestion from an expanding set of satellite and sensor providers, storage, and the query layer every customer report ultimately runs against. The company has added three new categories of data provider in the past year alone.

You identify where the current architecture will break under three years of projected data growth, propose and personally prototype alternatives before committing the wider organization to a direction, and influence hiring and leveling decisions for senior engineers joining the data organization. Part of the mandate is external too: this role periodically joins customer conversations where a prospective enterprise account wants technical assurance about how the platform handles their data volume before signing.

Required: a decade or more of distributed systems experience designing data infrastructure at scale, with deep hands-on history across Go, Kafka, Kubernetes and PostgreSQL rather than architecture diagrams alone, plus enough communication skill to make technical judgment legible to people outside the immediate team, including on occasion a skeptical enterprise customer. This is an individual-contributor track rather than a management one, so people-management experience is not required.

This one is fully remote, with a preference for candidates near the Berlin area where most of the data organization sits, and travel to meet enterprise customers happens periodically rather than on a fixed schedule. There is no fixed office to report to day to day. The role reports directly to the VP of engineering, full time.

jobs.title: Infrastructure Lead, Platform Engineering
jobs.summary:
Kubernetes clusters, CI/CD pipelines and the observability stack that every product team at Wrenfield ultimately depends on sit under one small infrastructure team, and this lead role oversees it. The spot-instance migration currently underway is projected to cut batch compute costs by close to a third once complete.
