You set quarterly priorities for two infrastructure engineers, personally drive larger initiatives such as the current migration to spot-instance-based worker pools for batch jobs, and act as the escalation point during major incidents regardless of which team's service is affected. You also inherit ownership of the on-call rotation policy, currently under review after a stretch of incidents landed disproportionately on one engineer. Planning benefits from in-person time together each week.

Required: a genuine track record with Kubernetes and infrastructure-as-code tooling such as Terraform in production, plus hands-on CI/CD pipeline and Prometheus experience, and some prior experience leading a small team, even informally. You should be able to make a credible call during a live incident rather than purely coordinate from the sidelines. A background specifically in AWS is preferred but a comparable cloud platform transfers fine.

Two days a week in the Berlin office overlap with the rest of the small infrastructure team, on a full-time schedule, with the remaining days worked independently. The finance team is watching the cost-savings number from the spot-instance migration closely, which puts a bit more visibility on this role than infrastructure work usually gets. Oversight for this lead role rests with the VP of engineering.

jobs.title: Engineering Manager, Platform Infrastructure
jobs.summary:
Wrenfield's platform infrastructure group is growing from four to seven engineers over the next two quarters, and this manager role leads it through that growth. This is an internal posting, limited to current employees who already have context on Wrenfield's infrastructure rather than posted externally.

Weekly one-on-ones anchor the job, alongside partnering with the director of engineering on the hiring plan for the new headcount and staying close enough to the technical work to make credible calls during incident retrospectives rather than deferring entirely to senior engineers. Representing infrastructure in the quarterly planning review is part of it too, where competing priorities across teams get negotiated, sometimes contentiously given how many product teams depend on the same shared clusters.

Required: six to nine years in infrastructure or platform engineering with Kubernetes, Terraform and AWS, including at least a year or two of direct people management and incident response rather than only leading informally. Existing context on Wrenfield's infrastructure is expected, which is why this opening is internal. Two of the three planned hires this quarter are relatively junior, so mentorship matters more early on than pure delegation, and prior experience managing junior engineers specifically is useful though not required.

Berlin is the daily reality for this one, onsite and full time, alongside the infrastructure engineers it manages every day. The expectation is a fairly short ramp-up given existing familiarity with the team's systems and its people. The manager this role reports to is the director of engineering, who also sponsors the hiring plan.

jobs.title: Application Security Engineer, Platform
jobs.summary:
Wrenfield Data Labs is standing up its first dedicated application security role, working alongside the backend and platform teams rather than reviewing their output from a separate function. The risk models the company sells to customers run on sensitive geospatial and portfolio data, which raises the bar on access control and data handling well past a typical SaaS product.

Expect to run threat-modeling sessions before major features ship, review pull requests across several codebases for the vulnerability classes that show up most often, and build small internal tools that catch problems like hardcoded secrets before they reach production. A good share of the early work is organizational rather than technical: standing up a lightweight vulnerability disclosure process and choosing which SAST tool is worth adopting, since none has been picked yet.

Required: hands-on secure-code-review experience against the OWASP Top Ten, enough Python to build and maintain small tools that plug into an existing CI pipeline, and prior exposure to threat modeling as a practice rather than a one-off workshop. Around four to six years of application security or security-minded software engineering work fits this seat. Compliance certifications are not expected; judgment on real codebases matters more than a credential.

Full-time, with arrangements flexible between the Berlin office and remote work across Europe. The security function is currently one person, this hire, so most collaboration happens through overlap with backend and platform engineers rather than a dedicated team; two mornings a week are set aside for shared review sessions.

jobs.title: Software Engineering Intern, Payments Platform
jobs.summary:
Payments infrastructure that other businesses embed to move money and track balances sits with the ledger team at Thistledown, and this internship places you on that team for the length of the program. The ledger group is deliberately small, five engineers today, so an intern gets exposure to production incidents and design discussions a larger team might otherwise shield juniors from.

You will fix small bugs reported through the developer support channel, write tests around ledger edge cases such as partial refunds and currency rounding that the existing suite does not fully cover, and pair with an assigned mentor twice a week to review progress against goals set at the start of the program. Towards the end of the internship you scope and ship one small feature end to end, with support, rather than working on throwaway practice tasks.

Required: fundamentals in TypeScript and Node.js, or a similarly typed language and runtime, from coursework, a bootcamp or personal projects, plus genuine curiosity about how financial systems handle correctness, since a wrong balance is a different class of bug from a wrong pixel, and enough comfort with Git to track changes and open a pull request for review. This internship assumes zero to one year of hands-on coding experience; a finished portfolio project is not expected, and neither is prior fintech exposure.

The program runs on a hybrid schedule based in the London office, with in-person days set by the mentor pairing rather than a fixed company-wide policy. You report to your assigned mentor on the ledger team for the internship's duration, with progress checked against the goals agreed at the outset.

jobs.title: Junior Frontend Engineer, Merchant Dashboard
jobs.summary:
Every business customer manages its relationship with Thistledown through the merchant dashboard, from settlement reports to payout schedules, and this junior role joins the small frontend team that maintains it. Several years of incremental changes have left the dashboard with inconsistent styling, and untangling that is a running theme of the work ahead.

Early projects typically include fixing accessibility issues flagged in a recent audit, adding test coverage to older components before they are touched again, and implementing design tweaks handed off for the upcoming payout-scheduling redesign. You will also help migrate older screens onto the newer shared component library, and everyone on the team, regardless of level, attends a weekly design-engineering sync before implementation starts on anything customer-facing.

Required: TypeScript and React fundamentals from coursework, a bootcamp or personal projects, along with basic comfort writing CSS and Jest tests and using Git to manage changes across a shared codebase. This seat assumes roughly one to two years of hands-on frontend work; production accessibility experience is a plus but not expected, since the audit itself is where you will pick it up. A mentor reviews your work closely for the first several months.

Full-time and fully onsite in the London office, with no remote option for this role. You report to the frontend team lead and work most closely day to day with two other engineers on the merchant dashboard, plus the design team ahead of the payout-scheduling redesign.

jobs.title: Backend Engineer, Payout Processing
jobs.summary:
Millions of payouts move through Thistledown's platform every month on behalf of the businesses that embed its ledger, and this role owns the service that batches, schedules and retries those payouts against banking rails that do not always respond quickly or predictably.

Current work includes reducing duplicate payouts caused by a race condition in the queue consumer during high-volume periods, and adding a delayed-retry mode for the banking partners whose rejection responses arrive inconsistently. The service runs on TypeScript and Node.js, backed by PostgreSQL and Redis, and getting to know a handful of banking partners' specific quirks well is genuinely part of the job rather than an afterthought.

Required: solid production experience with Node.js and message queues such as RabbitMQ, plus comfort with PostgreSQL and Redis at the level of debugging a live data issue, not just querying one. This seat calls for three to five years of backend experience, ideally including some money-handling code, where a subtle bug means a real customer does not get paid on time. Prior payments-industry experience is not required.

Full-time and fully remote, open to candidates anywhere in Europe, though most collaboration happens during hours that overlap comfortably with Dublin. On-call is shared on a weekly rotation between three backend engineers including this hire, with rotation weeks compensated separately from base pay. The role reports to the engineering manager for the payments platform team, and quarterly planning is done jointly across all three engineers on the rotation.

jobs.title: Software Engineer, Transaction Search
jobs.summary:
Support agents and business customers both need to find a specific transaction quickly across millions of ledger entries, and this role sits on the small team responsible for that search experience inside Thistledown's platform. Search volume spikes noticeably at the start of each month when business customers reconcile their books.

Tuning Elasticsearch relevance scoring based on real support-ticket feedback is a regular thread of the work, alongside extending the indexing pipeline to cover new transaction types as payment methods are added, and investigating the occasional slow-query report from a customer with an unusually large transaction history. The team has learned to schedule risky indexing changes well away from the monthly reconciliation window, and treats a rising p95 latency trend as worth investigating before it becomes a customer-visible complaint.

Required: comfort with Elasticsearch or a similar search technology, plus solid backend fundamentals in TypeScript, Node.js and PostgreSQL. Three to five years of backend experience fits this role, and some exposure to search-relevance tuning specifically is useful, though the team is glad to teach that part on the job. Deep Elasticsearch cluster-operations experience is not required.

Hybrid, with the Dublin-based team meeting in person on Tuesdays and Thursdays for planning and pairing. Full-time, with a light amount of on-call mostly triggered by slow-query alerts rather than outright outages, shared across the search team.

jobs.title: Backend Engineer, Statement Exports (Part-Time)
jobs.summary:
Business customers download their transaction history in bulk through Thistledown's statement export feature for their own accounting and reconciliation needs, and this part-time role keeps that feature maintained and gradually improving. The work is steady rather than urgent, with roughly a dozen recurring customer requests open at any given time.

Expect to triage the occasional export failure reported through support, add support for a new file format this quarter that a large customer specifically requested, and keep the underlying export job queue healthy as transaction volume grows. The feature currently supports three file formats, and triage judgment matters more here than raw throughput, since the backlog rarely empties in one sitting.

Required: practical Node.js and TypeScript experience backed by PostgreSQL, plus comfort with REST APIs and export or reporting tooling generally, since most of the codebase is plain logic wrapped around file generation. Three to five years of backend experience is the expected level, along with enough independence to keep a steady backlog moving without close supervision or daily check-ins. Prior experience specifically with CSV export pipelines is helpful but not assumed; most of the team picked it up on the job.

Fifteen to twenty hours a week, fully remote across Europe, with no fixed core hours beyond a weekly async standup. The schedule stays genuinely flexible around whatever else is going on in your week, and the role reports to the backend team lead who owns prioritization for the statement exports feature and the wider export backlog.

jobs.title: Software Engineer, Mobile Banking Sync
jobs.summary:
Business owners frequently check balances and recent transactions from Thistledown's mobile app while away from a desk, sometimes on a patchy connection, and keeping the app consistent with the web dashboard under those conditions is harder than it sounds. This role works across both native codebases on that problem.

The work covers fixing sync conflicts reported by users, adding automated tests around the conflict-resolution logic that has caused most recent bug reports, and collaborating closely with a QA engineer who runs manual scenarios your automated tests are likely to miss. Pairing regularly across the iOS and Android engineers is what the team has found actually keeps the two implementations from drifting apart.

Required: some prior exposure to either Kotlin or Swift, not necessarily both, plus solid testing habits and comfort with REST APIs and local storage such as SQLite. Three to five years of mobile or backend engineering experience fits this seat, and the team is happy to have you specialize in one platform initially rather than arrive fluent in both. Deep experience with sync-conflict resolution specifically is not expected; the team teaches its own approach to that part.

Two office days a week in London keep the small mobile team aligned on shared sync logic, with the rest of the week worked remotely. Full-time, reporting to the mobile team's lead alongside one iOS-focused and one Android-focused engineer, with a QA engineer embedded in the same team for manual scenario coverage.

jobs.title: Software Engineer, Platform Subscription Billing
jobs.summary:
Separate from the ledger product it sells, Thistledown itself charges business customers a mix of platform fees and transaction-based pricing, and this role maintains the billing system behind that relationship. A new usage-based tier is planned for later this year, and whoever takes this role will likely design the metering logic behind it.

Recent work has involved building proration logic for mid-cycle plan changes and closing gaps between internal billing records and the external payment processor, after a handful of reconciliation incidents last quarter that finance flagged as a priority. You will work closely with a product manager and one other engineer, with finance joining planning discussions roughly monthly to flag anything upcoming on pricing.

Required: solid Python and PostgreSQL experience, plus prior exposure to a payments API such as Stripe's, since the two systems interact in ways that are easy to get subtly wrong. Three to five years of backend experience is the expected level, ideally including some exposure to billing or metering logic specifically. Deep accounting or finance domain knowledge is not required; the finance team owns that side of the conversation and joins planning monthly.

Fully remote, open to candidates across Europe including London and Portugal specifically, with no requirement to be near either office. Full-time, with no formal reporting change expected from finance's monthly check-ins on pricing.

jobs.title: Senior Software Engineer, Real-Time Payment Rails
jobs.summary:
External banking networks that settle instantly and an internal ledger that must stay consistent regardless of event order meet at the real-time payment rails, and few engineers at Thistledown understand that intersection as deeply as this role requires. An instant-payments network is launching in several European markets this year, and this seat carries that launch.

Current priorities include reducing duplicate-processing incidents that surface when a banking partner retries a request the system already handled, and extending idempotency guarantees to the newly integrated network ahead of launch. A recent internal audit found one theoretical scenario, never triggered in production, where a specific retry pattern could double-count a payout, and closing that gap is a higher priority than any new feature work this quarter.

Required: prior experience with event-driven architectures or payment systems specifically, since the failure modes here are subtle and often only show up under real production load, plus strong TypeScript and Node.js skills and working familiarity with Kafka and PostgreSQL. Five to eight years of backend experience fits this seat. Direct people-management experience is not expected; the mentoring involved here is informal and folded into normal project work.

Based anywhere in Europe on a fully remote basis, full-time. The role mentors two engineers newer to distributed systems work and represents the payments team in periodic architecture reviews with other platform teams, reporting to the engineering manager for payments infrastructure, with schedule flexibility outside the instant-payments launch window.

jobs.title: Senior Engineer, Ledger Migration Tooling (Contract)
jobs.summary:
Thistledown is bringing on a contractor for approximately four months to build tooling that imports customer ledger data from three competing payment processors into the platform's internal format. Sales has already lined up prospective customers waiting specifically on this tooling before they will commit to switching providers.

The work includes writing parsers for each source format, handling the inevitable edge cases in historical transaction data that does not map cleanly onto Thistledown's schema, and building a dry-run mode so the customer success team can preview a migration's results before a business commits. You will report to the engineering manager for growth and demo progress every two weeks against an agreed plan.

Required: strong Python and data-migration experience, close to a hard requirement here, fluency writing PostgreSQL queries against the platform's ledger schema, the patience to work with messy real-world financial data that rarely matches its documentation, and comfort designing a dry-run mode rather than just a one-way import script. Five to eight years of relevant engineering experience is expected. Prior work with one of the three processors involved is a meaningful head start but not assumed.

Remote, based in the United Kingdom, on a fixed-term contract of roughly four months with no expectation of extension beyond the scope already agreed with sales. Full-time hours for the engagement, working independently between the biweekly check-ins and expected to flag any schema surprises in the source data as soon as they turn up rather than absorbing them quietly into the timeline.

jobs.title: Senior Frontend Engineer, Card Issuing Console
jobs.summary:
The card issuing console lets business customers create, freeze and manage employee cards at scale, and this senior role focuses specifically on performance as customers with thousands of cards have started reporting noticeable lag. One enterprise customer alone now issues close to twenty thousand cards through the console.

You will profile rendering slowdowns in the card-list view under large datasets, redesign parts of the virtualization layer that struggle once a business issues more than a few thousand cards, and coach two other frontend engineers through code review on the shared component library. That one enterprise customer's feedback has effectively become the team's informal performance benchmark, well beyond what the original implementation was designed around.

Required: strong TypeScript and React experience, plus a track record of diagnosing and fixing frontend performance problems in a production application rather than only building new features, and comfort profiling render performance under genuinely large datasets. Five to eight years of frontend experience fits this seat. Prior experience specifically with card-issuing or fintech products is not required; the performance problem transfers from any large-scale React application.

One office day a week in London for design reviews with product and design, the rest worked remotely. Full-time, with two other frontend engineers on the team looking to this role for review and guidance day to day, reporting to the frontend engineering manager who owns the console's roadmap.

jobs.title: Senior Backend Engineer, Account Access Control
jobs.summary:
Business banking accounts on Thistledown are often managed by several people with different responsibilities, and this role leads the redesign of the access-control system governing who can view balances, approve payouts or manage other users. The rules have grown organically over several years into something even their original authors now find difficult to reason about.

The project involves modeling a cleaner role-based system that still supports existing customer configurations without breaking them, migrating data without disrupting active business accounts mid-transition, and writing extensive tests given how much of the product depends on correct permission checks. Compliance has asked for a dry run of the new permission model against a sample of real customer account structures before any migration begins.

Required: strong backend experience in Node.js and TypeScript against a PostgreSQL-backed schema, including some prior work specifically on authorization or permissions systems, plus comfort explaining a migration plan clearly enough that a nervous compliance team signs off on it. Five to eight years of backend experience fits this seat, and prior work on financial or otherwise sensitive systems is a meaningful plus. Formal security certifications are not required; demonstrated judgment on real permission systems matters considerably more.

Fully remote across Europe, full-time. Expect close collaboration with a security-minded colleague on the infrastructure team throughout the project, since access control and security review overlap heavily here, reporting to the engineering manager for account services, based mainly around Dublin working hours.

jobs.title: Tech Lead, Onboarding and Growth Engineering
jobs.summary:
Signup, identity verification and the upgrade prompts that convert free accounts into paying business customers all run through experiments this role guides as tech lead for onboarding and growth engineering, directing three engineers across that surface. Identity verification sits in a gray area between growth and compliance that this lead is expected to watch closely.

Day to day the role mixes hands-on coding in the shared TypeScript codebase with quarterly technical planning, plus occasional pushback on experiment ideas that would add too much regulatory complexity for the expected upside on a financial product. Performance reviews for the engineers on this team weigh experiment quality rather than shipped volume, specifically to avoid rewarding a flood of low-value tests.

Required: solid full-stack experience across TypeScript, React, Node.js and PostgreSQL, plus some prior experience leading a small team and comfort working alongside compliance requirements a typical growth team would not usually encounter. This is a lead role scoped by team size and the regulatory exposure of the surface, rather than a fixed years figure. Deep compliance expertise itself is not required; the compliance team owns final sign-off.

Hybrid, working from the Dublin office several days a week, with two of the three engineers on the team remote across European time zones and expected to stay genuinely included in planning rather than sidelined. Full-time, reporting to the VP of Product Engineering, with quarterly OKRs jointly owned by product and engineering and reviewed together each quarter.

jobs.title: Senior Infrastructure Engineer, Deployment Platform (Freelance)
jobs.summary:
Thistledown is looking for a freelance infrastructure specialist to modernize its deployment pipeline over an engagement of roughly three months, work that carries extra weight given that deployments here touch systems handling real money. Roughly a third of services remain on a legacy VM-based deployment process, and two of those handle ledger writes directly.

The scope includes migrating the remaining legacy services onto the existing Kubernetes cluster, tightening CI pipeline reliability that has become a recurring source of complaints from engineers shipping to production, and documenting the new setup for the small internal infrastructure team to maintain afterward. The two ledger-writing services are the riskiest part of the engagement and the ones that team has been most reluctant to touch without outside help.

Required: strong Kubernetes and CI/CD experience on AWS, plus comfort with Terraform and observability tooling for a rollback plan that matters more here than in a typical SaaS deployment. Five to eight years of infrastructure experience fits this engagement, ideally including at least one legacy-to-Kubernetes migration carried out under a real deadline rather than as a greenfield exercise. Prior work in a regulated or compliance-sensitive environment is useful but not required.

Flexible scheduling, provided there is meaningful overlap with European working hours for handoff conversations near the engagement's end. Freelance, roughly three months, based in or near London with remote work across Europe accepted, checking in weekly with the infrastructure lead and expected to flag scope surprises early rather than absorb them silently.

jobs.title: Security Engineering Manager
jobs.summary:
Three engineers split across application security and vulnerability management make up Thistledown's growing security engineering function, and this internal posting covers the manager role leading them, needed given the compliance bar the company's payments product is held to. The team has grown from a single engineer eighteen months ago to three today.

You will set the team's roadmap in partnership with the head of engineering, represent security directly in customer due-diligence calls for larger enterprise deals where security posture is often the deciding factor, and continue carrying a portion of hands-on review work rather than moving fully into management. Two of the largest enterprise deals currently in procurement have named specific security requirements with no clear owner yet.

Required: established relationships across engineering leadership and working familiarity with the company's compliance obligations, since this opening is limited to internal candidates rather than posted externally. This is a management role scoped by team size and the deals it supports, rather than a fixed years figure, though prior hands-on application security work is expected. Formal management training is not required; the head of engineering will coach the transition.

No remote option: this is a full-time, fully onsite role based in the London office, in keeping with how closely it works with engineering leadership day to day. Reports to the head of engineering, leading three security engineers directly, and expected to resolve the current ownership gap on procurement requirements early into the role.

jobs.title: Product Security Engineer
jobs.summary:
Reviewing designs before they are built, not only auditing after the fact, is the point of this product security role, which embeds with feature teams rather than sitting apart from them, a distinction that matters more than usual for a platform that moves other businesses' money. The role reports into engineering rather than a separate security organization, deliberately.

Threat-modeling sessions for new features such as the upcoming instant-payments integration are a regular part of the job, alongside triaging reports that come in through the company's bug bounty program and building small internal tools that make secure defaults easier for other engineers to reach for without thinking about it every time. The bug bounty queue currently averages around fifteen open reports, mostly duplicate low-severity findings with the occasional issue worth escalating the same day.

Required: working knowledge of the OWASP Top Ten, enough Python to build small internal tools, and comfort running a threat-modeling session without a security specialist in the room. Three to five years of application security or security-minded engineering experience fits this seat. Formal penetration-testing certification is not required; the basics learned on the job are enough.

Hybrid, based in the Dublin office with in-person days set by the feature teams this role embeds with, typically a few days a week. Full-time, reporting to the engineering director rather than into a dedicated security organization, by design.

jobs.title: Software Engineering Intern, Robot Fleet Systems
jobs.summary:
Dozens of Fernway robots operate simultaneously inside partner warehouses at any given time, and this internship sits on the fleet software team that keeps them coordinated so two robots never try to occupy the same aisle at once. Interns typically rotate through a couple of smaller projects over the summer rather than a single fixed task.

You will write and test small Python modules within the fleet management service, help build a visualization tool the operations team has been requesting for months to see robot status at a glance, and spend time on the warehouse floor observing how the robots you work on actually behave in a live facility, not only in simulation. Fernway pairs every intern with a dedicated mentor engineer for the program's full duration and expects a presentation of your work at the end.

Required: solid Python fundamentals, basic comfort with Git and working on Linux from the command line, and genuine interest in robotics, more valuable here than a finished portfolio piece. This internship assumes zero to two years of hands-on coding experience total, including coursework and personal projects, so no professional robotics background is expected going in. Prior ROS experience is a nice-to-have rather than a requirement, since the mentor engineer covers that ramp-up directly.

Onsite for the full internship at the Denver facility, with no remote option available. Full-time hours for the internship's duration, reporting to an assigned mentor engineer on the fleet software team, with a full-time offer decision made at the end of the program either way.

jobs.title: Junior Embedded Software Engineer, Robot Controllers
jobs.summary:
The embedded team writes the software that runs directly on the onboard computer of every Fernway robot deployed to a customer warehouse, and this junior role joins that team as its newest member. The Denver office keeps a small fleet of test robots on-site specifically for hands-on debugging.

Fixing sensor-driver bugs found during hardware bring-up on new robot units fills much of the early calendar, alongside writing unit tests for existing navigation modules that have grown without much test coverage, and shadowing more senior engineers during on-site debugging sessions when a fleet behaves unexpectedly. Getting comfortable with cross-compiling and flashing firmware onto physical test units is usually the first real skill this role builds in the first month.

Required: some coursework or personal-project experience with C or C++, basic familiarity with Git for tracking changes, and the patience to accept that a bug here sometimes turns out to be a sensor issue rather than anything in the code. This role assumes one to two years of hands-on programming experience; prior embedded Linux exposure is helpful but not expected, since a senior engineer reviews your work closely for the first several months.

Full-time and fully onsite at the Denver office, with no remote option for this role. Most early work happens on real hardware rather than purely in simulation, a deliberate part of ramping up embedded engineers here, and the role reports to the embedded team's lead, with day-to-day questions routed through whichever senior engineer is on hardware bring-up duty that week.

jobs.title: Software Engineer, Robot Navigation
jobs.summary:
Warehouse aisles get rearranged by customer staff more often than anyone at Fernway would prefer, and this role works on the navigation stack that lets robots find efficient paths through that constantly shifting layout. A recent customer complaint about robots stalling near a mirrored refrigeration unit turned into a multi-week investigation that reshaped how the perception stack handles reflective surfaces generally.

Replanning around temporary obstacles like pallets left in an aisle overnight is one steady stream of the work, alongside reducing false-positive stops triggered by reflective surfaces on certain shelving types that have caused a handful of recent support tickets. The role involves regular time in a test warehouse near the Denver office alongside simulation-based development, since some navigation bugs only show up on real hardware, and engineers rotate through hands-on testing sessions there roughly every two weeks.

Required: solid C++ and Python, hands-on ROS experience and some exposure to SLAM or robotics navigation concepts, plus comfort moving between simulated and physical testing environments on Linux. Three to five years of robotics or systems software experience fits this seat. Prior warehouse-robotics experience specifically is not required, since most of what matters here is learned on this fleet.

Hybrid, based at the Denver office with regular in-person time at the nearby test warehouse. Full-time, working closely with the perception and simulation teams, reporting to the navigation team's engineering lead.

jobs.title: Full-Stack Engineer, Fleet Operations Dashboard (Part-Time)
jobs.summary:
Operations teams watch robot status, battery levels and task queues in real time through Fernway's fleet dashboard, and this part-time role maintains it as feature requests arrive from customer-facing operations staff. Work is scoped in small, well-defined chunks rather than open-ended projects.

Recent examples include adding a filter for robots flagged for maintenance and fixing a chart that was miscounting idle time during shift changes at one large customer site. Most weeks the work is genuinely light and predictable, though the pace picks up briefly around quarterly customer business reviews when operations staff want the dashboard polished for a walkthrough with their own leadership. Requests arrive through a shared queue that a full-time engineer triages before handing pieces off.

Required: solid TypeScript and React skills, plus enough backend comfort with Node.js and PostgreSQL to work across the full stack when a fix requires it. Three to five years of full-stack experience fits this seat. Robotics domain knowledge is not required; the dashboard is a fairly ordinary web application sitting on top of unusual data, and most of the learning curve is about the data model rather than robotics itself.

Around twenty hours a week, fully remote from the United States or Canada, with scheduling flexible around the rest of your week. Part-time, reporting to a full-time engineer who prioritizes the backlog so you always know what matters most heading into a given week, with async updates replacing most live meetings.

jobs.title: Software Engineer, Robot Simulation Environments
jobs.summary:
Before any navigation or task-planning change reaches a physical robot, it runs first against the virtual warehouse environments the simulation team builds and maintains, and this role is part of that team. The simulator now models close to a dozen distinct warehouse layouts drawn from real customer facilities.

Extending the simulator to model new shelving configurations customers have requested for their specific facilities is core to the role, alongside writing regression tests that catch navigation regressions automatically before a change reaches hardware, and working with the navigation team to reproduce field issues difficult to debug directly on a live warehouse floor. Keeping the layout library current as customers renovate their spaces is a steady stream of the work.

Required: solid C++ and Python, plus familiarity with a robotics simulation tool such as Gazebo and working knowledge of ROS, since the simulator has to mirror what runs on the real robots; strong candidates who have used a comparable tool such as Webots are also welcome to apply. Three to five years of software engineering experience fits this seat. Direct warehouse-operations experience is not required, since the layouts themselves come from the customer-facing teams rather than from firsthand floor experience.

Hybrid, with the Toronto team meeting in person a few days a week to review simulation results together, usually walking through a recorded playback of whatever navigation edge case is under discussion. Full-time, working closely with the navigation team and reporting to the simulation team's engineering lead.

jobs.title: Senior Software Engineer, Fleet Task Planning
jobs.summary:
Balancing speed against battery life and charging-dock availability across an entire robot fleet is a genuinely hard scheduling problem, and this senior role owns the task-planning system that makes those tradeoffs for every pick-and-move job Fernway's robots execute. The largest deployment today runs close to two hundred robots on a single site, well beyond what the scheduler was originally tuned for.

You will redesign parts of the scheduling algorithm to handle the larger fleet sizes newer customers are deploying, work through tradeoffs with the customer success team when planning decisions produce results operators find confusing, and mentor a mid-level engineer newly assigned to the team. That two-hundred-robot customer has agreed to a joint tuning exercise next quarter, likely the first chance to validate a redesigned scheduler against a real fleet at that scale.

Required: strong intuition for optimization under real-world constraints, more valuable here than familiarity with any specific framework, plus solid C++ and Python and enough robotics context to reason credibly about the physical constraints involved. Five to eight years of relevant engineering experience fits this seat. A formal operations-research background or advanced degree is not required if the practical intuition is genuinely there.

Fully remote across Canada and the United States, full-time. Most coordination happens asynchronously across the Toronto and Denver time zones, with a standing weekly sync to keep planning, customer success and the hardware team aligned, reporting to the engineering manager for fleet task planning.

jobs.title: Senior Software Engineer, Fleet Telemetry (Contract)
jobs.summary:
Every deployed Fernway robot streams sensor and performance data back to the cloud, and this contract role rebuilds the telemetry pipeline that collects and stores it over an engagement of about five months. The current batch process uploads once every fifteen minutes, which several customers have flagged as too slow to catch a stuck robot promptly.

Replacing the aging batch-upload process with a streaming pipeline that supports near-real-time dashboards for operations teams is the core of the project, alongside designing a schema that scales as fleet sizes grow well beyond current levels and training the permanent data engineering team on the new system before the contract concludes. Deliverables are structured around biweekly milestones agreed with the engineering director rather than an open-ended scope.

Required: strong Python and streaming-data experience, ideally including Kafka or a comparable system, plus comfort building the Grafana dashboards operations teams will use to watch the pipeline in near-real time, and the ability to hand off cleanly to a permanent team that will own the system after you leave. Five to eight years of relevant engineering experience fits this engagement. Prior robotics-domain experience is not required; the telemetry problem here is mostly a data-engineering one wrapped around unfamiliar hardware.

Fully remote within the United States, on a fixed-term contract of about five months with deliverables tied to biweekly milestones rather than an open-ended scope. Full-time hours for the engagement, reporting to the engineering director, and expected to document design decisions clearly enough that the permanent team can maintain the pipeline without the contractor in the room.

jobs.title: Senior Embedded Software Engineer, Sensor Fusion
jobs.summary:
Lidar, camera and wheel-encoder data combine into a single reliable estimate of each robot's position in the sensor fusion layer, arguably the piece of software a robot's safe operation depends on most directly, and this role owns it. Recent field issues have traced back to sensor timing drift under certain temperature conditions.

Resolving that class of drift problem for good is a primary focus here rather than a one-off fix, and the work includes periodic travel to customer sites, often two climate-controlled cold-storage facilities that have produced most recent drift reports, to observe hardware behavior difficult to reproduce back at the Denver lab. A firmware-level change to sensor sampling rates is under discussion, and this role is expected to make that call, backed by data, on whether the fix belongs in hardware or stays in software.

Required: strong C++ and real-time systems experience, plus specific prior exposure to sensor fusion or state estimation and fluency with Git for managing changes across the embedded codebase, since general embedded experience alone is not enough for this seat. Five to eight years of embedded or robotics engineering experience fits the role. A background specifically in cold-chain or refrigeration hardware is not required, even though two current cold-storage sites are where most drift reports originate.

The role splits time between the Denver office and remote days, hybrid, with periodic travel to customer sites layered on top of that schedule. Full-time, working closely with the hardware team whenever a software fix alone is not sufficient, and reporting to the staff engineer for fleet systems, who signs off on any firmware-level changes.

jobs.title: Staff Software Engineer, Fleet Systems Architecture
jobs.summary:
Fleet coordination, task planning and customer dashboards fit together less cleanly than they should at Fernway, an inconsistency built up as the company scaled quickly from a handful of pilot customers to dozens of live deployments, and this staff role is accountable for fixing that. The company has roughly tripled its live customer deployments in the past two years.

Writing a proposal for a cleaner service boundary between fleet coordination and task planning is the centerpiece, since the current architecture blurs the two in ways that make changes riskier than necessary. The role also reviews architecture decisions from teams across engineering, personally prototypes the riskiest parts of any major redesign before handing it off, and weighs in on hiring decisions for senior engineers across the robotics software organization.

Required: deep distributed-systems experience, more valuable here than any single certification, plus enough robotics-specific context in C++, Python and ROS to reason credibly about hardware constraints when reviewing other teams' designs. Eight or more years of relevant engineering experience fits this seat. This is an individual-contributor role with broad influence but no direct reports, so prior people-management experience is not required.

Fully remote across North America, full-time. Occasional travel to the Denver office for planning weeks, typically once a quarter, is part of the rhythm, and this seat sits under the VP of Engineering, who leans on its technical judgment across the robotics software organization.

jobs.title: Engineering Lead, Navigation Team
jobs.summary:
Fernway's navigation stack sits behind every warehouse robot the company ships, turning SLAM and sensor data into a path the robot can follow, and the four-engineer team that owns it just lost its lead to a cross-team architecture role. Fernway is filling the seat from inside the team rather than running an open search, given the context the job demands.

You would run sprint planning for the four engineers on the team, stay personally hands-on with the hardest navigation bugs that come in from robots already in the field rather than routing everything to someone else, and work closely with the hardware group on sensor placement for the next robot revision, now in design. Those placement calls are hard to undo once tooling is committed, which is why the hardware team wants navigation's input well before the revision locks.

Required: strong, current C++ and hands-on SLAM or ROS experience — deep enough to read the trickiest parts of the navigation stack without a walkthrough. Fernway scopes this seat by what it owns rather than a year count: leading a four-person team's sprint planning, staying technical enough to take the hardest field bugs personally, and representing navigation in sensor-placement calls with hardware. Formal people-management training is not required; informal lead experience on a small technical team is enough.

The team splits time between home and Fernway's Denver office, with in-person days aligned to sprint planning and the hardware sensor-placement reviews. You would report to the director of robotics engineering and manage the four navigation engineers directly, with authority to set the team's day-to-day priorities inside the roadmap the director sets.

jobs.title: Robotics Software Engineer, Cross-Functional Rotation
jobs.summary:
Robotics engineers who join this rotation spend roughly ten to twelve weeks apiece inside navigation, task planning and fleet coordination, picking up whichever problem the robotics group needs help with that quarter. Fernway runs the rotation as an onboarding path rather than a permanent generalist job, meant as preparation for a more specialized seat later.

One week might mean chasing down an odd navigation edge case that only shows up on specific warehouse floors; the next, adding a small feature to the fleet dashboard, or picking up a task-planning ticket nobody else has bandwidth for. The team keeps a shared backlog visible from day one, so incoming engineers can see exactly what is blocking each of the three areas before their rotation even starts, rather than waiting to be told.

Required: solid C++ and Python fundamentals, comfort with Git and Linux day to day, and enough command of ROS basics to get productive quickly in a new codebase every rotation. Fernway aims this seat at engineers roughly one to three years into a robotics career who want breadth before specializing — prior ROS production experience is welcome but not assumed going in. Deep expertise in any one of the three rotation areas is exactly what this role is not expecting yet.

Fernway runs this rotation fully on-site out of the Denver office, since bouncing between navigation, task planning and fleet coordination works best when you can walk over and ask the owning team directly. You would report to the robotics engineering manager who coordinates the rotation program rather than to any single team lead, and most engineers who complete it move into a specialized navigation or fleet-systems role within about a year.

jobs.title: Infrastructure Engineer, Fleet Cloud Platform
jobs.summary:
Every robot Fernway ships phones home to a cloud platform for fleet coordination, software updates and telemetry, and this role sits on the small infrastructure team that keeps that platform running. A bad rollout does not just cause an outage — it can strand robots mid-task inside a customer's warehouse, which shapes how the team treats anything touching deployment.

Kubernetes clusters serving fleet traffic sit at the center of the job: managing them day to day, extending the CI/CD pipeline that ships firmware updates out to robots already in customer sites, and helping build a canary-rollout mechanism now on the near-term roadmap specifically to shrink the blast radius of a bad push — a project this role would likely lead once it starts. Incident reviews after any deployment issue happen with the whole team, not just whoever was on call.

Required: solid production experience with Kubernetes, Terraform and AWS, plus comfort owning a CI/CD pipeline that ships Docker-packaged updates without hand-holding from another team. Fernway is looking for roughly three to five years of infrastructure experience in this seat. Direct exposure to fleet or IoT-style systems, where devices in the field depend on the cloud staying reachable, is a real plus here but not a requirement — the team would rather teach that context than screen out otherwise strong infrastructure candidates.

Toronto is where this role sits full time and in person, alongside the rest of Fernway's Toronto engineering group rather than any distributed arrangement. You would report to the infrastructure engineering manager for the fleet cloud platform, with planning sessions and incident reviews run in person as a matter of course rather than over video.

jobs.title: Site Reliability Engineer, Fleet Coordination Platform
jobs.summary:
Robots stall mid-task inside a customer's warehouse the moment Fernway's fleet coordination platform goes down for more than a few minutes, which is why a small site-reliability team in Toronto owns keeping it available around the clock, and this role joins that team.

Work includes tightening alerting so problems surface before customers notice anything, running blameless postmortems that dig into what actually needs to change rather than who was on call, and chipping away at the manual steps still needed to recover from the failure modes that show up most often. On-call rotates weekly across four engineers, and the team has already cut its mean time to recovery by more than half over the past year mostly through better alerting, a trend this role is expected to keep pushing rather than treat as finished.

Required: solid Kubernetes and AWS experience, with observability chops in Prometheus and Grafana specifically, since that is what the team's alerting runs on, plus genuine comfort operating production systems while an incident is actively unfolding. This seat calls for roughly three to five years of relevant operations or SRE experience. Fernway does not require prior experience with robotics or fleet systems specifically; that context builds quickly once you are on call.

Hybrid work out of the Toronto office is the norm here, with the team choosing in-person days around planning and postmortems rather than a fixed schedule. You would join a four-person on-call rotation and report to the SRE team lead for the fleet coordination platform, who reviews postmortems but leaves incident response itself to whoever is on call that week.

jobs.title: Senior Infrastructure Engineer, Edge Deployment (Contract)
jobs.summary:
Local edge computing inside customer warehouses keeps Fernway's robots working even when the link back to the cloud drops, and this four-month contract focuses on hardening that layer after a handful of field incidents traced back to network partitions. The infrastructure team wants the fix documented well enough to own outright once the contract ends.

Hardening the local orchestration setup against the network partitions that caused those incidents is the core of the engagement: building tooling to diagnose a failing edge node remotely instead of driving out to the site, and writing up the architecture clearly enough for the infrastructure team to maintain afterward. A site visit today means a multi-hour drive and a half-day of disrupted warehouse operations, exactly the cost this tooling removes. Occasional travel to a nearby customer site for hands-on testing is still expected.

Required: strong Kubernetes and networking experience, including real exposure to edge or IoT-style deployments where you cannot assume the network is up, plus solid Docker and Linux fundamentals for the orchestration work itself. Fernway is looking for roughly five to eight years of infrastructure experience for a contract at this scope, given the four-month timeline leaves little room for ramp-up. Prior experience specifically with warehouse robotics is not required — general edge-computing fluency transfers fine here.

Denver hosts this contract on-site, running for roughly four months with occasional travel to a nearby customer warehouse for testing. You would report to the infrastructure engineering manager for the term of the engagement and hand off directly to two infrastructure engineers who take over the work once the contract closes.

jobs.title: Senior Security Engineer, Fleet and Edge Systems
jobs.summary:
Fernway's robots and the edge devices they rely on sit inside customer facilities, creating a different attack surface than a browser-based product ever sees, and this senior role exists to own that surface specifically. It reports into the security team but works in close, regular contact with the embedded and fleet-platform groups, since most of the real risk sits where hardware meets network.

Leading a security review of the protocol connecting robots to the fleet cloud comes first, followed by work alongside the embedded team to harden the firmware-update mechanism against tampering — a compromised update could reach an entire fleet at once — and writing Fernway's first formal incident-response plan for compromised field hardware, which does not exist today. Several enterprise prospects have already flagged that gap during their own security reviews, giving the plan a real commercial deadline.

Required: strong network and embedded security experience, comfortable across threat modeling and hands-on penetration testing rather than one or the other, with enough Linux depth to work directly on real hardware rather than through a GUI. Fernway sets this seat at roughly five to eight years of security engineering experience. Direct background in IoT or robotics security is a strong plus and will speed up ramp-up considerably, but it is not required going in — the security fundamentals matter more than the specific hardware history.

Fernway leaves this one flexible: Denver's office or remote work anywhere in North America, with travel expected periodically for hands-on hardware security testing at customer sites. You would report to the head of security and coordinate closely with the embedded team's lead on anything touching firmware, without a fixed office-days requirement either way.

jobs.title: Junior Software Engineer, Developer CLI
jobs.summary:
Cinderforge ships a command-line tool and a set of SDKs that customers use to work with the cloud platform day to day, and a small developer-tools team is responsible for keeping both usable. This junior opening sits on that team, reporting to a senior engineer who reviews new hires' work closely before responsibilities widen.

Day-to-day work means fixing reported CLI bugs, adding automated test coverage to commands that today rely on manual verification, and keeping documentation examples in step with the API as it changes. A good part of the first few months goes into modernizing a cluster of older commands that predate the current API version and generate a disproportionate share of bug reports. Pairing happens twice a week during onboarding, then eases to once a week once you are shipping independently.

Required: solid Go fundamentals and real interest in developer experience and CLI design specifically, which is a different instinct than general backend work. This entry-level seat targets zero to two years of experience — coursework, internships or personal projects can stand in for a work history, though comfort with Git, REST APIs and writing tests should already be solid. Prior experience shipping a CLI tool professionally is not expected; the mentor engineer assigned to you exists precisely to build that skill on the job.

Cinderforge keeps the developer-tools team together in person at its Austin headquarters, on purpose, so pairing and reviews happen face to face rather than over a call. You would report to the developer-tools team lead, with the assigned mentor engineer handling day-to-day review for roughly your first several months.

jobs.title: Software Engineer, Compute Provisioning
jobs.summary:
Cinderforge's provisioning service is what actually spins up the virtual machines and containers customers request, and when it fails, those workloads simply do not start — which makes reliability the team's central concern more than almost anything else on the platform. This role joins that team as an individual contributor working across the provisioning path end to end.

Recent work from the team includes cutting average provisioning time by caching commonly used base images and closing a race condition that occasionally left orphaned resources behind after a failed request — a bug that was quietly costing the company real money in wasted compute before the fix shipped. You would carry a share of on-call for the provisioning service on a rotation with three other engineers, and the team treats provisioning incidents as a top priority regardless of whatever else is in flight that week.

Required: solid Go and Kubernetes experience, comfort with PostgreSQL and automated testing, and real ease debugging distributed failures that refuse to reproduce cleanly in a local environment. Cinderforge is looking to fill this seat with roughly three to five years of backend or infrastructure engineering experience. Direct gRPC experience is a plus given how the provisioning service talks to the rest of the platform, but the team is open to picking it up on the job if your RPC experience is elsewhere.

Remote work anywhere in the United States is the setup here, with the provisioning team anchored in Austin for planning purposes even though most engineers work from elsewhere. You would report to the engineering manager for compute provisioning and join the four-person on-call rotation covering the service around the clock.

jobs.title: Senior Software Engineer, Billing and Usage Metering
jobs.summary:
Every line item on a Cinderforge customer's monthly invoice traces back to the usage-metering pipeline this senior role would own, and accuracy errors here have direct financial consequences rather than just an annoyed support ticket. The billing team is small and fully distributed, which is part of why this seat carries real ownership rather than sitting under a more senior engineer.

Redesigning parts of the aggregation logic to support a new pricing tier launching this year is the headline project, alongside digging into a historical discrepancy that customer support has flagged twice without ever finding a clear root cause, and mentoring a mid-level engineer who recently joined the billing team. That unresolved discrepancy touches a small number of large accounts and has already triggered one uncomfortable finance escalation, so tracking it down is effectively this role's first real test rather than a background task.

Required: strong Go and distributed-systems experience, along with genuine comfort on Kafka, PostgreSQL and writing thorough automated tests, since the billing pipeline leans on all three under real load. Cinderforge sets this seat at roughly five to eight years of backend engineering experience, with prior work on a financially sensitive system valued highly given what a metering bug actually costs. Fluency with the company's specific pricing model is not assumed on day one — that is something this role learns by doing, not a prerequisite.

This position can be based in Europe or the United States, with the billing team fully distributed and meeting times rotating so no single region always bears the early or late calls. You would report to the engineering manager for billing and usage metering, who is based in Austin but manages the team's schedule around wherever people actually sit.

jobs.title: Infrastructure Engineer, Core Platform
jobs.summary:
The infrastructure Cinderforge's own product runs on is a separate concern from the compute platform sold to customers, and this role helps operate it as the company keeps expanding into new regions. It sits on the core-platform team, working alongside — but distinct from — the teams that build customer-facing infrastructure features.

Terraform modules used to stand up new regions are the first thing you would extend, alongside improving monitoring for services that have historically been under-instrumented, and taking part in the quarterly disaster-recovery exercise that tests failover between regions. The most recent region launch ran longer than planned because several modules quietly assumed configuration specific to the original region, and cleaning up those assumptions before the next expansion is one of this role's first projects.

Required: solid Terraform, Kubernetes and AWS experience, plus comfort with Prometheus-based monitoring and the CI/CD pipelines that ship infrastructure changes, and real interest in reliability practice rather than treating it as someone else's job. This seat's bar is roughly three to five years of infrastructure experience at Cinderforge. Prior experience with multi-region deployments is useful but not required — the team would rather teach it than lose a strong infrastructure engineer over it.

Two office days a week — Tuesdays and Wednesdays — anchor this hybrid role at Cinderforge's Austin office, set aside as the default time for cross-team planning. You would report to the core-platform engineering manager and take an active part in defining the reliability-review checklist the team is building for new region launches.

jobs.title: Site Reliability Engineer, Storage Platform
jobs.summary:
Underneath every compute instance Cinderforge sells sits a distributed block-and-object storage layer, and this role joins the SRE team that keeps it healthy under continuous production load. The team is small relative to how much of the platform depends on it, which means individual contributions here tend to show up quickly in the metrics everyone watches.

Storage-cluster performance tuning against production metrics is a constant here; the job also covers responding to incidents when a storage node degrades in ways that risk customer-visible latency, and automating the manual recovery steps that still page someone at three in the morning more often than anyone would like. On-call runs about one week in five, a cadence the team has deliberately kept sustainable, with a concrete goal of cutting manual recovery interventions in half over the next year.

Required: solid Kubernetes and distributed-storage experience, ideally including direct exposure to Ceph or a comparable system, Prometheus-based monitoring, and Go for the automation work, plus real comfort as a hands-on incident responder. Cinderforge scopes this seat to roughly three to five years of SRE or infrastructure experience. You do not need to have already solved the pattern of incidents clustering around certain hardware batches — that investigation is ongoing and part of what this role helps figure out.

Storage-platform engineers here work remotely anywhere in the United States, with the team anchored in Austin for planning even though most people sit elsewhere. You would report to the SRE manager for the storage platform and join the on-call rotation covering it, currently split across five engineers.

jobs.title: Cloud Infrastructure Engineer, Virtual Networking
jobs.summary:
Customer workloads reach the internet, and each other across regions, through the virtual networking layer this team owns, and this position sits inside that team at Cinderforge. Deep networking expertise is not assumed on day one here, but the role is built around developing it quickly through direct exposure to a live, business-critical network layer.

Latency complaints from customers running latency-sensitive workloads land here first, and helping debug them is routine, alongside extending automation around BGP configuration changes that used to be done by hand and occasionally caused costly mistakes. The role also feeds into modernizing how network policies get applied as infrastructure-as-code replaces manual steps, and one trading-adjacent customer has pushed the team to instrument cross-region paths more precisely, quietly becoming the team's new baseline.

Required: solid Linux, Terraform and Kubernetes experience, plus genuine willingness to learn networking internals — BGP included — on the job rather than treating it as a black box. Infrastructure engineering experience of roughly three to five years is what Cinderforge is aiming for with this hire. Deep prior BGP or networking-protocol expertise is a strong plus but explicitly not required — the team would rather teach networking to a strong infrastructure engineer than wait for someone who already has both skill sets.

Cinderforge's networking team sets its own in-person days at the Austin office rather than following a company-wide default, and this role follows that same hybrid pattern. You would report to the engineering manager for virtual networking and work alongside engineers who already own BGP automation, learning the protocol details directly from them rather than from documentation alone.

jobs.title: Senior Infrastructure Engineer, Kubernetes Platform (Contract)
jobs.summary:
Custom scripts have been Cinderforge's approach to internal Kubernetes tooling for years, added one at a time, and nobody on the platform team is happy running them anymore. This senior contract exists to replace that setup with a proper operator over roughly six months, and the team specifically wants someone who has already built a Kubernetes operator, not someone learning the pattern for the first time on this engagement.

The engagement covers designing the operator's reconciliation logic from scratch, migrating existing clusters over without customer-visible disruption, and pairing with two platform engineers who take over the operator once the contract ends, so the knowledge stays in-house. Weekly demos to the infrastructure director keep the project visible against its milestones. The current scripts have already caused two near-miss incidents in the past year, from different people running them with slightly different assumptions — the direct motivation for building an operator rather than continuing to patch scripts indefinitely.

Required: deep Kubernetes and Go experience, specifically including prior work building a Kubernetes operator rather than only operating clusters someone else built, plus enough CI/CD and observability background to wire the new operator into existing pipelines and dashboards. Cinderforge is looking for roughly six to eight years of infrastructure engineering experience given the contract's scope and timeline. Helm chart authoring is useful for the migration piece but not required going in, since the reconciliation-logic design work matters far more than familiarity with any one packaging tool.

Open to remote applicants anywhere in the United States, this contract runs for roughly six months with the platform team anchored in Austin. You would report to the infrastructure director for the length of the engagement.

jobs.title: Freelance Senior Infrastructure Engineer, Observability Consolidation
jobs.summary:
Three overlapping metrics systems, each inherited from a different acquisition, currently make up Cinderforge's observability stack, and this freelance engagement exists to consolidate them into one coherent system. None of the three systems' runbooks or dashboards agree with each other during a real incident, which is as much the point of this engagement as the technical pipeline work.

Designing a single OpenTelemetry-based pipeline is the anchor deliverable, alongside migrating a representative set of services onto it as a proof of concept ahead of the wider rollout, and writing a migration guide the rest of the infrastructure organization can follow without you in the room afterward. The engagement is scoped around that fixed deliverable rather than a set number of hours each week, which leaves real flexibility in how you structure the work over its course.

Required: deep observability experience, specifically OpenTelemetry, Prometheus and Grafana, backed by solid Kubernetes and Go skills for the pipeline work itself, plus comfort designing a migration path other engineers will execute after you hand it off. Cinderforge expects roughly five to eight years of relevant infrastructure experience for an engagement at this scope. Prior familiarity with the legacy metrics systems is not required — untangling how they disagree is part of the work.

Europe-based applicants can work this freelance engagement from anywhere in the region, structured around the fixed deliverable rather than a required weekly schedule. You would work largely independently, checking in with the infrastructure organization's leadership at agreed milestones rather than through a formal reporting line, and hand the finished migration guide off once the proof-of-concept rollout is complete.

jobs.title: Staff Infrastructure Engineer, Platform Reliability
jobs.summary:
Reliability at Cinderforge has largely been handled team by team without much shared strategy, and this staff seat exists to set technical direction across compute, storage and networking instead. Three incidents in the past year that a basic chaos-engineering practice would likely have caught are a large part of why this mandate now carries real executive sponsorship.

You would lead the rollout of a company-wide chaos-engineering practice that several teams have discussed but never implemented, review the reliability implications of major architecture proposals before they are approved rather than after something breaks, and act as an escalation point during the most serious production incidents regardless of which team owns the service. You would also help formalize an incident-severity framework that teams currently apply inconsistently, which makes postmortem data hard to compare across the organization.

Required: deep distributed-systems experience and real fluency with Kubernetes, Go, system design and chaos-engineering practice at a scale where architectural mistakes are expensive to reverse. Cinderforge sets this seat at eight or more years of infrastructure engineering experience, with enough credibility across disciplines to influence teams you do not manage directly. Formal management experience is not required — this stays an individual-contributor role, and influence here runs through technical judgment rather than a reporting line.

United States or Europe both work for this remote seat, with the infrastructure organization anchored in Austin for planning purposes. You would report directly to the VP of Infrastructure as an individual contributor, without a team of your own, and would be expected to work across the compute, storage and networking teams as needed rather than embedding permanently in any one of them.

jobs.title: Principal Infrastructure Engineer
jobs.summary:
Cinderforge is adding a principal engineer to own the multi-year technical roadmap for its core infrastructure — compute, storage, and the networking fabric that ties regions together. The company plans to roughly double its region count over the next three years, and the current storage and networking architecture was not built to absorb that gracefully, which this role exists to get ahead of.

This role is expected to spot architectural risks well before they become production incidents, represent infrastructure in the company's highest-level technical decisions — including ones with real business tradeoffs — and mentor staff and senior engineers across the infrastructure organization. The last major architecture bet the organization made, a multi-year commitment to a particular storage backend, is now being partially unwound at real cost, and this role's first substantive test will likely be earning enough trust that the next big bet gets more scrutiny before it locks in.

Required: a strong track record designing distributed, Kubernetes-based infrastructure at scale across multiple disciplines — compute, storage and networking together, not deep expertise in only one of them. Cinderforge sets this seat at roughly eight to twelve years of infrastructure engineering experience. Direct prior experience at exactly this scale of region count is not required; what matters more is having made a few big architecture calls before, and learned something from at least one that didn't fully work out.

On-site days at Cinderforge's Austin office run two per week, timed around the cross-team design sessions that happen there rather than over video. You would work at the same level as other principal engineers across the company, without any direct reports, and would be expected to spend time with staff and senior engineers across compute, storage and networking.

jobs.title: Infrastructure Team Lead, Storage Migration
jobs.summary:
Cinderforge's aging storage backend is partway through a multi-quarter replacement with something more scalable, and this lead role runs the four-person storage infrastructure team carrying that migration out. The current backend is already showing capacity warnings on its largest customer shard, which gives the project a real, if not yet urgent, deadline.

Planning the migration in phases that avoid customer-visible risk is the first job here, given how badly a storage migration can go if rushed; the role also means staying personally hands-on with the hardest technical problems rather than delegating everything, and representing the storage team in the infrastructure organization's monthly planning review. The team is four engineers today and expected to grow by one or two over the coming year as the migration's scope becomes clearer.

Required: deep storage and Kubernetes experience — direct exposure to Ceph specifically — plus Go for the tooling work and some prior experience leading a small team's planning through a genuinely risky technical project. Cinderforge scopes this seat by what it owns — running a four-person team through a multi-quarter migration with real customer-facing risk — rather than by a specific year count. Formal people-management credentials are not required if the technical leadership track record backs it up.

Migration planning and the monthly cross-team review set the rhythm for in-person days at Cinderforge's Austin office, where this hybrid role is based. You would report to the director of infrastructure and manage the four engineers on the storage migration team directly, with real latitude over how the migration phases are sequenced.

jobs.title: Engineering Manager, Cloud Networking
jobs.summary:
The cloud-networking manager role at Cinderforge has opened up after a director-level move elsewhere in the organization, and the company is filling it from inside the team rather than through an external search, given how much relationship and platform context the job assumes from day one.

Responsibilities include running the team's planning and one-on-ones, partnering with product on the roadmap for network-related customer features, and staying technical enough to participate credibly in architecture discussions rather than deferring entirely to senior engineers. The last three people to hold networking-adjacent management roles here all moved up from senior IC positions rather than being hired as managers directly, and that history still shapes how the team judges good technical judgment in this seat.

Required: solid networking and Kubernetes fluency, real people-management experience, and enough comfort with incident response to lead the team through one without panicking. Cinderforge scopes this seat by what it manages — a networking team where the manager is expected to stay technically credible — rather than by a year count. Coming up through networking specifically is not required; strong technical management experience in an adjacent infrastructure discipline transfers well here.

The cloud-networking team gathers in person at Cinderforge's Austin office full time, with no remote or hybrid option attached to this particular seat. You would report to the director of infrastructure and manage the engineers on the team directly, inheriting the roadmap and planning cadence the outgoing manager leaves behind.

jobs.title: Director of Security Engineering
jobs.summary:
Larger enterprise prospects keep asking Cinderforge for additional compliance certifications before they will sign, and this director role exists to lead the security organization through getting them. Two specific certifications are already named in signed contracts with penalty clauses tied to their delivery dates, giving this role a harder deadline than security leadership usually carries.

The role covers setting a multi-year security roadmap across platform hardening, customer-facing security features and the compliance processes that currently lag behind what the sales pipeline requires, managing two engineering managers, and serving as the executive point of contact during any serious security incident. The organization today runs roughly fifteen engineers across application security, detection and compliance, and this director is expected to make the case for further growth backed by a credible roadmap.

Required: a strong track record leading a security organization through a compliance-driven growth phase, with genuine depth in security architecture, cloud security and incident response rather than a purely managerial background. Cinderforge scopes this seat by the organization it runs — roughly fifteen engineers across three disciplines — rather than by a year count. Prior experience in exactly this industry is not required; compliance-driven security leadership experience elsewhere transfers directly.

Regular travel to Cinderforge's Austin headquarters comes with this hybrid role, expected even on weeks the broader security team works from home. You would report to the CTO, manage two engineering managers directly, and represent security at the executive level whenever a serious incident or a customer's compliance review requires it.

jobs.title: VP of Security
jobs.summary:
