Cinderforge's VP of Security reports directly to the CTO and holds overall accountability for security across the product, the platform sold to customers, and internal systems — a scope that has outgrown the company's current, lightweight security leadership structure. The board has asked for a formal risk briefing at every quarterly meeting going forward, a cadence the company has never sustained, and building the process to make that reliable is part of the job even though it isn't written down anywhere formal.

Three things anchor the mandate: building out a security leadership team as headcount roughly doubles over the next eighteen months, owning the relationship with external auditors through an upcoming certification renewal that several large deals are contingent on, and taking over the board's risk briefings. The board has also asked, informally, whether the company should commission a second-party security assessment of a key vendor before renewing a major contract, and this VP would likely scope and answer that question.

Required: prior experience as a security executive at a company of comparable scale, with fluency in executive and board communication, cloud security strategy and compliance oversight, rather than only technical depth in one narrow area. Cinderforge scopes this seat by the mandate — security accountability across product, platform and internal systems, reporting to the CTO — rather than by a year count. Deep hands-on penetration-testing skill is not required at this level; the job leans on strategy, risk framing and upward communication rather than technical work done personally.

Anywhere in the United States works for this remote seat, provided you can travel regularly for board and customer meetings. You would report directly to the CTO, lead the security organization as it's built out, and represent security in front of the board.

jobs.title: Security Engineer, Cloud Platform Hardening
jobs.summary:
Shared infrastructure underpins every customer workload at Cinderforge, and this role focuses specifically on hardening that shared layer rather than any single customer-facing feature. Demand for security review has been outpacing the platform-security function's capacity, with only a handful of new services reviewed each month today — a large part of why this opening exists.

Work includes reviewing new infrastructure services for security gaps before launch, building automated checks that catch cloud misconfigurations before they reach production, and contributing to incident response when something gets through anyway. Recent work closed gaps found in last quarter's Kubernetes security review, including clusters running with overly permissive RBAC bindings traced to a single misconfigured Terraform module. Those checks run against every new service, so false positives carry a real cost and need careful tuning.

Required: solid cloud-security fundamentals across AWS and Kubernetes, comfort with threat modeling for new infrastructure services, and enough Python to build and maintain the automated misconfiguration checks yourself. Candidates for this seat should have roughly three to five years of security engineering experience, Cinderforge's usual scope for the role. Hands-on penetration-testing experience is useful but not required — this role leans more on defensive tooling and review than on offensive security work.

Cinderforge leaves the arrangement flexible here — the Austin office or remote work anywhere in the United States, with no fixed in-office schedule attached. You would report to the platform-security team lead and work alongside the small group of engineers currently stretched thin across a growing list of infrastructure services awaiting review.

jobs.title: Software Engineer, Network Management Portal
jobs.summary:
Carrier customers configure and monitor their entire SD-WAN deployment through the web portal this role works on, and a confusing interface here turns directly into support tickets rather than staying a cosmetic problem. The team behind it ships weekly and treats those tickets as a primary source of prioritization rather than working strictly off a formal roadmap.

The device-health view got redesigned recently after feedback that it had become too cluttered to use during an active incident, and bulk-configuration support followed for customers managing hundreds of sites who had been scripting around its absence themselves. One carrier customer manages close to eight hundred sites through the portal alone, and their support tickets have become a fairly reliable early-warning system for usability problems before those problems show up more broadly across the customer base.

Required: solid TypeScript and React experience on the frontend, plus enough Node.js, PostgreSQL and REST API design sense to work across the full stack behind the portal rather than staying purely client-side. Glasspoint wants roughly three to five years of full-stack engineering experience for this seat. Prior experience with networking or SD-WAN concepts is not required going in — the team would rather teach that domain to a strong full-stack engineer than wait for someone who already knows it.

Europe-wide remote work is the default for this role, with the portal team anchored in London for planning and design reviews. You would report to the engineering manager for the network management portal, working alongside two other engineers on a team that ships to production every week rather than on a longer release cycle.

jobs.title: Senior Software Engineer, Configuration Management
jobs.summary:
Thousands of physical SD-WAN devices at customer sites receive their network-policy changes through the configuration management system this senior role owns, and a bad rollout here can take real customer sites offline rather than just causing a cosmetic glitch. An incident earlier this year pushed roughly three hundred sites offline at once and took the better part of a day to fully resolve, and it's still the team's reference point for any proposed change to rollouts.

You would redesign the rollout mechanism to better contain the blast radius of a bad configuration push, work directly with field engineers to understand failure modes that only show up on real hardware in real customer environments, and mentor two engineers who are newer to distributed-systems work through that redesign. The role also involves collaboration with the hardware team on firmware compatibility as new device models roll out, since a configuration change that assumes the wrong firmware version is the kind of mistake this redesign is meant to prevent.

Required: distributed-systems depth, strong Go skills, and hands-on comfort with PostgreSQL, gRPC and thorough test coverage for anything that touches the rollout path, plus a healthy respect for the blast radius of any change to a system that pushes configuration to physical devices in the field. Glasspoint sets this seat at roughly five to eight years of backend or distributed-systems experience. Prior experience specifically with SD-WAN hardware is not required — field engineers who lived through the incident are a better source of that context than a resume line would be.

London anchors the configuration-management team, but the role itself is remote anywhere in Europe, which is where most of the field-engineering collaboration originates. You would report to the engineering manager for configuration management.

jobs.title: Junior Network Operations Engineer
jobs.summary:
Glasspoint's global backbone and its customers' SD-WAN deployments are watched around the clock from the network operations center this entry-level role joins. The NOC handles somewhere around two hundred alerts on a typical day, and learning to tell the small number that matter from the noise quickly is really the core skill this role exists to build.

You would learn to triage incoming alerts, escalate genuine incidents to senior engineers while filtering out the considerable noise any large network generates, and gradually take on small configuration tasks under supervision as your networking knowledge builds over the first several months. New hires shadow an experienced analyst for roughly the first month before taking alerts on their own, and the fixed shift pattern — including evenings and occasional weekends — exists because NOC coverage has to be predictable around the clock.

Required: a genuine interest in networking and some foundational knowledge from coursework or a certification track, plus the calm temperament this kind of monitoring work rewards, and enough comfort with common monitoring tools and a ticketing queue to pick up the NOC's systems quickly. This entry-level seat targets zero to two years of experience — prior professional networking experience is not required, though basic Linux comfort should already be there. Deep BGP knowledge is not expected yet; that builds on the job.

Glasspoint's London network operations center is where this role sits full time, working a fixed shift pattern that includes evenings and occasional weekends rather than a standard nine-to-five. You would report to the NOC shift lead, with an experienced analyst assigned to shadow you directly during your first month on alerts.

jobs.title: Network Infrastructure Engineer
jobs.summary:
Glasspoint's own physical backbone network is a separate concern from the SD-WAN equipment deployed at customer sites, and this role helps operate — and gradually automate — that backbone infrastructure. The network spans several physical points of presence across Europe, and learning the quirks specific to each one tends to take longer than any amount of documentation can really substitute for.

Typical work means writing scripts to replace manual configuration steps that today rely on tribal knowledge held by a few senior engineers, taking part in planned maintenance windows for core routing changes that have to be coordinated carefully to avoid customer impact, and writing runbooks the wider infrastructure team can follow during an incident instead of paging the same two people every time. Those maintenance windows happen roughly once a month and need sign-off from two senior engineers before they proceed.

Required: solid BGP and general networking fundamentals, plus enough automation-scripting ability and comfort with monitoring tooling to support the work this role is building toward. Glasspoint is targeting roughly three to five years of networking or infrastructure experience for this hire. Deep Cisco IOS expertise is useful given the current hardware but not required on day one — the automation work matters more here than depth on any single vendor's command syntax.

Glasspoint keeps this hybrid role tied to two set days a week at the London office, to keep the team aligned on maintenance scheduling and cross-training on the backbone's quirks. You would report to the backbone infrastructure team lead and work alongside the senior engineers whose sign-off is needed before any core routing change goes live.

jobs.title: Infrastructure Engineer, Monitoring (Part-Time)
jobs.summary:
Glasspoint Networks operates a growing network estate, and this part-time role sits with the team that maintains its network management platform. The focus is observability: the dashboards, alerting rules and automated checks that show what the network is doing and catch problems before they reach an on-call engineer.

You will build and maintain Grafana dashboards across network segments that currently have none, write Python checks for conditions the existing alerting misses, and tune alert rules so they fire on what actually matters. You will occasionally join a live incident to help the on-call engineer interpret what the dashboards are showing. The first quarter is already scoped: dashboards for two unmonitored segments, then automated checks for the alert classes that keep arriving as pages rather than warnings.

Required: production experience with Prometheus and Grafana, and enough networking background to build dashboards that reflect what matters during an incident rather than what is easy to graph. You should be comfortable writing and maintaining small Python scripts, since that is how the checks are built. Roughly three to five years of hands-on monitoring work is what this seat calls for. Prior on-call experience is useful but not required.

Fifteen hours a week, scheduled flexibly around the team's core hours rather than fixed to set days. Fully remote across Europe, with the platform team anchored in Stockholm. The role reports to the staff engineer on the network management platform, who reviews dashboard designs before they go live and otherwise leaves day-to-day prioritisation to whoever holds the seat.

jobs.title: Network Software Engineer, Device Firmware
jobs.summary:
Glasspoint's SD-WAN appliances run control-plane software that this role helps build, working closer to the hardware than the cloud services that manage the fleet remotely. The team sits inside network engineering, based at the Stockholm hardware lab where physical test rigs sit a few steps from the desks that debug against them.

Day-to-day work means fixing protocol-handling bugs surfaced during interoperability testing against roughly six third-party vendors' equipment, contributing to the firmware release currently in progress, and pairing with hardware engineers when a bug turns out to be a driver issue rather than a control-plane one. Each new customer environment tends to surface at least one vendor combination the lab has not tried before.

Required: solid C and networking-protocol experience, plus genuine comfort working close to embedded hardware rather than purely in software; expect real time in the lab, not just at a desk. Linux systems knowledge and a disciplined testing habit matter as much as raw protocol depth. This opening calls for roughly three to five years in embedded or network-adjacent software. A formal electrical-engineering background is not required; the firmware and board documentation cover what you need to know about the hardware itself.

Full time, based on-site at the Stockholm hardware lab five days a week; this is not a remote or hybrid seat, since proximity to the test rigs is part of how the debugging gets done. The role sits within the firmware team inside network engineering, reporting to that team's engineering manager and working alongside hardware engineers who share the same floor and the same test equipment.

jobs.title: Senior Network Engineer, SD-WAN Deployment Automation (Contract)
jobs.summary:
New SD-WAN sites still need more manual effort than Glasspoint's deployment team wants, and this senior contract role exists to automate that away. The engagement sits with network engineering for roughly five months, working against a defined milestone plan rather than a loosely scoped brief.

The work covers designing an Ansible-based provisioning workflow that handles common site configurations without hand-holding, integrating it with the existing configuration management system so the two do not drift apart, and training the deployment team on the new process before the engagement ends. A typical deployment today takes a field engineer most of a day; the target is under an hour of hands-on time for the common cases, leaving only genuinely unusual sites for manual attention.

Required: strong Python and Ansible experience, plus real networking depth, including BGP, since automation that does not understand the underlying protocols tends to create new problems rather than remove old ones. Five to eight years of practical, hands-on network engineering experience is what this contract is scoped for. You do not need prior exposure to Glasspoint's specific configuration-management tooling; solid Ansible fundamentals transfer directly once you see how the pieces fit together.

Roughly five months as a fixed-term contract, fully remote across Europe, with the deployment team anchored in Stockholm for the occasional working session. Progress is tracked biweekly against milestones agreed with the head of network engineering, who signs off on the automation design before it ever touches a live production site.

jobs.title: Senior Site Reliability Engineer, Network Management Cloud
jobs.summary:
Cloud services that manage Glasspoint's SD-WAN fleet sit at the center of this reliability role: when they go down, customer devices can lose the ability to receive configuration updates until service returns, which raises the stakes on the team's day-to-day work. The role sits inside the network management cloud team, hybrid out of the London office.

Leading incident response for the most serious outages is central to the role, alongside improving automated failover between regions that has been drilled but never fully relied on during a real incident, and building pre-incident visibility so problems surface before customers notice. The failover mechanism last ran cleanly in a drill six months ago, though nobody is fully confident it would hold up under a genuine regional outage.

Required: solid Kubernetes and incident-response experience, Go for the tooling this team maintains, and Prometheus for the pre-incident visibility work this role owns, plus enough networking background to reason about the systems being protected rather than treating them as a black box. This seat calls for five to eight years of production reliability work. You do not need prior experience running multi-region failover specifically; the team's own setup is something you learn during onboarding and the first game-day drill.

Hybrid, with the team expected in the London office several days a week. On-call runs one week in four, a rotation the team has found sustainable given how the load is shared across its members. Reports to the engineering manager for the network management cloud team, working closely with network engineering, whose devices depend on this platform staying up.

jobs.title: Staff Infrastructure Engineer, Network Management Platform
jobs.summary:
The interface connecting Glasspoint's cloud management layer to physical devices across thousands of customer sites has picked up real inconsistencies as the hardware line expanded, and this staff role sets technical direction for fixing it. The seat sits inside the network management platform team, on-site full time out of the London office.

Proposing a cleaner abstraction between device types that currently need special-cased code is the central piece of work here, alongside reviewing architecture proposals from across network engineering before they are approved, and working personally through the highest-risk parts of any major redesign. Glasspoint now supports six hardware generations in the field at once, each with its own quirks, and consolidating that special-cased code without breaking any of them is the central technical challenge.

Required: deep networking and distributed-systems experience, hands-on Kubernetes fluency for how the cloud management layer is actually deployed, and comfort with system design at the scale of a multi-generation hardware fleet. Eight or more years in infrastructure or platform engineering is the level this staff opening is set at. You do not need experience with all six hardware generations already in the field; that context builds over the first few months working alongside the engineers who know each one.

Based on-site at the London office full time, since the cross-team architecture conversations this role requires have been more effective in person. You would also mentor two senior engineers who have proposed competing approaches to this problem without either being formally adopted, a stalemate this role is expected to help resolve. Reports to the director overseeing the network management platform.

jobs.title: Principal Network Software Engineer
jobs.summary:
Some of Glasspoint's protocol implementations date back to the company's earliest hardware, built for traffic volumes far below what carrier deployments see today. This principal role guides the technical direction of the network software organization as those implementations get modernized for current scale, working two days a week from the London office for cross-team design sessions.

You would evaluate where existing implementations will not scale to volumes projected over the next several years, prototype alternative approaches personally before proposing them broadly, and mentor senior engineers across the control-plane and cloud-management teams who will eventually build whatever direction is chosen. Traffic through the largest carrier deployments has grown roughly fourfold in three years.

Required: a strong track record with networking protocols and distributed systems at meaningful scale, and system-design judgment good enough to weigh backward compatibility against clean-sheet redesign. This is a principal-level opening, generally eight or more years of relevant experience, though depth on protocol work specifically matters most. A background co-authoring a standards-track protocol specification is not required, though it would not hurt.

Hybrid, two days a week in the London office for design sessions, with the rest worked remotely. At least one core protocol module is understood by only two engineers still at the company, making this as much a knowledge-continuity problem as a scaling one. Reports directly to the VP of network engineering.

jobs.title: Freelance Senior Security Engineer, Network Product Assessment
jobs.summary:
Several pending enterprise deals depend on a security certification the sales team needs, and this freelance engagement covers the security assessment of Glasspoint's SD-WAN product line required to get there. The work runs against network engineering and security together, scoped for roughly two months.

The scope includes reviewing the device-to-cloud communication protocol for weaknesses an attacker with network access might exploit, testing the update mechanism for tampering resistance given how much damage a compromised firmware update could cause, and producing a report with prioritized remediation guidance engineering teams can act on directly, rather than a purely academic findings list nobody has time to work through.

Required: strong network security and penetration-testing experience, ideally including prior work on embedded or IoT-style devices, comfort working from Linux for the tooling this kind of assessment depends on, plus enough cryptography grounding to assess the update mechanism properly. This engagement is scoped for someone with five to eight years of practical security-assessment experience, done hands-on rather than from behind a desk. A specific vendor security certification is not required, though relevant ones are welcome context.

Scheduled flexibly around assessment milestones over a roughly two-month engagement rather than a fixed weekly commitment. Based from London or elsewhere in Europe, working directly with Glasspoint's security and network engineering leads rather than through an account manager. A comparable assessment two years ago missed a firmware downgrade vector a customer later found independently.

jobs.title: Device Security Engineer, SD-WAN Hardware
jobs.summary:
Carrier and enterprise customers buy SD-WAN devices and management software that, until now, has relied mostly on external assessments for security coverage. This role adds dedicated internal ownership of product security for that hardware line, sitting inside the security team with a hybrid schedule out of the London office.

Responsibilities include reviewing new features for security gaps before release, coordinating with an external penetration-testing firm on the annual assessment so findings actually get tracked and closed, and helping triage vulnerability reports that arrive through customer channels. The role inherits a backlog of roughly a dozen findings from the most recent external assessment, several touching firmware update verification, and working through it is one of the first deliverables.

Required: threat modeling and network security fundamentals, working Python for tooling and scripts, and comfort reading code during review rather than only reports. Three to five years of relevant security or software experience fits this opening well. Deep firmware reverse-engineering skill is not required; the external assessment firm covers that depth, and this role coordinates and triages rather than duplicating it.

Hybrid, with regular time in the London office alongside the hardware team this role coordinates with most closely; coordination happens informally today, mostly over chat. Reports to the head of product security, working day-to-day with the hardware team and the external penetration-testing firm's lead tester on a more structured review checkpoint.

jobs.title: Security Team Lead, Detection Engineering
jobs.summary:
Detection engineering at Glasspoint watches for suspicious activity across both corporate systems and the infrastructure supporting customer networks, and this lead role oversees the three engineers who build and tune the alerting logic that does that watching. The team works on-site from the London office.

You would prioritize the detection backlog, personally investigate the more ambiguous alerts that need experienced judgment rather than a simple rule, and represent detection engineering in the monthly security leadership review where priorities get negotiated against other security work. The backlog currently runs close to forty open items, several more than six months old, and deciding which are still worth building is one of the first real calls this lead makes.

Required: solid SIEM and detection-engineering experience, genuine incident-response judgment, and enough Python to read and adjust the team's detection logic directly. This is a lead role scoped by team size and backlog ownership rather than a fixed year count, though prior experience running or senior-contributing to a detection team of a similar size is expected. Prior experience specifically with supply-chain attacks against network vendors is not required; the team is building that expertise together.

Full time, on-site from the London office; the rest of security works a hybrid-friendly schedule, but this role is expected in person given the operational nature of the work. Reports to the head of security and leads three detection engineers directly, representing the function in the monthly leadership review where priorities get weighed against other security work.

jobs.title: Security Operations Manager
jobs.summary:
Four analysts covering detection, incident response and vulnerability management make up Glasspoint's security operations team, and this internal posting covers the manager role over that team following a recent restructuring. The team works on-site from the London office.

The role involves running the team's shift and on-call schedule, coordinating the response to any significant incident from first alert through resolution, and reporting a monthly risk summary to the head of security that leadership reads and acts on. The team absorbed vulnerability management from a separate group in the last reorganization, and folding that workflow into the existing on-call structure without overloading any single analyst is one of the first practical problems this manager inherits.

Required: solid SIEM and incident-response fluency, prior experience managing or acting as senior lead on a security operations team of a comparable size, and enough compliance and vulnerability-management background to keep the risk summary credible. This is a manager-level opening scoped by team size and operational scope rather than a fixed year count. Hands-on rule-writing is not expected day to day, though enough technical fluency to review the team's work closely is.

Onsite in the London office five days a week, running a team of four analysts and their shift and on-call rotation. Reports to the head of security. Given the operational knowledge required to run the team effectively from day one, this opening is limited to internal candidates already familiar with how the team's current processes work.

jobs.title: Director of Product Security
jobs.summary:
Product security at Glasspoint has grown without a single accountable leader as the company scaled its SD-WAN hardware and cloud management software into new markets, and this director role exists to change that. The seat sits at the top of the product security function.

Building a small team of product security engineers largely from scratch is the first big task, alongside setting the technical requirements new certifications will demand of the hardware and firmware teams, and briefing the executive team on product-related security risk each quarter in terms they can act on. Entry into two new regulated markets is planned for next year, each with its own certification regime.

Required: security architecture and risk-management depth, people-leadership experience building a function rather than only running an established one, and the political patience to get hardware and firmware teams that do not report into security to prioritize its requirements anyway. This is a director-level role scoped by the size of the function being built rather than a fixed year count. Prior experience specifically with networking hardware is not required; security leadership across a regulated product line matters more.

Full time, with a flexible split between the London office and remote work across the rest of the United Kingdom. Reports directly to the executive team and briefs them quarterly, with no existing team inherited: the first hires, and the roadmap for meeting both markets' certification regimes without one blocking the other, are this director's own to make.

jobs.title: Junior Software Engineer, Detection Rule Platform
jobs.summary:
Security teams at other companies rely on the threat-detection platform Alderbrook builds, and this junior role joins the engineering team that maintains its rule-processing engine, the software that evaluates incoming security events against detection logic.

Early work typically includes fixing bugs found in existing detection rules, writing tests for edge cases the current suite misses, and shadowing a senior engineer during customer-reported incident investigations to see how the platform gets used under pressure. New engineers generally start on well-scoped bugs before moving to small new rules under review, a pace the team has found works better than open-ended detection logic before you have context on how customers actually use the platform.

Required: solid Python and SQL fundamentals, comfort with Git and REST APIs, and a habit of writing tests alongside code rather than after it. Up to two years of experience, internships included, is enough to be considered for this entry-level opening. No prior professional security experience is required; a senior engineer walks new hires through past customer incidents in the first two weeks to build the rest of the context on the job.

Full time, two days a week in the Boston office during the first year while you build context on the platform, remote the rest of the time. Reports to the engineering manager for the detection rule platform, working alongside three to four other engineers who each mix bug fixes with small new rules under review.

jobs.title: Backend Engineer, Security Alert Pipeline
jobs.summary:
Alderbrook's alert pipeline evaluates every security event from customer environments against thousands of detection rules in near real time before anything reaches an analyst's queue, and this role works on that pipeline directly. The team sits inside the detection platform group and works fully remotely across the United States.

Recent projects include reducing latency that had started to lag during traffic spikes on customers' busiest days, and fixing a deduplication bug that was creating duplicate alerts for a subset of customers and eroding trust in the platform's alert volume. The pipeline processes tens of millions of events on a typical day, and the team treats any change to the deduplication logic as high-risk given how directly it affects what an analyst sees.

Required: solid Python and streaming-data experience, ideally including Kafka or a comparable message system, plus working knowledge of PostgreSQL and Elasticsearch for how the pipeline stores and indexes events. Backend engineers with three to five years of experience fit this opening well. Prior experience specifically with detection-rule semantics is not required; that is learned on the job through the incident log the team keeps.

On-call for the pipeline rotates across four engineers, including whoever holds this role, with a clear escalation path for anything touching detection accuracy specifically. Reports to the engineering manager for the detection platform. The position is fully remote within the United States; Boston is where much of the team happens to sit, but it is not a requirement.

jobs.title: Software Engineer, Customer Data Integrations
jobs.summary:
Customer telemetry reaches Alderbrook's platform through a growing library of integrations with cloud accounts, identity providers and endpoint tools, and this role maintains that library. The team partners closely with a solutions engineer who surfaces most integration requests directly from customer conversations.

Typical work includes building a new integration for a data source customers have requested across several release cycles, fixing authentication issues that surface when a partner API changes without notice, and keeping the customer-facing integration guides current for solutions engineers to use during onboarding calls. The library currently covers close to thirty distinct data sources, growing by a handful each release cycle.

Required: solid Python and REST API experience, comfort working through OAuth flows across a wide variety of third-party providers, and enough PostgreSQL fluency to model new data sources cleanly. Three to five years of backend or integrations engineering experience fits this opening. You do not need experience with every identity provider customers use already; the pattern transfers after the first couple of integrations you build.

The solutions engineer this role partners with ranks requested sources loosely by deal size, the de facto signal for what gets built next. Roughly a quarter of monthly support tickets trace back to a third-party provider changing behavior without warning. Work happens fully remotely across the United States and Canada, reporting to the engineering manager for customer integrations.

jobs.title: Senior Software Engineer, Executive Reporting (Contract)
jobs.summary:
Alderbrook's executive reporting module, the screen customer security leadership teams use to review their organization's posture, needs a largely ground-up rebuild, and this contract role covers roughly four months of that work. The engagement sits with the platform team, working closely with product and a designer.

The work involves redesigning the underlying data model to support the new metrics product wants to expose in the next release, building the report-generation service in Python from the ground up, and coordinating closely with a designer on the visualizations so the output is something an executive actually wants to look at. Product has already committed the new metrics to a named release date in customer-facing marketing material.

Required: strong Python and data-visualization experience, solid PostgreSQL for the data-model redesign, and REST API fluency for how the service exposes report data. Five to eight years of relevant engineering experience is the level this fixed-scope engagement is set at. Design taste is not required; a designer owns the visual decisions, and the job is building reliably to that spec rather than making the calls yourself.

Progress is reviewed every two weeks against agreed milestones over the roughly four-month engagement, which carries a firmer deadline than a typical internal rebuild given the release date already committed in marketing material. Work is fully remote within the United States, coordinating closely with the platform team's engineering manager and a designer.

jobs.title: Senior Software Engineer, Detection Engine Performance
jobs.summary:
Alderbrook is migrating its detection engine, the software that evaluates customer security telemetry against the rule library, from Python to Rust for performance reasons, and this role takes a leading part in finishing that work. The team sits within the detection platform group and works fully remotely across the United States.

Completing the port for the highest-traffic rule categories still running the older implementation is the main task, alongside benchmarking the new implementation against the old one to catch behavioral differences before they reach customers as a missed or duplicated alert, and mentoring two engineers less familiar with Rust through the transition. The port completed so far has cut evaluation latency by more than sixty percent on migrated categories.

Required: strong Python experience and genuine comfort with Rust, or a clear track record picking up systems languages quickly, plus distributed-systems fundamentals and familiarity with Elasticsearch for how results get indexed downstream. Engineers with five to eight years of experience are the target for this opening. A public record of open-source Rust contributions is not required; production experience gained on a team is enough.

Reporting to the engineering manager for the detection platform, the role works closely with detection engineering on the security side of the business. The categories still on Python tend to be the oldest and least documented in the codebase, so part of the job is archaeology into decisions nobody currently at the company remembers making. Fully remote within the United States, with no default office hub.

jobs.title: Infrastructure Engineer, Security Data Platform
jobs.summary:
Security telemetry ingestion and storage at Alderbrook has grown faster over the past year than the infrastructure team supporting it, and this role supports the infrastructure underneath that data platform. The team works three days a week from the Boston office, which overlaps with most of the wider infrastructure group.

You would extend Terraform modules for a new storage tier the data team is introducing to handle growing retention requirements several enterprise customers have asked for, improve CI/CD pipeline reliability that has been a recurring complaint from engineers shipping to production, and take part in the team's on-call rotation for infrastructure-level incidents. Retention requirements vary considerably by customer contract, from as short as ninety days to well over a year.

Required: solid Kubernetes and Terraform experience, working knowledge of AWS and Kafka, and enough CI/CD familiarity to debug pipeline flakiness under load. This opening is set for someone with three to five years of infrastructure engineering experience. Prior experience specifically with security-data retention rules is not required; that context is provided once you join and start working with the data team.

Full time, three days a week in the Boston office, overlapping with most of the infrastructure team, remote the other two days. CI/CD reliability complaints spike noticeably whenever a large schema migration is in flight, which is one of the more visible near-term wins available here. Reports to the engineering manager for infrastructure.

jobs.title: Senior Infrastructure Engineer, Multi-Tenant Isolation
jobs.summary:
Multi-tenant isolation underpins Alderbrook's entire product credibility, since a leak between customer environments would be a serious incident for any platform and a particularly damaging one for a security company. This senior role owns the infrastructure work behind keeping those environments properly isolated, working fully remotely across the United States.

The work includes auditing existing isolation boundaries for gaps that have not yet caused a problem but reasonably could, hardening the Kubernetes namespace configuration that enforces tenant separation across the platform, and running a joint review with the security team before any change to the isolation model ships to production. A recent internal red-team exercise found a theoretical path between two tenant namespaces that, while never exploited, became the top item on this role's roadmap.

Required: deep Kubernetes networking experience, solid Terraform and AWS skills, and distributed-systems judgment good enough to reason about failure modes that have not happened yet. Five to eight years of infrastructure experience, ideally including isolation or security-hardening work specifically, fits this opening. A specific security certification such as CISSP is not required; demonstrated isolation work matters more.

Joint reviews with the security team happen before any isolation-model change ships, and the role reports to the engineering manager for platform infrastructure. The red-team finding also raised an open question about re-verifying isolation boundaries automatically after every change rather than only during scheduled audits. Fully remote within the United States, with no fixed office expectation.

jobs.title: Detection Engineer, Cloud Threats
jobs.summary:
Attacker research only matters to customers once it becomes logic that runs reliably against their telemetry, and that translation is the core of this detection engineer role. The team works on-site from the Boston office, closely with the threat intelligence group that supplies most of the raw research.

Writing and maintaining the detection rules that form the core of Alderbrook's product is the daily work here, turning research into logic that catches real attacker behavior without generating false positives that erode an analyst's trust in the alert queue. Recent work has included building detections for a newly disclosed cloud misconfiguration technique within days of public disclosure, and tuning a rule category several customers flagged as too noisy.

Required: solid SIEM and detection-engineering experience, working SQL for querying telemetry, and enough Python or similar scripting ability to move quickly from research to a working rule. Someone three to five years into a detection or security engineering career is a good match for this opening. Prior experience specifically with cloud misconfiguration research is not required; that comes from the threat intelligence team, and the job is turning it into a working rule quickly.

On-site from the Boston office full time; this team works in person rather than hybrid, given how closely it coordinates day to day with threat intelligence and customer-facing teams. Turnaround on a newly disclosed technique is treated as a competitive metric internally, targeted within forty-eight hours of credible disclosure. Reports to the engineering manager for detection engineering.

jobs.title: Security Analyst, Threat Intelligence
jobs.summary:
Threat intelligence feeds both Alderbrook's own detection engineering team and the briefings shared directly with customers, and this internal posting covers the analyst role that produces it. The team works closely alongside detection engineering, the group that turns this research into shipped rules.

Tracking emerging attacker groups relevant to the customer base across several industry verticals is the daily work, writing research that detection engineering turns into new rules within the same sprint when a finding is urgent, and contributing to the quarterly threat landscape report customers reference in their own board updates. The most recent quarterly report was cited directly in at least two customer board presentations, feedback that has raised the internal bar for how polished and defensible each edition needs to be going forward.

Required: threat intelligence and OSINT research skills, working knowledge of SIEM tooling to verify findings against real telemetry, and clear writing for reports that customers pass up to their own leadership. Relevant analyst experience of three to five years fits this opening. Deep malware reverse-engineering skill is not required; the basics plus strong research and writing carry most of the role day to day.

Full time, hybrid from the Boston office alongside detection engineering, with no fixed number of required days beyond what the team's own schedule sets. Because the role builds directly on relationships formed during a prior internal rotation through both teams, it is open only to current employees rather than posted externally.

jobs.title: Senior Security Engineer, Incident Response (Contract)
jobs.summary:
Incident response retainer hours from several new enterprise contracts have stretched Alderbrook's IR practice thinner than usual, and this senior contract role exists to relieve that pressure for roughly three months, with possible extension depending on demand. The engagement sits with the security team, working fully remotely across the United States.

Leading customer-facing incident investigations from initial triage through documented root cause is the main task, producing forensic reports customers can share directly with their own leadership without translation, and documenting playbooks the permanent incident response team can reuse on future engagements rather than starting from scratch each time. Several cases tend to run concurrently, so juggling more than one customer's timeline at once is normal.

Required: strong incident-response and digital-forensics experience, ideally including prior client-facing IR work, plus SIEM and threat-hunting skills for the investigative side and enough scripting ability to automate repetitive parts of a case. This engagement wants five to eight years of incident-response experience, gained hands-on rather than in an advisory capacity. A specific forensics-tool certification is not required; demonstrated casework matters more.

Reporting to the head of security for the engagement's duration, the role works directly alongside the permanent incident response team rather than in isolation. Retainer hours committed to the newest contracts alone already exceed what the permanent team can absorb without this contractor's help. The contract runs roughly three months with possible extension, fully remote within the United States.

jobs.title: Freelance Senior Security Engineer, Red Team Exercises
jobs.summary:
Red team exercises test whether the detections Alderbrook sells actually catch realistic attacker behavior, and this freelance engagement covers that work against the company's own corporate and product environments under controlled conditions. The engagement is scoped to conclude within a two-month window.

Planning and executing a multi-stage attack simulation against agreed targets without tipping off defenders ahead of time is the core of the work, documenting which detections fired and which gaps were found, and presenting findings to both the security and detection engineering teams in a session where hard questions are expected and welcomed on both sides. Targets are agreed in advance with security leadership so the simulation stays within bounds everyone has consented to.

Required: strong red-team and social-engineering experience, solid penetration-testing fundamentals, and clear reporting skills for findings that both security and engineering teams will act on. Five to eight years of offensive security work is the level this freelance engagement is scoped at. A specific offensive-security certification is not required; a track record of realistic engagements matters more.

Scheduled flexibly within an overall two-month window, working from Boston, elsewhere in the United States, or Canada. The last exercise, run about a year ago, found two gaps that led directly to new detection rules now shipped to every customer, the standard this engagement is implicitly measured against. Findings are reported jointly to the security and detection engineering teams.

jobs.title: Staff Security Engineer, Platform Security
jobs.summary:
Platform security at Alderbrook carries unusual visibility internally, since a security company's product credibility depends on practicing what it sells. This staff role sets technical direction for how the company secures its own platform, working fully remotely across the United States as an individual contributor with company-wide influence.

Leading the security review for any major new platform capability before launch rather than after the fact is the core responsibility, alongside building automated checks that catch common misconfigurations before they reach production, and acting as the technical escalation point during any security incident affecting the platform itself. Every new platform capability now goes through a security design review this role would chair.

Required: deep security-architecture experience, solid threat-modeling and cloud-security skills, including Kubernetes security specifically, and enough Python to build the automated checks this role owns. Eight or more years of security engineering experience is the level this staff opening is set at. People-management experience is not required; this is an individual-contributor role with no direct reports.

The role reports to the VP overseeing platform security and carries company-wide influence despite having no direct reports of its own. The design-review gate itself was added eighteen months ago in direct response to a near-miss that almost shipped without one. Work is fully remote within the United States, without a default office hub.

jobs.title: Principal Security Engineer, Detection Strategy
jobs.summary:
Detection strategy at Alderbrook needs someone thinking from both an attacker's and a defender's perspective at once, and this principal role owns the long-term technical direction of both the security of Alderbrook's own platform and the detection capabilities it sells to customers. The role is based in the Boston office with flexibility for occasional remote weeks.

Identifying strategic gaps in current detection coverage well ahead of customer complaints is the mandate here; you would also prototype solutions to the hardest technical problems personally rather than only writing proposals for others to build, and mentor senior engineers across both the platform security and detection engineering teams. Coverage gaps against a publicly tracked category of cloud-identity attacks have come up in three separate customer escalations this year.

Required: a strong track record spanning both offensive and defensive security work, deep security-architecture and threat-modeling skills, and system-design judgment for detection coverage at product scale. Eight or more years of security engineering experience is the level this principal opening is set at. People-management experience is not required either; this is an individual-contributor track with broad technical influence instead.

Full time, based in the Boston office most weeks with flexibility for occasional remote weeks when travel or personal circumstances call for it. Two of the customer escalations came from the same industry vertical within weeks of each other, an open question this role is expected to help answer. Reports directly to the VP of security.

jobs.title: Engineering Manager, Detection Engineering
jobs.summary:
Six engineers responsible for the rule library underpinning Alderbrook's core product make up the detection engineering team, and this internal posting covers the manager role over that team following a recent reorganization. The team works on-site from the Boston office.

Running the team's roadmap in partnership with the head of product is the core of the job, staying close enough to the technical work to review the highest-impact rule changes personally rather than delegating every decision, and continuing mentorship relationships built during a recent internal rotation through the team. The roadmap currently spans three active initiatives, and this manager decides which one gets a given engineer's time each week.

Required: solid detection-engineering fluency, prior experience managing or acting as senior technical lead on a team of a comparable size, and enough SIEM and project-planning skill to run a roadmap credibly. This is a manager-level opening scoped by team size and technical scope rather than a fixed year count. Deep rule-writing expertise is not required day to day, though enough to review the team's highest-impact changes closely is.

Managing six engineers directly, on-site from the Boston office full time. The reorganization that created this opening also merged two smaller rule-review sub-teams into one, so an early priority is reconciling two slightly different review standards into a single one the whole team can work from. This role is being filled internally rather than through an external search.

jobs.title: Director of Security Research
jobs.summary:
Alderbrook Cyber's detection product competes on original research into attacker behavior rather than public threat feeds, and this director leads the team that produces it. The group sits inside the security organization, publishing findings that double as material customers can act on inside their own environments.

Setting the research agenda is most of the job: balance defensive publication value against findings a customer can apply directly, and judge which threads are worth a team's time. The director will grow a five-person group into a larger, more specialized team this year and represent Alderbrook at industry conferences, presenting to an audience of peers and prospective buyers alike. Two reports published last year drew attention well beyond Alderbrook's usual reach, and marketing now tracks research output as a channel in its own right.

Required: a strong personal track record in threat research or malware analysis, with findings that held up under outside scrutiny, plus prior experience leading a research team and enough detection-engineering fluency to steer what the downstream team builds from the research. This is a director-level seat judged on the scope of the program run rather than a specific year count. A formal academic background, a doctorate or a list of published papers, is not required; what matters is a track record of findings that held up once shipped.

The arrangement splits flexibly between Alderbrook's Boston office and remote work anywhere in the United States, full-time, with conference travel recurring through the year, concentrated around major security events. The director reports to the VP of Security and sets the research team's priorities directly, without needing sign-off on individual publications.

jobs.title: Senior Data Engineer, Vehicle Telemetry
jobs.summary:
Vehicle telemetry at Fernwood Fleet Analytics arrives from roughly forty thousand vehicles across a dozen European fleet operators, and this engineer owns the pipelines that turn that raw feed into data the rest of the company can trust. The role sits on the data platform team, working closest with the science group that consumes the output.

Kafka and Airflow carry the vehicle telemetry stack, both straining as several large fleets onboarded within the same quarter. The near-term priority is redesigning ingestion so it absorbs bursty traffic without dropping records during peak commuting hours. Day to day work includes maintaining existing pipelines, building new ones as fleets add sensor types like tire-pressure or battery-health monitors, and coordinating with data science so telemetry lands clean enough for predictive-maintenance models.

Required: production experience with Kafka or a comparable streaming system at meaningful scale, strong SQL and Python, and enough Airflow experience to redesign a DAG under load rather than just schedule one. Data engineers with five to eight years under their belt are the target for this seat. Familiarity with the automotive or logistics domain is not required; the telemetry concepts and fleet-specific quirks are taught on the job during the first few weeks.

Hybrid work applies here: a few days a week at Fernwood's Amsterdam office, full-time, reporting to the data platform lead. On-call rotates across three engineers and covers business hours only, with a lightweight escalation path so nobody is paged alone overnight, and pipeline uptime is the metric the role is measured against.

jobs.title: Analytics Engineer, Fleet Utilization
jobs.summary:
Fleet utilization numbers that operations managers check every morning depend on a chain of dbt transformations that has grown considerably since Fernwood's early days. This analytics engineer keeps that chain reliable as more fleets and vehicle types join the platform, working within the data platform team.

Much of the work is rebuilding older models that were written quickly to unblock a specific customer request and have since gone fragile, then adding tests so a bad upstream load gets caught before it reaches a dashboard. The role also covers documenting how core metrics like utilization rate and idle time are actually calculated, since three teams have historically landed on slightly different numbers depending on which query they copied years ago.

Required: solid SQL and dbt modeling experience, plus comfort with Snowflake as the underlying warehouse. Three to five years of analytics engineering work fits this seat. Comfort with real-world data that arrives late, duplicated, or out of order matters more than deep expertise in any single tool beyond dbt and SQL. Prior fleet exposure is not required, though some models do need to account for local regulatory differences in downtime reporting.

Full-time and fully remote across European time zones, with a few hours of daily overlap expected for team syncs and pairing sessions. The analytics engineer reports to the data platform lead and works closely with the data scientists who build forecasting models on top of these same tables, coordinating on schema changes before they land in production.

jobs.title: Machine Learning Engineer, Route Optimization
jobs.summary:
Route optimization sits at the center of what makes Fernwood's platform valuable to fleet operators: small improvements in how delivery and service routes are sequenced translate directly into fuel savings and fewer missed appointment windows. This engineer works on the models that generate those route suggestions.

The current system blends a classical optimization solver with a learned component that predicts realistic travel times from historical telemetry rather than static map data. Recent work has focused on improving accuracy in dense urban areas, where traffic patterns vary heavily by time of day, and on making the solver fast enough to re-optimize mid-day when a driver falls behind or a new stop appears. The role spans applied modeling and the engineering to package models so they run reliably in production without timing out under load.

Required: solid Python and PyTorch skills, working knowledge of MLOps practices, including Docker, for shipping models into a live service, and genuine familiarity with combinatorial optimization rather than supervised learning alone. Around three to five years of applied machine learning experience suits this role, though the team weighs a strong optimization background over an exact year count. Deep transportation-industry background is not required.

Async is the default across this team: full-time and remote, spanning several European countries with a couple of overlapping hours reserved each week for joint debugging. The team is small, three engineers plus one applied scientist, reporting to the engineering lead who owns the route-planning service.

jobs.title: Staff Data Scientist, Predictive Maintenance
jobs.summary:
Predictive maintenance exists to flag likely vehicle failures before one strands a driver on the road, and this staff data scientist sets the technical direction for how Fernwood's failure-risk models get built, validated, and trusted enough that fleet managers act on their warnings.

Recent work has included redesigning the model that predicts battery degradation in electric vans after early versions produced too many false alarms in winter months, and building a framework for judging whether a given warning would actually have prevented a breakdown in hindsight. Beyond hands-on modeling, this person mentors two mid-level data scientists, reviews methodology across the wider data science team, and pushes back when a customer request doesn't hold up statistically once examined closely.

Required: genuine comfort with survival analysis and time-to-event modeling, not just standard classification, plus strong SQL and Python. Eight or more years of applied data science experience is the seniority this seat is calibrated to, reflecting its role as the most senior individual contributor on the program. Formal management experience is not required, since mentoring here is informal rather than a direct-report relationship.

In-person time matters for this seat's reviews and mentoring, so the arrangement is hybrid from the Amsterdam office rather than fully remote, full-time. The data scientist reports to the data science director and sets technical calls for the predictive maintenance program without case-by-case sign-off.

jobs.title: Data Platform Engineer
jobs.summary:
Every product feature at Fernwood, from utilization dashboards to route optimization, depends on a shared data platform that has to serve very different workloads, from streaming telemetry to nightly batch reporting, without one starving another. This engineer owns pieces of that shared infrastructure.

The role covers the Snowflake warehouse, the orchestration layer that schedules hundreds of jobs each night, and the access controls that keep customer fleet data properly separated between accounts. A recurring part of the job is diagnosing why a particular job is slow or flaky, usually by digging through warehouse query plans or orchestration logs rather than writing new code from scratch. The engineer also helps onboard new data sources as Fernwood adds fleet operators in new countries, each with its own quirks in how vehicles report data.

Required: hands-on Snowflake and Airflow experience, solid SQL and Python, and enough background in access control or data governance to keep customer accounts properly separated. Three to five years of data platform or infrastructure work fits this seat. Deep expertise in fleet or automotive data specifically is not required; the platform concepts transfer from any domain with mixed streaming and batch workloads.

European time zones anchor this fully remote, full-time role. The platform team is small, so the engineer works independently on infrastructure problems with limited hand-holding, reporting to the data platform lead and coordinating closely with data engineers across the telemetry and analytics pods on shared schema changes.

jobs.title: Junior Data Analyst, Fleet Operations
jobs.summary:
Fleet operators get direct exposure through this entry-level analyst role, which sits with the customer analytics team rather than a purely internal reporting function detached from the businesses Fernwood actually serves day to day, from Amsterdam outward across its European fleet accounts.

The analyst builds recurring dashboards for two or three fleet operator accounts, helps prepare short summaries ahead of quarterly business reviews, and gradually takes on small ad hoc requests, like investigating why one region shows unusually high idle time, as confidence grows over the first several months. Senior analysts review all customer-facing output before it goes out, so there is structured support built into the workflow rather than being left to work things out alone.

Required: working SQL skills strong enough to write and modify queries independently, plus comfort building dashboards in Tableau or a similar tool. This is an entry-level seat: no prior experience with fleet or logistics data is required, though SQL comfort from coursework or an internship is expected on day one. Excel fluency helps for the quicker ad hoc requests that come up between the scheduled reviews.

Five days a week on-site at Fernwood's Amsterdam office is the expectation for this full-time, entry-level seat, working alongside the senior analysts who review its output before anything reaches a customer. The analyst reports to the customer analytics lead and joins the same quarterly review cycle as the rest of the team.

jobs.title: Lead MLOps Engineer
jobs.summary:
Several fleet-specific model deployment setups, each built independently over the past two years as customer pilots demanded quick turnaround, are being consolidated into one internal platform the whole applied science team can rely on. This lead role owns that migration end to end.

The engineer designs shared infrastructure for packaging, deploying, and monitoring models, sets standards for how model performance gets tracked in production, and coordinates a small rotating team pulled from different fleet-facing pods. Trade-offs between short-term customer deadlines and the longer migration timeline come up constantly, so navigating prioritization disagreements matters as much as systems design. A recent milestone cut deployment time for a route-optimization model from two weeks to under a day.

Required: solid Python, hands-on MLOps practice, and Kubernetes and Docker experience, with a real record of running distributed systems in production. This is a lead-level seat, evaluated on the scope of the migration run rather than a fixed year count, though prior experience standardizing infrastructure across teams with competing priorities is a strong plus. Deep applied-science modeling experience is not required; the science team owns that half of the work.

Amsterdam is home base for this hybrid, full-time role. Migration progress is tracked pod by pod on a shared board visible to the whole applied science team. This lead reports up through the head of ML infrastructure and pulls engineers from other pods on a rotating basis rather than owning a fixed headcount.

jobs.title: Data Science Manager, Mobility Insights
jobs.summary:
Six data scientists spread across telemetry, route optimization, and predictive maintenance report to this manager, whose job balances hands-on technical involvement with enough distance to let each scientist own their part of the roadmap and make their own calls day to day.

The manager runs weekly one-on-ones, reviews major analytical deliverables for methodological soundness before they inform a customer-facing feature, and works with account leads to staff upcoming projects against the team's specific skills and interests. A recent focus has been improving how the team documents modeling assumptions, after a disagreement with a fleet customer about a maintenance risk score took longer than it should have to resolve because the original reasoning wasn't written down.

Required: direct hands-on experience with mobility or telemetry data, including enough Python fluency to review analysis code personally, since the team looks to this person for technical judgment calls and not only scheduling and reviews. This is a manager-level seat evaluated on the scope of the team led, six scientists, growing by two more this year, rather than a specific year count. Deep statistics research background is useful but not required beyond what the role's technical reviews demand.

Enough in-person time for weekly one-on-ones and methodology reviews is the reason this full-time role stays hybrid out of the Amsterdam office rather than going fully remote. The manager reports to the director of data science and owns hiring decisions for the team's two open scientist seats this year, alongside the usual performance-cycle work.

jobs.title: Director of Data Science
jobs.summary:
Technical standards across all of Fernwood's data science pods run through this director, who also represents the practice directly in conversations with prospective enterprise fleet customers during the sales process, where credibility often determines whether a pilot gets approved.

The role involves reviewing proposed methodologies for new customer engagements before commitments are made, resolving disagreements between managers about how scarce data science time gets allocated across competing fleet accounts, and building a more formal career ladder for a team that has roughly tripled in size over two years without one. The director also sits on the extended leadership team that sets company-wide quarterly priorities, representing data science interests in planning conversations that aren't purely technical.

Required: a demonstrated record leading data science managers or senior practitioners, plus enough statistics depth and Python fluency to review methodology and code personally on live customer engagements. This is a director-level seat judged by the scope of the practice run, currently around a dozen scientists across several pods, rather than a specific year count. Producing new analysis personally on a regular basis is not required; the job is mostly evaluating other people's technical judgment rather than doing the analysis directly.

Amsterdam on-site, full-time, is the arrangement for this seat. This posting is limited to internal candidates, so familiarity with Fernwood's stack and customer base is assumed rather than something to learn on the job. The director reports to the VP of product and engineering and sets priorities for the data science pods directly.

jobs.title: Data Science Intern
jobs.summary:
Six months is the length of this internship, which pairs a student or recent graduate with a mentor on the predictive maintenance team for a realistic view of what applied analytics work looks like outside of coursework and closer to how a real fleet customer experiences the product.

Early weeks focus on getting comfortable with Fernwood's internal data stack and shadowing calls with fleet operators. After that, the intern takes ownership of a small, well-scoped analysis with regular check-ins from their mentor rather than being left to sink or swim. Past interns have contributed to churn analysis for smaller fleet accounts, cleanup of inconsistent maintenance-log data, and a prototype dashboard now used internally by the customer success team.

Required: working knowledge of Python, SQL, and basic statistics from coursework, since the internship assumes classroom-level familiarity rather than professional experience. No prior professional experience is required or expected; this seat exists specifically for students and recent graduates early in an analytics path. Prior exposure to fleet or logistics data is not expected, and the first few weeks are built around closing that gap.

Six months, on-site at Fernwood's Amsterdam office, is the shape of this full-time internship, paired with a dedicated mentor on the predictive maintenance team throughout the placement. The intern joins the same weekly team rhythms as full-time data scientists, minus the on-call responsibilities that come with the permanent role.

jobs.title: Product Analyst, Rider Experience
jobs.summary:
Thousands of drivers across Fernwood's customer fleets use the driver-facing mobile app every day, and this analyst supports the product team responsible for it, brought on under an initial six-month contract to add dedicated analytics capacity while the roadmap stays especially active.

Work includes tracking feature adoption after each app release, running lightweight in-app surveys with drivers, and turning findings into short write-ups the product manager can act on within a sprint or two rather than waiting for a quarterly report. Because the app is used across every fleet Fernwood serves, small usability problems tend to surface quickly through support tickets, giving the analyst a steady stream of specific questions to investigate rather than open-ended exploration.

Required: solid SQL for pulling and shaping usage data, plus some exposure to product analytics or A/B testing concepts, even from a coursework or internship setting. This is an entry-level contract role: prior professional product analytics experience is not required, though comfort moving fast without a senior analyst reviewing every query is expected. Excel is used for lighter-weight reporting alongside SQL.

Remote across European time zones, with a few overlapping hours for syncs with the product manager, is how this initial six-month contract runs day to day. The contract may convert to a permanent role depending on roadmap needs for the second half of the year, though that conversion isn't guaranteed at signing.

jobs.title: Senior Product Manager, Fleet Platform
jobs.summary:
Fernwood's customer-facing fleet management portal has grown well past its original scope over several years of incremental feature additions, and this role exists to bring coherence back to its roadmap after growth outpaced the original planning process.

The product manager interviews fleet operators about recurring pain points, many of which turn out to be workarounds for portal gaps rather than genuinely new feature requests, prioritizes a backlog managed somewhat informally until now, and works with a team of four engineers to ship improvements on a steady monthly cadence. Changes are validated with a handful of pilot customers before wider release, and a current initiative consolidates three overlapping reporting views that different customer segments requested independently.

Required: several years of product management experience with a B2B or platform product, strong SQL for digging into usage data directly, and comfort turning informal, scattered feedback into a structured, defensible roadmap. Five to eight years of product experience fits the seniority this seat is pitched at. Deep engineering background is not required, though enough technical fluency to work through trade-offs with engineers directly is expected.

Monthly release cadence sets the rhythm here: hybrid from Fernwood's Amsterdam office, full-time, working alongside a team of four engineers on shared priorities. The product manager reports to the VP of product and coordinates directly with account teams on pilot customer validation before anything ships broadly.

jobs.title: Product Operations Lead
jobs.summary:
Sprint planning, release notes, and communication with fleet account managers about upcoming platform changes all run through this product operations seat, rather than being handled ad hoc by whichever product manager happens to remember to send an update that week.

The person in this seat also maintains a lightweight intake process for feature requests from customer-facing staff, which currently arrive through an inconsistent mix of chat messages, spreadsheets, and hallway conversations that are easy to lose track of. The work spans product, engineering, and customer success teams working across different time zones, so a large part of the job is making sure the right people see the right update at the right time without everyone needing to ask.

Required: solid process-design skills and working fluency in Jira, plus the judgment to build a lightweight intake system rather than an overengineered one nobody actually uses. A background in program or project coordination, on the order of a few years, translates well into this seat, more so than prior product management experience itself. Deep technical or engineering background is not required.

Coordination across product, engineering, and customer success time zones is the whole point of this seat, so both schedule and location stay flexible: Amsterdam office access is available but not required, and hours shift to match whichever team needs coverage that day. This seat answers to the VP of product and acts as the connective layer between the three functions.

jobs.title: UX Researcher, Driver App
jobs.summary:
Drivers may be using Fernwood's mobile app quite differently than the check-in and route-acceptance flows were originally designed for, and this freelance researcher runs a study to find out exactly where that gap sits, engaged for an initial quarter of dedicated research time.

The engagement includes conducting roughly a dozen contextual interviews with drivers across two or three fleet customers, synthesizing findings into a report for the product manager, and presenting recommendations to the wider product team at the end of the engagement. Because drivers often interact with the app one-handed while parked briefly between stops, the research has to account for conditions very different from a typical office-based study.

Required: several years of hands-on user research experience, including interview and survey design and synthesis work delivered independently without a research team backing up the engagement. Three to five years of UX research experience fits this seat. Prior research into field or frontline worker apps used in vehicles or on the move is preferred over purely office-based consumer research, though not strictly required.

One quarter is the length of this freelance engagement, remote across European time zones with some overlap expected for interview scheduling and the final presentation to the product team. There is potential for follow-on freelance work depending on what the findings surface for the next planning cycle, though nothing beyond the quarter is committed upfront.

jobs.title: Senior Product Designer, Dispatch Console
jobs.summary:
Dispatchers at Fernwood's fleet customers spend entire shifts inside the dispatch console, assigning jobs, monitoring vehicle status, and reacting to delays, which makes this one of the more operationally demanding interfaces the design team owns today.

This designer leads a redesign of the console's job-assignment screen, assembled quickly under deadline pressure two years ago and since burdened with inconsistent patterns that make training new dispatchers harder than it needs to be. The work involves interviewing dispatchers about their workflow during live shifts, prototyping alternatives that cut the clicks needed for common actions, and running usability sessions with dispatchers from two pilot customers before anything rolls out more broadly.

Required: strong Figma and prototyping skills, real experience designing dense, information-heavy, real-time interfaces, and enough design-systems thinking to keep new patterns consistent as the console grows. Product designers land this seat with somewhere around five to eight years of experience behind them. A consumer mobile app background is not required; what matters is experience designing for operational, time-pressured users, wherever that experience comes from.

Fernwood's Amsterdam office hosts this hybrid, full-time role. Prototype testing happens with dispatchers still on an active shift where scheduling allows, since brief sessions between calls tend to surface more honest reactions than longer sessions booked well in advance. The designer reports to the design lead for the fleet platform product line.
