jobs.title: Senior Machine Learning Engineer, Crop Yield Models
jobs.summary:
Satellite imagery, soil sensor readings, and weather data combine at Loamwell into a season-long yield forecast that grain and row-crop farmers plan around every season, and this engineer works directly on the models sitting at the center of that forecast.

The current architecture blends a gradient-boosted baseline with a deep learning component trained on multi-spectral satellite imagery, and this role focuses on making the deep learning piece handle cloud cover and partial-field damage from hail or flooding more gracefully. Because the forecast directly influences decisions farmers make about grain contracts and storage, honest uncertainty estimates matter more than marginal gains on an offline benchmark. The engineer also helps incorporate new data sources as they arrive.

Required: strong Python and PyTorch skills, hands-on remote sensing or geospatial modeling experience, working MLOps practice for shipping model updates safely through a shadow season, and enough statistics background to reason about calibration and uncertainty rather than just accuracy. Five to eight years of applied machine learning experience is roughly the bar for this seat. Agronomy domain expertise is not required, since the research scientist team owns that side of the work.

Open to candidates anywhere in the United States, this full-time role is fully remote apart from quarterly in-person gatherings for the broader engineering team. Model changes go through a shadow season against the previous version before fully replacing it, so nothing reaches growers without a full season of comparison behind it.

jobs.title: Research Scientist, Remote Sensing
jobs.summary:
Raw satellite and aerial imagery becomes usable model features through the small research group this scientist joins, a less visible but foundational piece of how Loamwell's yield and crop-health forecasts actually get built each season across the company's grower regions.

Typical work includes evaluating new imagery providers as they become available, developing methods to detect early signs of crop stress from spectral signatures before it's visible during a field visit, and validating those methods against ground-truth data the agronomy team collects during the season. The team publishes internal findings on a biweekly cadence that inform which techniques the applied ML engineers eventually build into production features.

Required: solid Python skills, real experience with remote sensing or geospatial analysis, and enough experimentation design background to catch a flawed study before a season is lost to it. Three to five years of applied research experience fits this seat. A background in agronomy itself is not required; that domain knowledge sits with the agronomy team the role validates against. Candidates should be comfortable moving between hands-on analysis and code other engineers build on.

Fort Collins on-site time matters most around the growing season, when coordination with the agronomy team peaks, and this full-time role runs hybrid rather than fully remote for that reason. The scientist reports to the head of remote sensing research and works on a biweekly publishing rhythm with the rest of the group.

jobs.title: Principal Data Scientist, Agronomic Modeling
jobs.summary:
As the most senior individual contributor on the science side, this person sets technical direction for how Loamwell models the agronomy behind its recommendations, deciding where deeper research actually changes what the company tells farmers to do.

Recent work has involved rebuilding the nitrogen recommendation model after several agronomists flagged poor performance on fields with unusual soil composition, requiring a first-principles rework of how the model represented soil chemistry rather than simply retraining on more data. The role carries no formal management responsibility but does involve mentoring several scientists and engineers informally, reviewing methodology across the research team, and occasionally explaining a recommendation directly to a skeptical grower.

Required: deep domain knowledge in agronomy or soil science, not just machine learning technique, plus strong Python and causal inference skills for work that has to hold up against a farmer's own field experience. Eight or more years of applied experience is the bar this seat is set to, reflecting its role as the senior-most technical voice on the science side. Formal people-management experience is not required.

Fort Collins hosts this role on-site, full-time, given how often in-person collaboration with the agronomy team drives the work day to day. This role sits under the VP of data and AI and sets technical direction for agronomic modeling without carrying a direct-report team, though input flows both ways with the applied engineers who build on this research.

jobs.title: Data Platform Engineer, Sensor Networks
jobs.summary:
Loamwell's soil moisture and weather sensor network has grown from a handful of pilot fields to several thousand devices scattered across farms with spotty rural connectivity, and this engineer owns the infrastructure that gets readings from those devices into a usable warehouse despite the gaps.

Building resilient ingestion pipelines is the core of the job: handling devices that go offline for days at a time and catch up once connectivity returns, rather than simply dropping missed readings, and working with the hardware team to understand new sensor types before they ship at scale. Timestamp handling and deduplication need real care, since farms sit in different time zones and report on their own local schedule.

Required: production Kafka experience, strong SQL and Python, working familiarity with MLOps practices since these pipelines feed the models Loamwell's science team trains on sensor data, and a real record with distributed systems handling unreliable or intermittent connections, such as IoT deployments in remote areas. This seat is built around five to eight years of data platform or infrastructure experience. Agricultural domain knowledge is not required; the connectivity problem is the same one field-deployed IoT systems face anywhere, whether the sensors sit on a farm or a factory floor.

Remote work is open to candidates anywhere in the United States for this full-time role, with no fixed office to report into. The engineer works closely with the hardware team on new sensor rollouts and reports to the data platform lead, owning monitoring and alerting directly rather than sharing it across a rotation.

jobs.title: Data Scientist, Field Trial Analysis
jobs.summary:
Dozens of field trials run each growing season to test whether a new recommendation, on seed variety, fertilizer timing, or irrigation scheduling, actually improves outcomes against a grower's usual practice, and this data scientist designs and analyzes them.

The work means close collaboration with the agronomy team that manages the physical plots and the growers who host them on their own land. Because a field trial can't simply be rerun if something goes wrong partway through a season, careful upfront design and monitoring for issues like uneven irrigation or treatment mix-ups matter enormously. The role also builds reusable statistical tooling so smaller trials don't need a dedicated analyst from scratch each time a question comes up mid-season.

Required: strong experimentation design and causal inference skills, solid Python and SQL, and the communication range to explain a result to a grower in plain terms as well as to a scientist in technical ones. Three to five years of applied statistics or data science experience fits this seat. Agricultural or environmental field-experiment experience is preferred but not required; a lab-only research background is workable here.

Growing-season travel to trial sites supplements this hybrid, full-time role based out of Fort Collins rather than fully remote. Every trial design gets a second set of eyes from another scientist before it goes into the ground. The data scientist reports to the head of agronomic research and coordinates directly with the growers hosting each trial.

jobs.title: Staff Machine Learning Engineer, Irrigation Systems
jobs.summary:
Water is the single most constrained input for many of Loamwell's grower customers, particularly in drought-affected regions, and the irrigation optimization product exists to help growers use less water while protecting yield. This staff engineer anchors its technical direction.

Current work centers on a shared modeling framework that several regional irrigation models can plug into, instead of each being built from scratch with different assumptions. The engineer spends real time reading current agronomic and hydrology literature as well as reviewing pull requests from junior teammates extending the framework to new crop types. A recent milestone shipped an irrigation scheduling recommendation for almond orchards, unlike the row crops the framework was built around.

Required: strong Python and PyTorch skills, real experience with optimization algorithms beyond standard supervised learning, working MLOps discipline for keeping a shared framework other models plug into stable in production, and enough hydrology or agronomic literacy to read the relevant research directly. This seat is pegged at eight or more years of applied machine learning experience. Formal management experience is not required, though reviewing other engineers' work is a regular part of the job.

Global and remote, full-time, is how this role is structured, given the asynchronous, research-heavy nature of the work, with travel to grower sites a few times a year during the growing season. The engineer reports to the VP of data and AI and sets technical direction for the irrigation product without a fixed direct-report team.

jobs.title: Research Engineer, Crop Disease Detection
jobs.summary:
Fungal disease often shows on drone imagery before it's visible on the ground, and Loamwell's current rules-based detection system struggles to catch it outside a narrow set of well-documented conditions. This four-month contract is scoped to evaluate whether newer computer vision models can do better.

Work includes benchmarking candidate models against a labeled dataset built from several seasons of confirmed disease outbreaks, running field validation against a small set of pilot farms during the current growing season, and writing up comparative findings for the science team to decide whether to invest further. Because outbreaks can spread quickly once detected late, false negatives are weighted much more heavily than false positives when judging any candidate approach. The scope is narrow and well-defined rather than open-ended research.

Required: strong Python and PyTorch skills, hands-on computer vision experience including model evaluation beyond a single accuracy number, and strong written communication since findings will be read by agronomists as well as engineers. Three to five years of applied computer vision experience fits this seat. Deep agronomy background is not required; the science team supplies the disease-outbreak labels and context.

Four months, remote, open to candidates anywhere in the United States, is the frame for this contract, structured around the current growing season's pilot farms. The engagement has a fixed, narrow scope rather than an open-ended research mandate, reporting progress to the science team on a set benchmarking timeline.

jobs.title: Machine Learning Engineering Manager
jobs.summary:
Five engineers report to this manager, whose team takes Loamwell's research models, spanning yield forecasting, disease detection, and irrigation, from validated prototypes into features that run reliably during a live growing season when farmers are depending on them.

Beyond the usual rhythm of one-on-ones and performance conversations, the role involves negotiating scope with the research team, who sometimes underestimate what it takes to productionize a promising result, and prioritizing work against a calendar that doesn't forgive slipped deadlines the way a typical software launch might, since a missed planting-season deadline effectively means waiting a full year. A recent priority has been shrinking the gap between a validated research model and a farmer-facing feature.

Required: hands-on machine learning engineering experience, including Python and MLOps practice, alongside people-management skills, since the team looks to this person for technical judgment on production issues rather than only process. This is a manager-level seat evaluated on the scope of the team led, five engineers, growing by two more before the next season, rather than a specific year count. Deep research-scientist modeling experience is not required; that stays with the research team.

Full-time and based on-site in Fort Collins, close to the engineers this role manages day to day. The manager owns the postmortem process for any production incident touching a farmer-facing recommendation, since those write-ups have become the main way the team accumulates knowledge across growing seasons. Hiring two additional engineers before the next season is a meaningful part of this year's mandate.

jobs.title: VP of Data and AI
jobs.summary:
Reporting to the CEO, this executive owns the overall technical strategy for Loamwell's science and engineering organization, including which sensor investments, imagery providers, and modeling approaches the company standardizes on for the next several growing seasons.

Grower cooperatives and agricultural retailers expect regular, direct engagement from this executive, since technical credibility matters as much as the roadmap itself and these customers often bring their own agronomists who press hard on methodology. The executive also balances long-term research investment against the shorter commercial timelines the sales team pushes for, and chairs the annual planning session where the science and commercial teams jointly decide the next season's technical bets.

Required: significant executive-level experience inside a company with a genuine seasonal cadence rather than a continuous release cycle, a clear point of view on MLOps standards since this seat decides how modeling approaches get built and deployed company-wide, plus enough agronomy fluency to hold your own against a grower's own technical staff. This is an executive-level seat judged by the scope of the organization run, spanning science and engineering, rather than a specific year count. Experience at a larger, more bureaucratic organization is not required and often doesn't transfer; what matters is comfort with a business that only gets one shot per year.

Based on-site in Fort Collins, full-time, and reporting directly to the CEO. This posting is limited to internal candidates, so deep familiarity with Loamwell's technical stack, team structure, and grower relationships is assumed rather than something to build from scratch. Travel to a small number of agricultural technology conferences each year rounds out the role's external-facing side.

jobs.title: Junior Machine Learning Engineer
jobs.summary:
Loamwell Agritech turns field-sensor data into yield forecasts and other agronomic models, and this junior role sits on the applied machine learning team that keeps those models running through each growing season. The team supports several model families rather than one, so a new engineer gets broader exposure than a single-project role would give.

Early work is deliberately scoped: writing and testing data preprocessing code, fixing small bugs in existing pipelines, and getting pull requests reviewed by a senior engineer mentor before submitting your own. As familiarity builds over the first few months, that scope grows into an actual feature added to the yield forecasting pipeline, with the mentor reviewing design choices rather than every line. A structured first month pairs technical ramp-up with a short visit to a partner farm, giving the training data a physical referent.

Required: working Python and enough PyTorch experience to read and modify an existing model rather than build one from a blank file, plus SQL to pull training data out of Loamwell's warehouses without help. This is an entry-level seat — zero to two years, counting internships and coursework projects, is enough seniority to start. A machine learning degree is not required; strong fundamentals demonstrated through projects, rather than a transcript, count the same.

Reporting runs directly to a senior engineer mentor rather than a rotating set of leads, which is deliberate for a first machine learning role. The arrangement is full-time and fully remote within the United States, with the team anchored in Fort Collins for the first month of onboarding and periodic in-person weeks afterward.

jobs.title: Technical Product Manager, Farm Data Platform
jobs.summary:
Growers using Loamwell want their field data flowing into the accounting and equipment-telemetry tools they already run, and this technical product manager owns the data platform and API layer that makes those integrations possible. The role sits close to engineering rather than to the grower-facing product teams.

Regular roadmap reviews with engineering leads anchor this job, alongside gathering integration requirements from growers and the third-party vendors who build on Loamwell's API and making the prioritization call when a large partner's request competes with platform-health work. A recent project rebuilt the field-boundary API after partners reported inconsistent results depending on how a field's shape had been drawn, which meant rethinking how the geospatial data was stored rather than patching the symptom.

Required: API design experience good enough to defend design choices in front of partner engineers, stakeholder management sharp enough to say no to a large partner without damaging the relationship, and SQL for querying platform usage directly. This seat expects five to eight years in a technical product role, real product strategy instincts, and at least some time spent on a platform or API product. Deep geospatial systems expertise is not required — the team already has that.

A public API changelog is part of the job, maintained on a steady cadence, since partner engineering teams have said silent changes erode trust faster than any single bug. The seat is hybrid out of Fort Collins, with in-office days concentrated around the engineering team's planning cycle rather than fixed to the same days every week, reporting to the VP of product and working daily alongside the engineering lead for the platform team.

jobs.title: Product Manager, Grower Tools
jobs.summary:
Growers logging field observations through Loamwell's mobile app are the focus of this six-month contract, which exists to simplify what they see and report back to their agronomist. The engagement sits with the grower tools team rather than the broader platform organization.

Auditing existing usage data comes first, to find where growers abandon a task partway through, followed by prioritizing a short list of fixes with a small engineering team and coordinating a beta program with a handful of pilot farms before wider release ahead of next season. Because growers often use the app outdoors in bright sunlight or with gloves on, the usability constraints here are physical and environmental rather than typical mobile product concerns.

Required: comfort reading product analytics well enough to find a drop-off point without a data analyst's help, mobile UX judgment suited to outdoor and gloved use, and clear stakeholder communication since findings get shared weekly with agronomists who are not product people. Three to five years in product roles, at least one of them on a mobile product, fits this seat. Experience with agriculture specifically is not required; field-service or frontline-worker mobile products count just as well.

Defined end dates suit someone looking for a contract with a clear deliverable, which is what this well-bounded piece of work offers rather than ongoing roadmap ownership. It runs remote across the United States for the six-month term, with a possible extension if the beta program runs long, reporting to the grower tools lead alongside a small dedicated engineering team rather than one pulling resources from other projects.

jobs.title: UX Researcher, Grower Mobile App
jobs.summary:
Adoption of Loamwell's grower mobile app plateaus a few weeks after a farm signs up, a pattern the product team keeps seeing in usage data without ever having investigated it directly with the growers themselves. This freelance engagement exists to close that gap.

The researcher designs and runs a mix of on-farm interviews and short diary studies with growers who fit the plateau pattern, ideally observing real fieldwork rather than only a follow-up call, then presents synthesized findings the product team can act on before the next release. Because participants are often in rural areas with unpredictable schedules tied to weather, flexible and sometimes short-notice scheduling is a real requirement rather than a nice-to-have.

Required: experience running user interviews and usability testing in field conditions rather than only a lab or remote-call setting, plus research synthesis skills strong enough to turn a handful of visits into concrete screen-level recommendations, not a general report on grower attitudes. Five to eight years of research experience is the level this engagement is set at, with prior work in agricultural or other physically demanding field contexts weighted heavily. Deep statistical analysis is not required.

Findings come back as concrete recommendations tied to specific screens, with consented video clips from sessions included alongside the write-up. The engagement is flexible and freelance, running roughly eight weeks with a possible extension into the following season, scheduled around growers' availability rather than a fixed calendar, and reporting findings directly to the product team rather than through a research operations layer.

jobs.title: Design Systems Lead, Grower Products
jobs.summary:
Three different teams built Loamwell's grower-facing products — a mobile app, a web dashboard, and an internal agronomist tool — at different times, and it shows: components, terminology, and even how a basic action like confirming a field boundary gets handled all vary by surface. This lead role exists to fix that without stalling any of the three roadmaps.

Defining a shared design system across all three surfaces comes first, then migrating the highest-traffic screens and setting up lightweight governance so new features stay consistent without slowing down a design team of only three people. Adoption is tracked screen by screen rather than declared complete all at once, since a big-bang migration across three products with different release schedules would likely stall everything.

Required: fluency in Figma and design tokens sufficient to build a system other designers actually adopt, working knowledge of WCAG accessibility standards, and interaction design judgment that holds up for a grower using the app one-handed in a field as well as an agronomist on a desktop monitor. This is a lead-level seat defined by scope rather than a years figure: you should have introduced a design system into an organization that did not previously have one. Experience with agricultural products specifically is not required.

Component documentation leans on real usage examples pulled from shipped screens rather than idealized mockups, since designers elsewhere say the abstract version alone rarely answers their question. The role is hybrid out of Fort Collins, reporting to the head of design, and makes the case internally for continued investment once migration is complete, since design-systems work competes directly with the feature roadmap.

jobs.title: Junior Product Designer, Grower Mobile App
jobs.summary:
Design students rarely get to see how a screen holds up outdoors on an actual farm rather than only in a conference room, and this twelve-week summer internship on the grower mobile app team builds that in from week one under the mentorship of a senior designer. The program centers on one scoped project rather than a rotation across several teams.

Over the course of the internship, you take on a scoped project such as redesigning a single field-logging screen, present work in progress during weekly design critiques, and incorporate feedback into higher-fidelity prototypes tested with a couple of local pilot growers if scheduling allows. Every prototype gets tested with someone outside the design team before it is called finished, mentor included, and past interns have gone on to contribute directly to shipped features by the end of their term.

Required: working fluency in Figma for both design and prototyping, and a portfolio showing coursework or personal projects even without professional experience. This is an entry-level, onsite internship — no prior design job is expected, and visual design ability matters more here than a resume. Familiarity with agriculture or outdoor products is not required; the mentorship structure is built to teach that context on the job.

The internship closes with a short presentation to the wider product team, walking through what changed between the first sketch and the shipped version. It runs onsite in Fort Collins for the full twelve weeks, working alongside the grower mobile app design team five days a week, reporting to a senior designer who reviews work daily, with weekly critiques open to the wider design group.

jobs.title: Analytics Engineer, Learning Platform
jobs.summary:
Every quiz attempt, video pause, and assignment submission on Chalkline's learning platform generates an event, and this analytics engineer turns that raw stream into the modeled tables curriculum and product teams actually use to understand how students engage with a course.

Many of the existing dbt models were built quickly during an earlier growth push and have started to show their age, particularly around how partially completed assignments get counted, which has left two teams reporting different completion rates for the same course. The role untangles that specific discrepancy and documents metric definitions clearly enough that a curriculum designer without a data background can follow what a number represents.

Required: solid SQL and dbt for building and testing models, and enough Snowflake experience to work efficiently against a warehouse this size. Around three years of hands-on analytics engineering, including some exposure to messy behavioral event data, fits this role well; a data warehousing background from any industry works, and deep prior EdTech experience is not required. Since Chalkline serves both individual learners and school districts with different usage patterns, some models need separate logic to avoid misleading comparisons.

New models go through a short peer review before merging, mainly to catch the kind of subtle counting mistake that caused the completion-rate discrepancy in the first place. The role is hybrid out of London, with in-office days set around team planning rather than fixed daily attendance, sitting within the data platform team and working closely with the curriculum and product stakeholders who consume the finished models.

jobs.title: Data Analyst, Student Engagement
jobs.summary:
Curriculum designers at Chalkline need a clear, recurring read on where students stall out inside a course, and this analyst turns course-level engagement data into a monthly report that flags exactly which lessons cause the most drop-off for the wider team.

Ad hoc data requests from curriculum designers fill out the rest of the role, varying widely in scope — from a quick lookup of how many students used a particular feature to a deeper look at whether a redesigned unit actually improved completion rates. Requests typically arrive through a shared queue rather than a hallway conversation, so setting realistic turnaround expectations is part of the job. Structured mentorship from a senior analyst runs through the first three months to build fluency with Chalkline's internal data warehouse.

Required: solid SQL for querying the data warehouse directly, Excel for the reporting side, and enough data visualization sense to make a monthly report legible to a non-technical curriculum team. Zero to two years of analytics experience is the right level here, and prior EdTech experience specifically is not required — general SQL fluency from any analyst role transfers fine. Comfort presenting a finding out loud to a room of curriculum designers matters as much as producing the number in the first place.

A good starting point for someone aiming toward a more analytical role inside an education-focused product organization, this seat runs onsite in London, full-time, with the desk sitting inside the curriculum team's space rather than a separate data function, reporting to a senior analyst who runs the first three months of structured mentorship directly.

jobs.title: Senior Data Engineer, Content Pipeline
jobs.summary:
Course content on Chalkline's platform — videos, quizzes, reading passages, interactive exercises — moves through a publishing pipeline that has to track versioning, translations, and accessibility metadata across thousands of lessons, and this engineer keeps that pipeline fast and reliable as the library keeps growing.

Recent priorities have focused on cutting the time between an editor publishing a change and that change appearing for students, which had stretched to several hours during peak periods before this quarter's optimization work began. The role works closely with the platform engineering team and the curriculum team's own tooling, which depends on the pipeline being predictable rather than something to work around. Content exists in multiple languages and reading levels that must stay synchronized when a lesson changes.

Required: strong Python and SQL, real experience with distributed systems and ETL pipelines at a scale where a naive approach falls over, and data modeling skills that hold up across multiple languages and reading levels at once. Expect to bring five to eight years of data engineering experience, with at least some of it on content or publishing systems specifically. Deep expertise in Chalkline's particular tech stack is not required — the team will get you there; the scale experience is what transfers.

Publish-to-live latency is tracked as a headline metric and reviewed monthly with curriculum, since a slow pipeline directly limits how fast a fix reaches students. The role is fully remote within the United Kingdom, full-time, with the team distributed across the country and syncing through scheduled calls rather than shared office hours, reporting to the platform engineering manager.

jobs.title: Product Manager, Course Authoring
jobs.summary:
Parental leave has opened up a nine-month contract owning the roadmap for the internal authoring tool Chalkline's curriculum designers use to build and update courses, right as the team pushes hard for changes to how interactive exercises get created.

Curriculum designers' requirements, often expressed in pedagogical rather than technical terms, get translated into specifications engineering can build against, with a phased rollout coordinated so existing course content isn't disrupted mid-update for enrolled students. A specific near-term goal is cutting the number of steps it takes to add a new interactive exercise type, which currently requires an engineering ticket rather than something a curriculum designer can configure directly.

Required: comfort running a roadmap in Jira, gathering requirements from non-technical stakeholders without losing precision in translation, and stakeholder management skills good enough to manage a phased rollout without disrupting live courses. Three to five years in product management, ideally with some exposure to internal tools or authoring systems, fits this seat. Deep pedagogical expertise is not required — that lives with the curriculum designers; the job is translating it, not replacing it.

Weekly check-ins with a rotating group of curriculum designers keep the roadmap grounded in daily friction rather than the loudest requests in a shared inbox, and a short usability pass with two or three designers precedes any workflow change. The contract is hybrid out of London for nine months, covering a parental leave period with a documented handover expected at the end, reporting to the group product manager for the learning platform.

jobs.title: Senior Product Manager, Assessments
jobs.summary:
Quizzes generated and graded by Chalkline's assessment engine serve both individual learners studying independently and school districts running gradebook reporting off the same tool, and this manager guides its roadmap as those two use cases keep pulling in different directions.

Much of the work involves talking directly to teachers at partner districts who have built unexpectedly specific grading workflows around the tool, then working out which requests reflect genuine gaps versus edge cases not worth solving for the broader product. The role also partners with support to reduce a recurring category of confusion around how partial credit gets calculated for multi-part questions, which generates a disproportionate share of tickets relative to actual usage.

Required: stakeholder management strong enough to keep district requests from derailing the roadmap, customer discovery skills for real requirements in those workflows, product strategy judgment on what to generalize versus decline, and SQL to check grading data directly. Five to eight years of product management experience, with rules-heavy or assessment-adjacent products a strong plus, is the level this role targets. K-12 experience specifically is not required if that background is strong.

Proposed grading rule changes go through review with a small panel of teachers before release, and the team keeps a separate changelog of grading logic changes, since districts have asked for a clear audit trail when a parent disputes a grade. The seat is hybrid out of London, with in-office time concentrated around district-facing planning sessions, reporting to the group product manager for the learning platform.

jobs.title: Group Product Manager, Learning Platform
jobs.summary:
Four product managers cover different areas of Chalkline's core learning platform, and this group product manager keeps their roadmaps coherent as a whole, quarter after quarter, rather than a set of disconnected initiatives sharing only an engineering org.

Quarterly planning across the group is the anchor of the job, alongside resolving prioritization conflicts when two teams want the same engineering resources at the same time and representing product in leadership planning meetings where school-district sales commitments sometimes create pressure to reprioritize on short notice. A current focus is untangling technical dependencies between the assessment team and the content authoring team, which have historically planned in isolation despite sharing a substantial amount of underlying data.

Required: experience managing other product managers, not just doing individual contributor product work, plus roadmapping and stakeholder management skills strong enough to run cross-team quarterly planning. This is a manager-level seat defined by scope — four direct reports across a shared platform — rather than a years figure. Comfort with institutional buyers, not just end users, matters; deep assessment-domain expertise specifically is not required going in.

A monthly retrospective across the group exists specifically to catch dependency conflicts before they turn into a scheduling crisis two sprints later. The seat is onsite in London, full-time, with the whole group working from the same office to support the weekly cross-team coordination the role depends on, reporting to the director of product management.

jobs.title: Director of Product Management
jobs.summary:
Chalkline's product organisation has grown well past what informal processes can support, and this director owns strategy across the full platform while sitting on the extended leadership team that sets company-wide priorities each quarter, from headcount to market focus.

Cross-group prioritization conflicts that group product managers cannot settle on their own land here, alongside representing product in board-level reporting and building out a more structured product operations function as the team has grown. Decisions include how much of the roadmap should serve individual learners versus the growing school-district segment, which pulls the org in genuinely different directions.

Required: a demonstrated track record leading product organisations through multiple group product managers, strategy work at a company rather than single-team level, and stakeholder management skilled enough to hold its own in board-level reporting. This is a director-level seat defined by organisational scope rather than a years figure — you should already have run product strategy for a multi-team org. Deep prior EdTech experience is useful but not required if the organisational leadership track record is strong.

Direct conversations with large district customers during contract renewals are part of the job too, not just internal leadership settings. The seat is onsite in London, full-time, working from the same office as the leadership team, reporting to the VP of product and sitting on the extended leadership team for quarterly company-wide planning.

jobs.title: Associate Product Manager
jobs.summary:
New product managers at Chalkline start here: a structured entry point pairing each associate with a senior product manager mentor for their first year, rather than dropping someone into ownership of a roadmap on day one. The seat sits inside the assessment product group specifically, not a rotating pool spanning the wider platform.

Responsibilities start small — writing up findings from teacher interviews, maintaining a backlog for a narrow slice of the assessment product — before growing into owning a small feature area under supervision as confidence and context build over the first several months. The associate also rotates through a short stint on the support team to build genuine empathy for how teachers and students experience the product day to day, which tends to surface issues that never show up in a roadmap review.

Required: basic SQL for looking at product data directly, comfort with Jira for backlog work, and customer discovery instincts sharp enough to get something useful out of a teacher interview. Zero to two years of experience fits this seat, and prior formal product management experience is not required — a demonstrated interest in education or product work through internships, tutoring, or side projects counts for more here. Jira tickets should be written clearly enough for another person to pick up without a follow-up question.

Weekly one-on-ones with the mentor cover both the specific backlog work and the broader question of how a product decision actually gets made, plus occasional in-person weeks that bring the wider associate cohort together. Day to day the role is fully remote within the United Kingdom, full-time, reporting to the senior product manager assigned as mentor for the first year.

jobs.title: Program Manager, District Rollouts
jobs.summary:
New school districts joining Chalkline bring a genuinely operational challenge — data migration from a district's previous system, staff training scheduled around the school calendar, coordination across sales, support, and engineering teams that don't naturally talk to each other — and this program manager owns that rollout process end to end.

A checklist of rollout dependencies, grown organically over several years and due a proper overhaul, gets tracked here, alongside troubleshooting issues as they surface — a data import failing on unusual legacy formatting, a training session needing to move around exam week — and reporting rollout health to leadership in a way that flags risk early rather than after a launch date has already slipped.

Required: process design skills strong enough to rebuild an ageing rollout checklist from scratch, stakeholder communication across sales, support, and engineering, and reporting discipline that surfaces risk early. This is a lead-level seat defined by scope — full ownership of every district rollout — rather than a years figure, though genuine comfort working with school administrators juggling many other priorities is essential. Prior K-12 experience specifically is not required if the cross-functional program management background is solid.

A short post-launch check-in with each district, roughly a month after go-live, has become the main way the team catches quieter problems, like a training gap, before they turn into a renewal risk. The role is fully remote within the United Kingdom, full-time, working alongside sales, support, and engineering colleagues who are themselves spread across the country, and reports to the director of product management.

jobs.title: Staff Product Manager, Accessibility Compliance
jobs.summary:
Public procurement contracts often carry specific accessibility requirements, and several of Chalkline's district contracts are no exception — this staff product manager owns making sure the platform actually meets those obligations rather than treating accessibility as a checklist completed once and forgotten.

Existing features get audited against relevant accessibility standards first, with individual product teams brought in to fix gaps without derailing their own roadmaps, and a lightweight review process built so new features get checked before launch instead of after a customer complaint. A recent project reworked how the assessment engine handles screen readers for visually impaired students taking a timed quiz, which meant rethinking timing behavior rather than a simple markup fix.

Required: real depth in WCAG accessibility standards, product strategy skills for building a review process other teams will actually follow, and stakeholder management strong enough to influence teams without direct authority over their sprints. Eight or more years of product experience, with a meaningful chunk of it in accessibility or a regulated context, is the level this staff role is set at. Deep expertise in every product surface is not required — this role leans on influence and audit process more than hands-on feature design.

A quarterly audit against district contract requirements keeps the team honest about where gaps remain, with the resulting list prioritized jointly with whichever team owns the affected feature, and a short accessibility training session for new engineers runs during onboarding. The role is fully remote within the United Kingdom, full-time, reporting to the director of product management.

jobs.title: Principal Product Manager, Learning Strategy
jobs.summary:
Strategic bets about Chalkline's future — expand further into adaptive, personalized learning paths, or keep investing primarily in the existing linear course model — run through this principal-level role, which carries no direct reports but real influence over overall product direction.

Curriculum research, competitive analysis, and district customer feedback get synthesized into a small number of well-argued strategic recommendations for leadership each quarter, rather than owning any single team's day-to-day roadmap. Execution stays with group product managers, though this person needs to stay close enough to classroom usage data to keep recommendations grounded rather than theoretical. A recent contribution proposed piloting adaptive difficulty in one subject area before committing to a platform-wide investment.

Required: market analysis and product strategy skills sharp enough to produce recommendations leadership actually acts on, plus stakeholder management across a leadership team without formal authority over any of them. Eight or more years of product experience, with a track record of shaping strategy at a company level rather than a single team's roadmap, is the level this principal seat is set at. Deep learning-science credentials are not required, though genuine interest in the field is expected.

Quarterly strategy memos circulate to the whole leadership team ahead of the planning meeting, so debate can focus on substance rather than the framing being seen for the first time in the room, and this person is expected to be explicit about which parts of a proposal rest on solid evidence versus a reasonable bet worth testing. The role is hybrid out of London, full-time, reporting to the VP of product.

jobs.title: Senior Product Designer, Classroom Tools
jobs.summary:
Teachers at Chalkline's partner schools have said plainly, in more than one survey this year, that the teacher-facing classroom dashboard looks dated next to the rest of the product, and this six-month contract exists to lead its redesign from the ground up.

Existing dashboard usage gets audited against what teachers say they actually need day to day, which usually turns out to be a much shorter list than the current dashboard tries to serve, followed by prototyping a simplified alternative in Figma and running usability sessions with teachers at a handful of partner schools before anything ships broadly. Feedback from those sessions feeds directly into the next prototype round rather than waiting for one big review.

Required: strong Figma and prototyping skills, design systems fluency good enough to work inside Chalkline's existing component library rather than build parallel patterns, and interaction design judgment suited to professional, task-focused users under real time pressure. Five to eight years of product design experience, ideally including a dashboard or data-dense redesign, fits this contract. Experience designing specifically for education is not required if that track record is strong.

Because dashboard changes affect how teachers plan their week, the rollout is gradual and closely watched, with the designer expected to help interpret early feedback rather than handing that work off once designs are finalized. The contract runs fully remote within the United Kingdom for six months, with usability sessions requiring occasional travel to partner schools, reporting to the design manager for product design.

jobs.title: UX Researcher, Educator Feedback
jobs.summary:
Teachers configuring and troubleshooting Chalkline's classroom and grading tools generate a steady stream of friction the design team needs visibility into, and this part-time role — roughly three days a week — supports that with ongoing research through a typical school term.

Regular usability sessions on features still in development make up part of the work, alongside maintaining a repository of past research findings so teams stop rediscovering the same insights every time a new designer joins the classroom tools group. The reduced schedule suits someone balancing other commitments — consulting work or a teaching background they still maintain — who wants meaningful ongoing involvement in product decisions without a full-time commitment.

Required: solid user interview and usability testing skills applied specifically to teacher and classroom-tool contexts, research synthesis strong enough to maintain a findings repository other designers actually use, and working survey design ability. Three to five years of UX research experience, ideally with some in-house time in an education or teacher-facing product, is the level this role targets. A background limited to agency work is not disqualifying, though in-house experience is preferred.

Survey data from the educator advisory panel, which meets each semester, gets folded into the same research rhythm. The role runs remote within the United Kingdom, roughly three days a week on a part-time schedule that follows the school term rather than a fixed calendar, reporting to the design manager for product design.

jobs.title: Design Manager, Product Design
jobs.summary:
Five product designers spread across Chalkline's different platform areas report into this design manager, whose job balances hands-on critique with enough distance to let each designer own their own work rather than second-guessing every decision made along the way.

Beyond regular one-on-ones, the role partners with the design systems function to keep new feature designs consistent across the classroom, assessment, and authoring surfaces, and negotiates design resourcing when two product teams need support in the same sprint cycle. A recent challenge involved rebuilding trust with the assessment product team after a rushed design handoff caused avoidable rework late in a release, which prompted a broader look at how design and product timelines get coordinated earlier in a project.

Required: real coaching ability, not just design critique, plus enough Figma and design systems fluency to review work credibly across five designers' output. This is a manager-level seat defined by scope — five direct reports across three product surfaces — rather than a years figure, though prior experience managing designers, not just doing individual design work, is essential. Hands-on design-tokens or tooling work is not required, since that partnership sits with the design systems lead.

Design critique here runs on the wider team's shared schedule rather than a private cadence, with in-office days in London aligned to that rhythm under a hybrid arrangement. This manager reports to the director of product management and coordinates closely with the design systems lead, carrying real weight in how design resourcing gets allocated across the group.

jobs.title: Content Designer, Course Experience
jobs.summary:
In-product copy across Chalkline's platform — quiz instructions, progress-tracking notifications — has been written inconsistently by whichever engineer or curriculum designer happened to build a given feature, and this content designer exists to bring order to that without slowing shipping down.

Tone and clarity issues in existing copy across the platform get audited first, then folded into a lightweight style guide the design and engineering teams will actually follow rather than a document that gets ignored after launch, alongside reviewing copy for upcoming releases before they reach students and teachers. A specific near-term project rewrites the language shown when a student fails an assessment, which current data suggests discourages some students from retrying rather than encouraging them.

Required: strong UX writing and content strategy skills, working Figma fluency to embed copy directly into design files, and the judgment to build and maintain a style guide that survives contact with a real release calendar. Three to five years of content design experience, with some of it writing for young or student audiences rather than purely enterprise or marketing copy, fits this role. Deep curriculum or pedagogy expertise is not required — that partnership comes from the curriculum team.

Draft copy gets tested informally with a handful of students where feasible, since phrasing that reads as clear to an adult reviewer doesn't always land the same way with an eleven-year-old working through a hard assignment. The role sits under a flexible work model out of London, full-time, reporting to the design manager for product design.

jobs.title: Data Scientist, Marketplace Matching
jobs.summary:
Meridian Loop connects homeowners with independent electricians, plumbers, and other skilled tradespeople, and this data scientist supports the team responsible for matching a homeowner's job posting with the right set of available professionals nearby.

Small ranking changes here tend to have outsized effects on both how quickly a job gets booked and how satisfied a tradesperson is with the leads they receive, which makes the tuning work more delicate than it looks. The role designs experiments to test changes to the matching algorithm, builds models predicting which professionals are likely to respond quickly to a given job type, and presents results in a way non-technical marketplace stakeholders can act on within a sprint rather than waiting for a quarterly review.

Required: strong Python and SQL, real A/B testing experience end to end, and enough statistics and causal inference background to separate a genuine effect from noise on a two-sided marketplace. Three to five years of applied data science experience, with some exposure to marketplace or two-sided platform dynamics, is the level this role targets. Deep expertise in the home services industry specifically is not required if the marketplace experimentation background is solid.

Matching changes ship to a small percentage of traffic first, and the scientist is expected to define upfront what result would justify a full rollout rather than deciding after seeing which way the numbers moved. The role is fully remote within Canada, full-time, syncing with the marketplace team through scheduled calls, and reports to the head of data science.

jobs.title: Analytics Engineer, Marketplace Metrics
jobs.summary:
Ad hoc SQL queries against Meridian's raw production tables have multiplied as the marketplace has grown, and this role exists to replace that pattern with well-modeled, tested dbt datasets the whole analyst team can rely on. The backlog of queries worth turning into models has been growing faster than anyone has had time to address.

A backlog of high-traffic queries gets worked through to identify which deserve to become proper models, built with appropriate tests and documented clearly for the growing analyst team spread across marketplace, trust and safety, and finance. Production data changes frequently as the marketplace evolves, particularly as new service categories get added beyond the original electrician and plumber focus, so keeping models resilient to schema changes is an ongoing concern.

Required: solid dbt and SQL for building and testing models, and enough Snowflake experience to work efficiently against a warehouse serving several analyst teams at once. Around three years of analytics engineering experience, with comfort working directly against messy, evolving production data, fits this role better than deep dbt expertise alone. Prior marketplace experience is useful but not required — the data modeling discipline transfers from most domains.

A short model-review step catches most of the breakage before it reaches a dashboard someone else depends on. The role is hybrid at the Toronto office, a few days a week for team planning, full-time, reporting to the head of data and staying closely connected to the analyst teams that rely on these models day to day.

jobs.title: Senior Data Scientist, Pricing Strategy
jobs.summary:
Two-sided pricing is a genuinely hard problem — changes that help professionals earn more can hurt homeowner conversion and vice versa — and this senior scientist owns the analytical work behind Meridian Loop's pricing recommendations to both sides of the platform.

Recent work built a model suggesting a competitive quote range to professionals bidding on a job, then evaluated, after the fact, whether professionals who followed the suggestion actually won more work without leaving money on the table compared to those who priced independently. The role reports into the pricing product manager and works closely with engineering to get models into production without the multi-week delays that have historically slowed pricing experiments.

Required: strong Python, statistics, and causal inference for evaluating pricing changes rigorously, plus SQL and enough pricing-model experience to build a recommendation professionals will actually trust. Five to eight years of applied data science experience, with pricing, auctions, or other two-sided marketplace dynamics specifically represented, is the level this role targets. Deep home-services domain knowledge is not required if that pricing and experimentation background is strong.

The team reviews every shipped pricing change a month out to check whether it held up outside the initial experiment window, since dynamics can shift once professionals adjust their own behavior. The scientist also presents trade-offs clearly to skeptical, income-dependent professionals rather than a bare headline number. The role is hybrid at the Toronto office, full-time, alongside the pricing product manager.

jobs.title: Product Manager, Booking Experience
jobs.summary:
Homeowners posting a job on Meridian Loop pass through the core job-posting and booking flow the moment they decide they need an electrician or plumber, making it one of the highest-traffic and most closely watched parts of the entire product, and this manager owns it.

Regular interviews with homeowners who abandoned a booking partway through anchor the work, alongside reviewing session recordings to spot friction surveys alone wouldn't surface and making prioritization calls that weigh both the homeowner experience and the quality of information professionals receive about a job. A current initiative focuses on cutting the number of steps needed to post a job with enough detail that a professional can quote confidently without a follow-up call.

Required: SQL sufficient to review booking funnel data directly, customer discovery skills for running homeowner interviews that surface real friction rather than surface complaints, and stakeholder management strong enough to balance homeowner and professional interests that don't always align. Three to five years of product management experience, ideally including a lead-generation or on-demand marketplace product, is the level this role targets. Deep tradesperson-side experience is not required if those marketplace instincts are solid.

Every change to the booking form gets tested against a small holdout group first, since a field that looks like harmless extra detail to the team can quietly become the exact step where a homeowner gives up. The role is onsite at the Toronto headquarters, full-time, staying close to the engineering team shipping these changes weekly, and reports to the head of product for the marketplace.

jobs.title: Senior Product Manager, Provider Success
jobs.summary:
Churn among Meridian Loop's high-volume electricians and plumbers has risen over the past two quarters, and the board now treats provider retention as a company priority. The senior product manager in this seat leads the response, working with the provider success team that owns the relationship with the platform's busiest tradespeople.

You will find out why professionals leave — lead quality, payout speed, or a competitor paying better — and turn that into a roadmap mixing quick wins with the structural fixes underneath them. Changes are piloted on a subset of accounts before they reach everyone; a pilot on faster payouts for top-rated professionals is at that stage now. Cohort retention curves go to the executive team monthly, and you present them with a view on what moved, including the experiments that failed.

Required: roadmapping and product strategy on a two-sided marketplace, customer discovery you run yourself rather than commission, and the stakeholder management to hold an executive audience through a quarter with no clean win. Five to eight years in product management, with real time spent on retention, is the level the work assumes. You do not need a background in the trades — the provider success team supplies that context.

Fully remote across North America, with the product organization anchored in Toronto and core hours on Eastern time. Two engineers, a designer and an analyst sit with you on the retention pod; provider success is a separate and larger team. Your reporting line is the VP of Product, who reviews the roadmap quarterly and leaves the sequencing inside it to you.

jobs.title: Product Analyst, Marketplace Growth
jobs.summary:
Meridian Loop's growth team runs a four-month push on professional onboarding this quarter, and this contract analyst supports it. The funnel starts at sign-up and ends when a tradesperson completes their first job on the platform — several steps, several systems, and no single dashboard covering the whole of it today.

Building and maintaining that dashboard is the core of the engagement, alongside flagging conversion drops worth the product manager's attention and pulling ad hoc numbers for planning meetings on a day's notice. The other half of the job is documentation: writing down how each funnel metric is actually defined, so the next analyst does not spend their first two weeks reverse-engineering old queries the way you will spend yours.

Required: SQL you can write without a reference open, enough product analytics vocabulary to tell a real conversion drop from a reporting artifact, and Excel for the requests that never justify a dashboard. One to three years of analytics work is the range this contract is aimed at, and a first role plus solid coursework counts. No familiarity with the home-services market is expected.

Four months, fixed end date, tied to this initiative rather than rolling into something open-ended. Fully remote within Canada; the growth team keeps core hours on Eastern time and gathers in Toronto once a quarter, which you are welcome at but not required to attend. Onboarding is short given the length of the contract, so expect to be working fairly independently by the second week. The growth product manager is your point of contact.

jobs.title: Lead Product Manager, Core Marketplace
jobs.summary:
Search, matching, booking and payment each belong to a different product manager, and each of the three has their own roadmap and their own local optimum. The lead in this role sits above all of them and is accountable for whether those roadmaps add up to one coherent homeowner experience or three good products pointing in different directions.

Most of the week goes to cross-team planning, arbitrating shared engineering capacity, and writing down decisions that were previously understood differently by each team. The rest is hands-on: a ranking redesign for search results recently stalled for weeks between two teams holding reasonable, incompatible positions, and unsticking that kind of problem cannot be delegated. You are measured on the three managers' output and on the cross-cutting problems no single team naturally owns.

Required: product strategy at the level of a whole marketplace rather than one surface, roadmapping across teams whose plans have to interlock, and the stakeholder management to keep three managers aligned when you do not own their performance reviews. Scope defines this seat more than any year count — you should have led product managers before, formally or otherwise, and mediated between teams with genuinely opposed incentives. Direct line-management experience is not something the role requires.

Hybrid out of the Toronto office, three days on site with the rest of the week wherever you work best; the planning sessions this job depends on are deliberately scheduled on the in-office days. Full-time. Your reporting line runs to the VP of Product, and you sit on the product leadership group that sets quarterly priorities across the marketplace.

jobs.title: Director of Product Operations
jobs.summary:
Headcount in Meridian Loop's product organization roughly doubled last year with no matching investment in how that organization runs itself. This director builds the product operations function that closes the gap, starting from the spreadsheet-based planning the company outgrew several quarters ago.

First order of business is a roadmap planning process that survives contact with a dozen teams, then a standard way for those teams to report progress upward so leadership stops receiving twelve different formats. After that comes hiring and running a small operations team to keep it all going. Much of the work is facilitation: getting product, engineering and go-to-market leaders into one quarterly plan they each actually signed up to.

Required: process design you have taken from blank page to adopted practice, reporting that leaders read rather than skim, and the stakeholder management to push back on a VP without turning it into a standoff. Leadership here is judged by scope — you should have owned an operations function or an equivalent company-wide program. Since the posting is internal, familiarity with the current product organization and its standing tension between homeowner-facing and provider-facing priorities is assumed rather than learned.

On site at the Toronto office five days a week; the job runs on hallway access to the people whose process you are changing. Full-time, open to internal candidates only. The VP of Product is your reporting line, with a standing channel to the CEO for anything touching company-wide planning, and you will hire two operations managers during the first year.

jobs.title: VP of Product
jobs.summary:
Growth in electrical and plumbing work has flattened in Meridian Loop's mature markets, which turns the question of what the marketplace covers next into an executive decision rather than a roadmap item. The VP of Product owns that call, along with product strategy across every group in the organization.

Quarterly priorities across all product groups are set here. So is the defence of marketplace liquidity in board meetings, where how the number is measured gets as much scrutiny as the number itself, and the decision about which adjacent home-service categories the company enters and in what order. Alongside that sits a succession problem: the current layer of managers no longer covers the organization's surface area, and building the next one is part of the job.

Required: product strategy at company scale, leadership of leaders rather than of teams, and the stakeholder management that board and executive rooms demand. Marketplace experience at executive level is the bar, ideally somewhere with a skilled-trades or field-services supply side. Because the posting is open to internal candidates only, existing knowledge of Meridian Loop's liquidity dynamics and competitive position is assumed. Hands-on experience in the trades themselves has never been part of this role.

Five days a week in the Toronto office, with regular travel to the regional markets where category expansion gets tested first. Full-time, internal candidates only. The CEO is your reporting line and you sit on the executive team, with four product groups and the product operations function underneath you. You also chair the quarterly review where liquidity, retention and expansion bets are weighed against each other rather than championed separately.

jobs.title: Product Management Intern
jobs.summary:
Four months on the homeowner booking experience team, paired with a mentor who does this job full-time. The team owns everything between a homeowner deciding they need an electrician and a job being posted that a professional can quote against. Interns here get real scope rather than a research project shelved at the end of the term.

Expect to run a small number of homeowner interviews with your mentor sitting in, help keep the team's backlog in order, and own one narrowly scoped improvement end to end — a copy change to the job-posting form, for instance — from definition through launch and the check on whether it did anything. Pulling your own numbers is part of it rather than something you queue with an analyst. Nobody expects polished interview technique by week two; each session is debriefed with you.

Required: enough SQL to answer a question about your own feature without help, an interest in customer discovery you can show from coursework or a side project, and some exposure to how a roadmap gets built. This is an entry-level position — no professional product experience is expected, and a prior internship in product, human-computer interaction or a related field is a bonus rather than a filter.

Four months, with scheduling flexibility around coursework: roughly full-time hours through the core weeks and a lighter arrangement negotiable around exams. Work from the Toronto office or from anywhere in Canada, whichever suits the week, though most interns come in for the Tuesday critique. A senior product manager on the booking team mentors you directly.

jobs.title: Technical Product Manager, Trust and Safety
jobs.summary:
Payments and identity verification sit underneath every job booked on Meridian Loop, so the trust and safety group ships more slowly than the rest of the product organization and does so deliberately. The technical product manager here owns fraud protections and the identity checks a professional passes before taking work.

The work is translation in both directions: regulatory and risk requirements into specifications engineers can build, and engineering constraints back into something the compliance team can sign. Overcorrecting is its own failure mode — a check strict enough to stop fraud also turns away legitimate tradespeople, which is why the monthly review tracks fraud attempts and false positives side by side. A recent project opened a faster verification path for professionals with a track record elsewhere, coordinated across engineering, a third-party vendor and legal.

Required: API design fluency sufficient to specify an integration with a verification vendor and argue about its edge cases, roadmapping under compliance constraints, and the stakeholder management to hold a line with legal and engineering at once. Five to eight years in product management, at least two of them in payments, fraud, identity or another area a regulator watches. A legal qualification is not needed; the compliance team has one.

Fully remote across North America, with the group overlapping Eastern hours for a daily standup. Full-time. Incident response belongs to this role rather than interrupting it, and the group rotates a weekday escalation contact. The director of trust and safety is your reporting line, and you work alongside a compliance lead and five engineers.

jobs.title: Senior UX Researcher, Provider Insights
jobs.summary:
Before the provider success team commits engineering time to fixing churn, it wants to know which segments of tradespeople are actually leaving and why. This ten-week freelance engagement answers that with evidence rather than the assumptions currently standing in for it.

Designing and running a mixed-methods study is the whole of the work: phone and video interviews with professionals who have already left, plus a survey across the active provider base to see how far the interview findings generalize. What you deliver is a set of findings a product team can act on — segments, causes, and what would plausibly change each one — not a descriptive report. Those findings feed a roadmap presented to executives, so the synthesis has to hold up under questions from people who were not in the room.

Required: user interviews with people who have no particular reason to be generous about the product, survey design producing a sample worth trusting, and research synthesis that ends in a recommendation. Usability testing experience is useful for the follow-on work. Senior range, roughly five to eight years running studies end to end, and prior churn or retention research with a supply-side or gig-economy population counts for a great deal. Domain knowledge of the trades is not expected.

Ten weeks, freelance, fully remote across North America. Scheduling bends around tradespeople's working days, which means interviews land early morning and evening more often than not, and the engagement is scoped with that in mind. Study design is reviewed with the principal researcher in Toronto; the rest of the calendar is yours to run.

jobs.title: Product Designer, Booking Flow
jobs.summary:
Eight months, one initiative: the job-posting flow homeowners use to describe what they need has collected extra steps across several years of unrelated changes, and this contract designer redesigns it. A product manager and two engineers are dedicated to the same project.

Start with an audit of the current flow against drop-off data, because the steps that feel worst are not always the ones homeowners abandon. Then prototype something shorter that still captures enough detail for a professional to quote without a phone call, and test it with real homeowners before any of it ships. Rollout is staged and watched closely — booking volume is the number the company runs on — and you stay through that rollout to help read the results rather than handing off at the design review.

Required: Figma as a working tool rather than a deliverable format, prototyping fast enough to test three versions in a week, interaction design judgment about where a form can lose a field safely, and usability testing you moderate yourself. Three to five years designing product, with at least one checkout, booking or comparable conversion flow behind you. A background in home services is not needed.

The engineers on this project sit together at the Toronto office and the designer sits with them, on site, five days. Eight-month contract with defined scope and no expectation of conversion to a permanent role. Standard working days. Craft review comes from the design manager for the homeowner side, while the product manager on the project sets priorities day to day.

jobs.title: Principal UX Researcher, Marketplace Trust
jobs.summary:
Trust runs through nearly every part of Meridian Loop's product — a homeowner deciding to let an unfamiliar tradesperson into their house, a professional deciding a homeowner will pay on time — and it looks different everywhere it surfaces. The principal researcher sets the research agenda across both sides of the marketplace.

Much of the job is deciding what not to study: which questions are uncertain enough that research will change a roadmap decision, and which already have enough evidence behind them to act. You mentor three researchers, take the highest-stakes questions yourself — how verification badges affect booking conversion, for one — and push back when a team wants to skip research on a decision that is genuinely open. A lightweight framework you would inherit already helps teams size how much research a decision warrants.

Required: research strategy as a practice rather than a long list of completed studies, user interviews and synthesis at a standard the rest of the team can copy, and the leadership to hold a position against a product director. Eight or more years in research, several of them spent setting direction instead of executing someone else's plan. No single methodology specialty is required — breadth across qualitative and quantitative work matters more here.

Hybrid from Toronto, two fixed days on site with the research team and the rest flexible. Full-time. Three researchers report to you, and you hold a seat on the product leadership team's monthly planning review — there to surface trust risks before a commitment is made, not to approve every decision.

jobs.title: Junior Product Designer, Provider Tools
jobs.summary:
Provider tools is the side of Meridian Loop that tradespeople use between jobs: the dashboard where work arrives, quotes go out and payment status lives. This junior designer supports that team on smaller pieces of it and grows into owning larger ones. The design team is four people, so work reaches you early rather than after three rounds of review elsewhere.

Early work is concrete — design variations for A/B tests on the professional dashboard, keeping components consistent as small features land, and producing screens a developer can build from without a meeting. Shadowing interviews with professionals is part of it too, taking notes at first, because the fastest way to understand this product is watching an electrician use it in a van between calls.

Required: Figma at a working level, prototyping good enough to show an interaction rather than describe it, and visual design fundamentals a portfolio can demonstrate — hierarchy, spacing, restraint. One to three years, and at this level a strong portfolio outweighs the year count. Design-systems experience is not expected, nor is running your own research; both are things this team teaches.

Flexible arrangement: some weeks mostly at the Toronto office, some mostly remote from anywhere in Canada, settled with the team rather than by policy. Critique runs Thursday and is the one session people come in for. Full-time. A senior designer on provider tools reviews your work weekly, and the design manager handles everything else.

jobs.title: Data Analyst, Clinical Operations
jobs.summary:
Outpatient clinics across several European countries run their scheduling and care coordination on Solstice's software, and the clinical operations team turns what that produces into something a clinic manager can act on. This six-month contract analyst does that work. Appointment utilization and no-show rates are the two numbers most of it hangs off.

Recurring dashboards tracking utilization and no-shows across partner clinics are yours to build, along with the investigation when a clinic manager flags a spike — a sudden run of cancellations at one location, say, which has turned out to mean four different things in the past year. Documentation is part of the job: clinics use slightly different scheduling conventions, and the definition of a no-show needs to live somewhere other than inside a query.

Required: SQL for everything that repeats, Excel for the requests that do not, and data visualization judgment about when a chart is clearer than a table. Data governance carries more weight here than in most analyst roles, since patient scheduling data sits behind access controls you work within rather than around. Three to five years in analytics. Healthcare operational data experience helps; a clinical background does not.

Six months initially, with extension likely if the reporting program continues. Fully remote across Europe, with the clinical operations team keeping Berlin hours. Reports are walked through with clinic managers rather than emailed, so a few hours each week go to calls where someone asks what a rising number actually means. Any breakdown below clinic level needs a governance check first, which occasionally slows an analysis down.

jobs.title: Analytics Engineer, Patient Data Platform
jobs.summary:
Modeled datasets behind Solstice's internal reporting are what this part-time analytics engineer maintains: platform usage across the clinics the company serves, scoped deliberately to stay clear of directly identifiable patient health information. That boundary and the regulation behind it shape how the work gets done.

You own a small number of dbt models feeding internal dashboards, and you adjust them when the scheduling system changes its data structure, which happens with roughly every release. Beyond that, the clinical operations and product teams request custom cuts of usage data often enough to fill the remaining hours.
