Any model put to a new reporting purpose goes through review with the data governance lead first — not a formality, and it has caught things.

Required: dbt in production, SQL past the point where window functions are still interesting, and data modeling judgment about what belongs in a shared layer. Working knowledge of data governance under European data protection rules is part of the job rather than a nice-to-have. Three to five years in analytics engineering. Orchestration is owned by the platform team, so Airflow experience is not something this role needs.

Twenty hours a week, arranged as four short days or two and a half long ones — the team has both and does not mind which. Fully remote across Europe with the data team in Berlin; one shared call a week and asynchronous otherwise. This is a stable ongoing part-time seat rather than a stopgap, suited to someone who wants depth in one domain alongside other work. The data governance lead reviews what you build.

jobs.title: Product Manager, Care Coordination Tools
jobs.summary:
Referrals between a patient's primary doctor and a specialist used to travel by fax and phone call. Solstice's care coordination tool replaced that for the clinics on the platform, and this product manager owns where it goes next as adoption spreads to new partner clinics — each of which arrives with a slightly different idea of how a referral should be tracked.

The people worth listening to are care coordinators, who work in this tool all day and hold strong, well-informed and frequently conflicting opinions about referral status. You turn that into a roadmap a small engineering team can execute, carrying the responsibility that comes with it: a referral that quietly stalls has consequences for a patient, so changes are piloted at one clinic before going anywhere else. Automatic reminders for referrals gone quiet for a week shipped on exactly that path.

Required: roadmapping for a team of four to six engineers, stakeholder management across clinics that each want their own workflow honored, and enough SQL to check an adoption question yourself instead of queueing it with an analyst. Three to five years in product management. Healthcare workflow or care coordination software is directly relevant experience; a clinical background is not required, and most of the team does not have one.

Hybrid from Berlin, two days a week on site, with the engineering team in the same building and clinic visits a few times a quarter. Full-time. The head of clinical products is your reporting line, and pilot decisions are made jointly with the clinical safety reviewer assigned to the tool.

jobs.title: Senior Product Manager, Clinician Platform
jobs.summary:
Doctors and nurses open Solstice's clinician platform dozens of times a shift to review histories, document visits and manage their day. Its original design assumed one clinician working in one location, an assumption that has not survived the company moving upmarket into multi-site clinic groups. Correcting that is what this role exists for.

Interviewing clinicians about their real workflow is harder to arrange than it sounds — a doctor's spare time arrives in ten-minute pieces — and what comes out of it has to be prioritized against a mid-size engineering team's capacity. The standing tension is between large clinic groups with procurement leverage and small independent practices on the same platform, and it does not resolve itself. Recent work cut the clicks needed to document a routine follow-up, something clinicians had raised repeatedly.

Required: product strategy for a platform serving two quite different customer sizes, roadmapping under a fixed engineering budget, and stakeholder management with clinicians who will tell you plainly when a design is wrong. Healthcare compliance is a working constraint — you should be able to read a clinical safety review and answer it rather than route it onward. Five to eight years in product, ideally on clinical workflow software or another regulated professional tool. Clinical training is not expected.

Hybrid from Berlin, three days on site, partly by design: every proposed interface change is reviewed jointly by product and the clinical safety team before it reaches engineering, and those sessions happen in person. Full-time. The head of clinical products is your reporting line, and you work with a designer, a researcher and eight engineers.

jobs.title: Program Manager, Clinical Rollouts
jobs.summary:
Bringing a new clinic onto Solstice means migrating its existing scheduling data, training staff around shifts that are already full, and working through an IT contact who is juggling four other vendors. This program manager owns that process for every mid-size clinic group the company signs, and the rollouts have grown more intricate as those groups have grown larger.

In practice the work is dependency tracking and troubleshooting: a legacy scheduling export arrives in a format nobody has seen, a training session collides with a clinic's busiest week, a group's IT contact goes quiet for eight days. You keep the rollout moving and report its health upward so risk surfaces early rather than at the point it becomes a slipped date. Every rollout closes with a short retrospective that feeds the checklist used for the next one.

Required: process design that holds up when a clinic deviates from it, reporting that gives leadership a real read on rollout health, project coordination across several rollouts at once, and stakeholder communication with people who did not choose to be part of a software project. Three to five years running programs or implementations. No methodology certification is expected; patience with healthcare operational reality matters more, since a delay means staff quietly reverting to paper.

Fully remote across Europe with the rollout team anchored in Berlin, plus travel to clinic sites roughly one week in four during an active go-live. Full-time, on a schedule that occasionally starts early to catch a clinic before its first appointments. The director of customer operations is your reporting line, with a dotted line into clinical products for anything that turns out to be a product problem rather than a rollout one.

jobs.title: Senior Product Designer, Patient App
jobs.summary:
Patients book appointments, message their care team and read visit summaries in Solstice's patient app, and this freelance engagement covers its visual and interaction redesign. Discovery is already finished — the research team has interviewed patients across several age groups, and the findings are waiting.

Scope runs from concept exploration through high-fidelity prototypes ready for engineering handoff. The constraint shaping everything is the patient population the partner clinics serve: older people, people managing a chronic condition, people who use very few apps and are opening this one while worried. Each major screen gets a plain-language pass before usability testing, because confusing wording and a confusing layout compound each other for someone in that state.

Required: Figma at a senior standard, design systems experience since this app has one and the redesign has to extend it rather than fork it, interaction design for flows with real consequences, and working WCAG knowledge — accessibility review is a gate here, not a final check. Five to eight years designing consumer-facing products. Healthcare experience is welcome but not a requirement; several people on this team came from outside it.

Three to four months freelance, with a likely follow-on phase covering the messaging feature. Fully remote across Europe, overlapping Berlin hours for the twice-weekly design review. Expect to present rationale to the internal product team and, once or twice, to a clinic's patient advisory group — a design that convinces designers can still land badly with the people who use it under stress. Reviews come from the design manager for patient experience.

jobs.title: UX Researcher, Clinician Workflows
jobs.summary:
How a documentation tool behaves during a real shift and how it behaves in a mockup reviewed at three in the afternoon are two different things. The researcher on the clinician platform team studies the first: doctors and nurses using Solstice's scheduling and documentation tools while they are actually seeing patients.

A typical study means shadowing clinicians through a morning at a partner clinic, running usability tests on an upcoming documentation feature during a scheduled training slot, and turning what you saw into recommendations the product team can weigh against engineering cost. Recruiting is the hard part — clinicians cannot be pulled away from patient care casually, so sessions are arranged with clinic administrators weeks ahead rather than through a panel.

Required: user interviews and usability testing with professionals rather than consumers, contextual inquiry since much of what matters here is only visible on site, and research synthesis that ends somewhere actionable. Three to five years in research. Prior work on clinical or other professional software counts for more than fluency with any particular research platform. Running quantitative studies alone is not asked of this role; the analytics team partners on those.

Hybrid from Berlin, two days on site plus clinic visits that land wherever a study does. Full-time. Readouts circulate in writing before the team meeting so discussion is about what to do rather than what was found. You work closely with the accessibility specialist, since clinicians under time pressure and clinicians with visual or motor constraints run into overlapping problems. The principal researcher is your manager.

jobs.title: Junior UX Researcher, Patient Experience
jobs.summary:
Sitting in on patient interviews is where this role starts. The patient experience team studies how people book appointments, receive reminders and message their care team through Solstice's app and portal, and this entry-level researcher supports the senior researchers doing that work. The team is small enough that support turns into ownership quickly.

Early responsibilities are note-taking and session logistics, which sound administrative and are not: participants are often describing a health concern alongside their experience of the software, and handling that well is most of the skill. Over the first months you move into moderating simpler sessions on your own. Patient-facing work arrives far sooner than it would at a larger healthcare organization, always with a supervising researcher present.

Required: interview technique you can demonstrate from coursework, a research project or an internship; exposure to usability testing; and enough research synthesis practice to turn six sessions into something other than a transcript. One to three years, and a relevant degree or a coursework portfolio is accepted in place of professional experience. Healthcare exposure of any kind is a genuine plus. Statistics beyond the basics is not required.

Berlin office, five days a week, which is deliberate at this level — the learning happens in the debrief after a session rather than over a call. Full-time. Every session is followed by a short debrief with your supervising researcher, part technique review and part checking how you are doing after a difficult conversation. The senior researcher on patient experience is your reporting line.

jobs.title: Interaction Designer, Care Navigation
jobs.summary:
Care navigation takes a patient from describing a symptom to booking the right kind of appointment, and it is the most interaction-heavy part of Solstice's patient app. This lead designer owns how that flow behaves in detail: transitions, error states, and the order the questions come in.

Work here sits between interaction design and content strategy, because the wording of a question and the point at which it gets asked matter as much as anything visual. One recent redesign cut abandonment by replacing a clinically phrased question, which patients did not know how to answer, with a plain-language alternative developed alongside the clinical safety team. Changes reach a small pilot group of clinics first, with abandonment and question-skip rates watched before anything goes wider.

Required: interaction design fundamentals strong enough to defend a transition choice, Figma and prototyping at the fidelity a flow like this has to be tested at, and content strategy — you write the questions rather than briefing someone else to. Ownership of the flow defines this lead seat more than a year count, though nobody arrives here early. Clinical knowledge is not required; the safety team reviews every significant change with you.

Hybrid from Berlin, two to three days on site depending on where a review cycle sits. Full-time. Anything substantial passes through both the design and clinical safety teams before shipping, which adds about a week and has been worth it. The design manager for patient experience is your reporting line, and you work with one researcher and three engineers.

jobs.title: Design Systems Lead, Clinical Interfaces
jobs.summary:
Confirming a medication change looks one way on one Solstice screen and another way three screens later, because different teams built them at different times. For clinicians moving quickly, that inconsistency is cognitive load with a safety edge. This lead is hired to remove it, giving clinical interfaces their own system distinct from the patient app's.

Defining that system comes first, then migrating the highest-traffic clinician screens onto it and setting up governance so new features stay consistent without adding a week to every design review. Part of the specification is explicit: how a critical action — a prescription change, a referral update — is visually distinguished from a routine one. A small clinical advisory panel reviews the riskiest patterns before they enter the library, and has already caught two ambiguous icons.

Required: a design system you have built and shipped rather than contributed to, design tokens plus the discipline to keep them meaningful as a library grows, Figma library architecture other designers can work in without breaking, and enough healthcare compliance literacy to know which patterns carry regulatory weight. Lead level by scope. Component implementation belongs to the platform team, so shipping the front-end code yourself is not part of this.

Fully remote across Europe, with the design organization centered in Berlin and one week a quarter on site for the system review. Full-time. Nobody reports to you, yet the standard you set governs the whole design team, which makes persuasion most of the job. The design director reviews your work, and clinical safety signs off on high-risk patterns.

jobs.title: Accessibility Specialist, Health Products
jobs.summary:
Solstice's partner clinics serve a patient population that skews older and includes many people managing conditions affecting vision, motor control or concentration. Accessibility is therefore a product requirement rather than a review at the end of a project, and this principal specialist is the person who holds that line across the whole portfolio.

Auditing the patient app and the clinician tools against the standards is continuous work, as is helping product and design teams close gaps without wrecking their timelines. The rest is training, so accessibility gets raised during initial design instead of caught late. A recent project reworked how the patient app announces appointment confirmations to screen readers, which had been reading information out in an order that made no sense without the layout in front of you.

Required: deep WCAG expertise, including the parts that get argued about rather than only the checklist; usability testing with people who use assistive technology instead of simulations of them; and design systems knowledge, since durable fixes live in components rather than screens. Eight or more years in accessibility work. Stakeholder management matters as much as technical depth — this role can block a ship on accessibility grounds but holds no authority over any product team. A development background is not required.

On site in Berlin, five days, because auditing an interface next to the designer who built it works and a ticket does not. Full-time. Progress shows up as a shrinking backlog of open issues and, increasingly, as feedback gathered directly from patients who use assistive technology. The design director is your reporting line, and you hold a standing slot in every product team's design review.

jobs.title: Design Manager, Patient Experience
jobs.summary:
Five designers work across the patient app, the clinician tools and the shared design system, and this manager holds that group together — close enough to critique the work honestly, far enough back that each designer genuinely owns their area. It is a people job with enough craft left in it to keep a designer interested.

Beyond one-on-ones and career conversations, much of the week goes to negotiating design staffing with product leadership when the patient app and the clinician platform both need help in the same sprint. Clinician work tends to carry harder deadlines, which can quietly starve the patient side, so the split gets reviewed every sprint rather than when someone complains. You step in personally when a decision carries clinical safety weight.

Required: leadership of a design team around this size, coaching that has visibly moved someone's craft rather than only their confidence, Figma fluency sufficient to critique at file level, and working familiarity with healthcare compliance and how it constrains a design. Management experience on a regulated or safety-conscious product is preferred, though it need not have been healthcare. Personal design output is not what this role is measured on.

Critique, staffing conversations and the harder one-on-ones all happen in person, which is why this seat is on site in Berlin five days a week. Full-time. Five designers report to you, and you sit in the design leadership group alongside the systems lead and the accessibility specialist. The design director is your own manager.

jobs.title: Director of Design
jobs.summary:
Design strategy and quality standards across every Solstice product, patient-facing and clinician-facing alike, sit with this director. The remit reaches past the design organization: which clinic segments and care models the company prioritizes is partly a design and research question, and the executive team treats it as one.

Highest-stakes initiatives get reviewed at their milestones rather than continuously, the lead and principal designers across the organization get mentored, and design gets represented directly in procurement conversations with large clinic groups, who now ask detailed questions about accessibility and clinical safety before signing. You also chair the quarterly review where design, legal and clinical safety jointly decide which open risks are acceptable to ship with and which are not.

Required: design strategy at organization scale, leadership of leads and principals rather than of individual designers, and healthcare compliance fluency deep enough to hold your own in a procurement review. Director-level experience inside a healthcare or otherwise safety-critical product organization counts for more than breadth across unrelated industries. Because the posting is open to internal candidates only, familiarity with the existing design organization, the clinical safety review process and current customer relationships is assumed.

Fully remote across Europe, with the design organization based in Berlin and roughly one week a month on site for reviews and executive sessions. Full-time, internal candidates only. Four leads and one principal report to you, and the chief product officer is your reporting line. Procurement conversations occasionally require travel to a customer's site.

jobs.title: UX Research Intern
jobs.summary:
Healthcare research carries obligations most internships never touch: consent that has to be genuinely informed, recruitment that cannot lean on convenience, and participants who are sometimes unwell. Five months on Solstice's research team is an introduction to that as much as to method. Studies here run with both clinicians and patients.

Supporting those studies means scheduling participants and taking notes during clinician and patient interviews, always with a supervising researcher in the room. Smaller independent pieces follow as you settle in — analyzing responses to a patient feedback survey, drafting a section of a readout — each closely reviewed. Participant recruitment is where you will learn the most, because who ends up in a study determines what that study can honestly claim.

Required: coursework or a project that involved talking to people systematically, some grounding in survey design, and the care participant recruitment in a health context demands. This is an internship — no professional experience is expected. Psychology, human factors, design or a related field of study helps, and a stated interest in healthcare specifically is weighed favorably given the subject matter. Statistical modeling is not part of the role.

Five months, with hours arranged around coursework: consistent weekly hours through the core period rather than a fixed daily schedule. Work from the Berlin office or remotely from within Europe, though interview days are usually on site with the team. You are paired with a researcher who supervises every session you take part in and debriefs each one with you.

jobs.title: Staff Product Designer, Clinical Dashboards
jobs.summary:
Solstice Health Systems builds the clinical dashboards where a clinician or clinic administrator reviews patient panels, upcoming appointments and outstanding referrals at a glance, and this staff designer sits with the product team that owns those screens, holding the line as every team asks to add one more useful data point.

The work means giving senior design judgment across two or three dashboard initiatives at once, stepping in when a redesign has stalled because clinical stakeholders want conflicting information prioritized, and coaching newer designers to push back on scope creep from well-meaning clinical advisors. A recent project rebuilt the multi-site clinic administrator dashboard after staff said they could no longer tell which locations needed attention on a given day. Clinic administrators review major changes before launch.

Required: strong Figma craft, experience running a design system across more than one product team, and enough data visualization skill to keep a dense clinical screen scannable rather than merely full. Eight or more years designing information-dense, professional-use interfaces is the rough bar here, ideally including regulated-industry work, plus the stakeholder management to hold a position through disagreement. Deep specialization in consumer visual design is not required.

Full-time with a flexible schedule, reflecting the cross-team, project-based nature of staff design work here. You can be based in Berlin or elsewhere in Europe, with only light overlap expected against the Berlin product team's core hours. The role reports to the design director and moves between whichever clinical product team needs staff-level judgment that quarter.

jobs.title: Data Engineer, Smart Meter Pipelines
jobs.summary:
Fenwick's platform ingests interval readings from smart meters across several regional utilities, and this engineer works on the pipelines that turn that raw meter data into the usage records billing, forecasting and outage-detection systems all depend on downstream.

New ingestion pipelines get built as utilities onboard additional meter types, and existing ones need maintenance as data volumes grow with each new contract; on-call for pipeline breaks rotates through the team, since a stalled pipeline backs up billing for a utility's customer base. Because meter vendors format and clean data differently, part of the job is negotiating data-quality expectations with utility partners directly rather than accepting whatever arrives. A short data-quality scorecard for each utility feed is reviewed monthly.

Required: production Python and SQL, hands-on Airflow experience orchestrating pipelines other teams depend on, working Kafka knowledge for streaming ingestion, and enough data modeling sense to design schemas that survive the next new utility contract. Three to five years of data engineering work fits this seat, most of it on messy real-world data rather than a clean internal dataset. Deep prior utility-industry background is not required.

Full-time and hybrid, based in Austin with the team in the office a few days a week; heads-down pipeline work fits comfortably around that pattern. On-call rotates across the data engineering team and runs heavier during storm season, when pipeline failures are most likely. The role reports to the lead data engineer on grid infrastructure.

jobs.title: Senior Data Scientist, Load Forecasting
jobs.summary:
Utilities rely on Fenwick's load forecasts to decide how much power to procure ahead of time, and getting those forecasts wrong in either direction carries real financial and reliability consequences for the partners this senior scientist's work reaches directly.

Recent work included reassessing how the model handles extreme weather after last year's forecasts underperformed during a severe heat wave, and building a framework the wider team now uses to reason through weather-driven demand spikes more systematically. The role also covers mentoring two mid-level data scientists who are still building intuition for validating a forecasting model beyond a standard holdout test. Forecast error gets reviewed openly with each utility partner after any significant miss.

Required: strong Python and SQL, real depth in statistics and time-series forecasting, and enough causal inference background to separate a genuine demand shift from a coincidence. Plan on five to eight years doing applied forecasting or statistical modeling, along with the composure to defend a conclusion to utility engineers who know their own grid better than anyone. A background specifically in energy or utilities is not required if the forecasting fundamentals are strong.

Full-time and fully remote within the United States, with the load-forecasting team anchored in Austin and most collaboration happening asynchronously across time zones. Occasional travel to Austin for planning weeks is likely but not frequent. The role reports to the data science manager overseeing the forecasting and anomaly-detection scientists.

jobs.title: Machine Learning Engineer, Grid Anomaly Detection
jobs.summary:
Grid equipment on Fenwick's network throws off sensor data that an anomaly-detection model already reads well in offline testing, but competing engineering priorities have kept it out of production, and this five-month contract exists to close that gap.

Serving infrastructure comes first: enough of it to run the model against a continuous stream of grid sensor data, with basic monitoring so operations staff are alerted quickly when it flags something worth checking. You will also work with the data science team that built the model to confirm production behavior matches offline expectations under noisier real conditions, and leave a short handover document covering deployment decisions and known limitations for whoever inherits maintenance.

Required: production Python, hands-on PyTorch for working with an existing trained model rather than building a new one, Docker for packaging the serving layer, and enough MLOps grounding to monitor a live model responsibly. This contract wants three to five years taking models from research into production. A research-only background, without prior production deployment work, is not what this engagement needs.

This is a remote, five-month contract open across the United States, with the anomaly-detection and data science teams anchored in Austin for planning syncs. Alert thresholds are tuned conservatively at launch and adjusted from the first weeks of live flags. The engineer works alongside the data science team but reports to the engineering manager for grid operations tooling.

jobs.title: Analytics Engineer, Outage Reporting
jobs.summary:
Utility partners expect timely, accurate outage reports during severe weather, and this analytics engineer sits with the Outage Reporting team at Fenwick, building and maintaining the dbt models that turn raw grid sensor and customer-call data into those reports.

Direct contact with the operations analysts and utility account managers who consume these models is part of the daily routine, so you understand what they actually need during a live outage. Test coverage on models built quickly during earlier storm seasons, under real time pressure, needs to rise gradually. Because outage patterns and reporting needs differ by utility and region, the underlying data structures shift more often than in a single-customer data model, and reliability during a storm matters more than architectural elegance.

Required: solid SQL and dbt modeling skill, and enough data modeling judgment to keep models maintainable as utility-specific quirks pile up under deadline pressure. Three to five years building and maintaining production data models is what the role assumes. Deep specialization in a single, already well-documented pipeline is not required; comfort picking up an unfamiliar one quickly and working under real time pressure matters more.

Full-time and onsite in Austin, working alongside the outage-reporting and operations teams day to day rather than remotely. Coverage expectations rise during declared severe-weather events, when the team works from the office together regardless of the usual schedule. The role reports to the analytics engineering lead on the outage-reporting product.

jobs.title: Lead Data Engineer, Grid Infrastructure
jobs.summary:
Three utility-facing product lines at Fenwick have historically built their own ingestion and processing pipelines somewhat independently, and this lead role exists to address the duplicated effort and inconsistent data-quality practices that grew out of that, across teams that ultimately serve overlapping utility customers.

A shared data infrastructure strategy is the first deliverable, designed together with each product line's engineers so migration onto common tooling doesn't disrupt service to existing utility partners mid-contract. Technical standards need to balance consistency against each team's different latency and reliability needs. A recent milestone migrated the outage-reporting and load-forecasting teams onto a shared streaming layer, cutting duplicated infrastructure cost meaningfully, though persuading a team to give up a familiar pipeline is hard.

Required: deep Python and distributed-systems fluency, production Kafka and Kubernetes experience, and enough data modeling judgment to design schemas three different teams can share. Scope is what defines this seat, not tenure: you should already have consolidated fragmented data infrastructure across previously independent teams, not simply contributed to one. A background specifically in the energy sector is not required.

In-office days in Austin run several a week during the migration's active phases, easing back once the new tooling stabilizes; the role is full-time and hybrid throughout. Reporting into the head of platform engineering, this person works closely with each product line's own tech lead, rather than dictating changes from a distance.

jobs.title: Data Science Manager, Energy Analytics
jobs.summary:
Five data scientists embedded across load forecasting, anomaly detection and outage prediction report to this manager on Fenwick's energy analytics team, who balances hands-on technical guidance with the hiring, performance reviews and resource planning that come with running the group.

Disagreements between product lines over the same data scientist's time flare up reliably during storm season, and resolving them falls to you, along with reviewing major analyses for methodological soundness before they inform a utility-facing commitment. A more structured onboarding process is also overdue, after several recent hires struggled to get up to speed given how domain-specific grid data is. A brief joint review with the affected utility account manager follows any model change that touches a customer-visible number.

Required: hands-on Python and statistics strong enough to review someone else's analysis critically, plus real leadership and coaching skill. The bar is roughly five years doing applied data science, with some of that time spent directly managing other data scientists. A track record managing a large organization is not required, five people is the scope here, and coaching matters more than headcount previously managed.

In-office days align with the wider data organization's planning weeks, typically three a week, in a full-time hybrid arrangement based in Austin. This manager reports to the director overseeing energy analytics.

jobs.title: Senior Forecasting Scientist, Renewable Generation
jobs.summary:
As utilities in Fenwick's portfolio add more solar and wind capacity, predicting how much power those sources will actually generate on a given day has become as important to grid planning as predicting demand, and this scientist owns the modeling behind those renewable-generation forecasts.

Current priorities include improving forecast accuracy for distributed rooftop solar, which is harder to observe directly than a single large wind farm and has to be estimated from weather data and a sample of monitored installations. The role also sets modeling conventions for newer scientists as the renewable-forecasting effort grows from a one-person project into a small team. A recent improvement cut forecast error for a partner utility's solar portfolio meaningfully during an unusually variable spring.

Required: strong Python and statistics, real time-series forecasting depth, SQL for pulling your own data, and enough weather modeling background to connect meteorological inputs to generation output. This role calls for five to eight years owning forecasting models that downstream planning decisions depend on directly. A background specifically in solar engineering or meteorology is not required if the statistical fundamentals transfer.

Full-time and fully remote across Europe, with the renewable-forecasting team anchored in Dublin and most collaboration happening asynchronously. Occasional travel to Dublin for team planning is expected a few times a year. The role reports to the senior manager for energy analytics and sets modeling conventions the newer team members follow.

jobs.title: Product Manager, Utility Portal
jobs.summary:
Utility account managers use Fenwick's web portal to monitor grid health, review outage reports and configure alerting thresholds for their own service territory, and this product manager owns that portal end to end on behalf of professional utility staff rather than everyday consumers.

Requirements come straight from utility partners: what portal capabilities would help their own operations teams, weighed against competing requests from other accounts, and communicated clearly enough that utility staff are never caught off guard during a live grid event. A recent project added configurable alert thresholds after several utilities asked for different sensitivity settings than the one-size-fits-all default the portal originally shipped with.

Required: roadmapping experience, enough API design literacy to have a real conversation with engineering about what's feasible, and the stakeholder management to balance requests arriving from several competing utility accounts at once. Three to five years in product management is the expectation here. Prior utility-industry experience is not required if you've managed a partner-facing roadmap before.

Based onsite in Austin, working alongside the utility portal's engineering team day to day rather than remotely, this is a full-time role reporting to the senior product manager for field operations tools. It also coordinates closely with the utility account management team on rollout timing and external messaging, since a late heads-up lands worse than a rough one.

jobs.title: Senior Product Manager, Field Operations Tools
jobs.summary:
Field technicians who maintain Fenwick's grid equipment use a separate mobile tool to log inspections, report faults and close out repair tickets, often while standing at a substation with limited connectivity, and this senior product manager brings more intentional prioritization to a tool that has grown somewhat haphazardly.

Field technicians get surveyed regularly about their biggest workflow pain points, from confusing offline-sync behavior to inspection checklists that don't match how a particular utility structures its maintenance program, and the roadmap addresses the highest-impact problems first rather than whichever utility complains loudest. Proposed changes get tested with a handful of technicians in the field before wider rollout, and a rolling list of offline-sync failures is a reliable early signal that a release needs attention.

Required: strong roadmapping and product strategy skill, and the stakeholder management to make a credible case for engineering resources on a tool that rarely gets the visible investment a customer-facing dashboard does. Five to eight years in product management, most of it shipping to a genuinely operational user base, is what gets you in the door. Prior field-service or frontline-worker software experience is a plus, not a requirement.

In-office days in Austin are set around field-technician survey work and roadmap reviews, in a full-time hybrid role, with occasional travel to a utility substation to observe technicians directly. This role answers to the director of product overseeing operational tooling, alongside the utility portal's product manager.

jobs.title: Product Analyst, Grid Operations
jobs.summary:
Fenwick Grid Systems just signed its largest utility partner to date, and the resulting spike in inspection volume is why this four-month contract opening exists on the field operations product team, working alongside the account managers who need clean data fastest.

Grid inspection data currently arrives through five different field-tool integrations, and every time one ships a new release the underlying schema shifts just enough to break a dashboard filter or mislabel a status field. You will track down which release caused a given break, patch the affected SQL queries, and rebuild the dashboard views utility account managers check each morning. Account managers also routinely need a one-off cut of inspection data ahead of a partner meeting, sometimes with only a day's notice.

Required: working SQL and Excel, plus enough product analytics instinct to know which number an account manager actually needs before their client call. This is an entry-level seat: up to two years of hands-on analytics work, including academic or project experience, is enough. Deep prior familiarity with Fenwick's specific tools is not required, the first deliverable is a document defining basic metrics precisely because that knowledge isn't written down yet.

Open remotely across the United States, this four-month contract runs through the new partner's onboarding period rather than indefinitely, with the field operations team anchored in Austin. Because ramp-up time is short, comfort asking pointed questions in the first week matters more than polish. The role reports to the product analyst lead on grid operations.

jobs.title: Technical Product Manager, Grid Infrastructure
jobs.summary:
Infrastructure reliability, ingestion capacity and internal developer tooling rarely draw the same attention as a utility-facing feature, yet they matter enormously to platform health during high-demand events like storm season, and this technical product manager makes the case for investing in them anyway.

Translating infrastructure engineers' technical concerns into business cases leadership can weigh against other priorities is most of the job, along with occasionally arguing for infrastructure work over more visible feature requests. A recent success secured dedicated engineering time for an ingestion bottleneck flagged internally for over a year before it nearly caused a reporting delay during a major storm. A quarterly reliability scorecard shared with utility partners now backs that argument with real numbers.

Required: real API design literacy, roadmapping experience, and enough distributed-systems fluency to engage credibly with infrastructure engineers on architecture trade-offs. Five to eight years in technical product management is what this role wants, ideally including infrastructure or platform work specifically, plus the stakeholder management to sell that work internally. Hands-on coding ability is not required, though you need enough technical depth to evaluate a trade-off engineers propose.

Full-time and onsite at the Dublin office, serving Fenwick's growing European utility customer base alongside the infrastructure engineering team in person rather than over video. Management responsibility for this role sits with the director of product for operational tooling, with daily contact alongside the infrastructure engineering lead.

jobs.title: Director of Product
jobs.summary:
Product strategy across Fenwick's utility portal and field operations tooling falls to this director, working alongside a peer who owns the core grid-analytics product lines so these more operational products serve the company's overall direction rather than becoming disconnected side efforts.

Quarterly planning across several product managers anchors the role, along with resolving disputes over shared engineering resources between the operational tooling and core analytics teams, and representing operational-tooling priorities in company-wide leadership planning, where utility-facing analytics tends to get more attention by default. A quarterly review of staffing requests across both areas usually means making an explicit trade-off rather than approving whichever team asked first.

Required: strong leadership and strategy skill, and the stakeholder management and roadmapping experience to run several product managers at once. Years matter less here than scope: you should already be balancing infrastructure and tooling investment against feature-delivery pressure at a senior level. Deep domain expertise in any one of the two product areas is not required, since the point of the role is balancing both.

Open only to internal candidates, given how much of the job depends on already understanding Fenwick's product organization and the tension between visible analytics and less visible tooling, this is a full-time, hybrid role based in Austin. It reports to the VP of product and manages the product managers on both portfolios.

jobs.title: Group Product Manager, Internal Tools
jobs.summary:
Three product managers responsible for different parts of Fenwick's internal tooling suite, the software the company's own operations and support staff use rather than utility customers directly, report through this group product manager, who owns the group's overall output.

Regular planning across the group takes up a good share of the week, mediating when two product managers want overlapping engineering resources during the same sprint, and representing the group's priorities when platform leadership makes trade-off decisions that affect internal tooling investment. A current focus is improving how the group measures the impact of internal tools, which had previously been tracked inconsistently or, in some cases, only through anecdotal feedback from support staff.

Required: real leadership skill, roadmapping experience, and the stakeholder management to argue for internal-facing investment that never shows up directly in customer-facing metrics. Figure on at least five years in product management, including direct experience managing other product managers. Specific experience with utility-facing products is not required, since this group serves internal staff only.

Full-time and hybrid, based in the Dublin office, with in-office days set around the group's planning cadence rather than fixed to particular weekdays. The role reports to platform leadership and manages the three product managers on the internal tooling suite directly, coordinating with the Austin-based leadership team on shared roadmap decisions.

jobs.title: Senior Product Designer, Operations Dashboard
jobs.summary:
Fenwick's internal operations dashboard has grown slow to load and cluttered with information most support staff and grid operators rarely use during a shift, and this freelance engagement brings in a designer for a focused, time-boxed redesign of the whole experience.

The engagement covers research into current pain points through short interviews with dashboard users, prototyping a streamlined alternative organized around the handful of metrics operators actually check hour to hour, and preparing detailed specifications for the engineering team to implement once the engagement concludes. Because the users are internal Fenwick staff rather than external customers, feedback cycles move faster than typical utility-facing work.

Required: strong Figma and interaction design skill, real design systems fluency, and enough data visualization judgment to know which metrics earn a permanent spot on a dashboard operators check constantly. This engagement expects five to eight years of product design work behind you. Prior utility or B2B dashboard experience is not required, since the interviews and prototyping process are what matter here.

This is a remote freelance engagement open globally, expected to run approximately ten weeks with a lighter, usage-based follow-up review afterward. Because the work is internal-facing, approval chains are short, and a designer who prefers rapid iteration over long external sign-off will fit well. The engagement reports to the field operations product lead.

jobs.title: UX Researcher, Field Technician Tools
jobs.summary:
Standing at a substation in bright sun with a phone that keeps losing signal is not something a usability lab replicates well, and this researcher exists to study how technicians actually use Fenwick's mobile inspection tool under exactly those conditions.

Accompanying technicians on real inspection routes makes up a good share of the work, observing how gloves, outdoor light and spotty connectivity affect their interaction with the app, then running follow-up interviews about specific moments of friction from those sessions. Because utility account managers and frontline field technicians have very different expectations and vocabulary, adapting research approach and style to the audience is constant rather than occasional. Findings are shared back with technicians directly wherever possible.

Required: real user-interview and usability-testing skill, research synthesis strong enough to turn scattered field observations into something a product team can act on, and contextual inquiry experience for studying behavior in a physical, non-desk setting. Three to five years doing applied UX research is about right for this seat. Fluency in German is not required, since sessions run in English with technicians across the region.

Schedule and location are flexible within Europe, anchored loosely to the Dublin research team, in a full-time role that accommodates occasional travel to field sites and alignment with technicians' own shift patterns across regions. It reports to the senior researcher on the field operations product team.

jobs.title: Checkout QA Automation Engineer
jobs.summary:
The Checkout Platform group at Vantail Systems owns the payment flows merchants embed directly into their storefronts, and this role keeps those flows dependable across dozens of card networks, wallets and regional payment methods used by merchants worldwide.

Playwright suites that run against every checkout release are the core deliverable, extended and maintained in TypeScript alongside the engineers shipping the flow rather than behind a separate QA wall. Day-to-day work includes designing test scenarios for new payment methods before they reach production, maintaining the CI pipeline that gates merges into the checkout service, and chasing flaky tests to a real root cause instead of retrying them away. Coverage also gets added directly from any issue found in the team's incident retrospectives.

Required: solid TypeScript and Playwright skill, real API testing experience, and enough CI/CD fluency to own a pipeline other engineers merge against daily without becoming a bottleneck. Three to five years in test automation, ideally with some payments or other regulated-flow work in the mix, puts you in range for this seat. Familiarity with payment gateways, including quirks like 3D Secure or wallet tokenization, is a plus, not a requirement on day one.

Full-time and fully remote within Europe, with core hours overlapping Central European time and the checkout team shipping on a weekly release train. This role signs off on release readiness alongside the engineering lead, and success is tracked through defect escape rate rather than raw test count.

jobs.title: Senior Payments SDET
jobs.summary:
Payment failures that only appear under load or across specific bank routing paths are the hardest bugs to catch before they hit merchants, and that is the core problem this SDET role, reporting into the Payments Platform engineering group, exists to solve.

Automated test frameworks in Java, built to simulate high-volume transaction bursts, partial gateway outages and retry storms, are the main deliverable, wired into the release pipeline so regressions are caught before rollout rather than after a merchant complaint. Close partnership with the platform's SRE team turns production incidents into repeatable automated tests, and PCI-relevant regression coverage for card tokenization is owned end to end, alongside mentoring two mid-level engineers building out a newer service-level test harness.

Required: strong Java and Selenium skill, real test-automation-framework design experience, and comfort reading distributed tracing to track a failure across several services at once. Five to eight years in test engineering, much of it PCI compliance and regression testing on a system that cannot silently drop a transaction, is what the role calls for. Prior banking-sector employment is not required; the team will teach payments domain specifics to a strong test engineer.

The team meets twice weekly for planning and incident review rather than daily standups, in a full-time role that's fully remote within Europe. Quarterly test-coverage findings get presented to payments engineering leadership, translating technical gaps into a prioritized list they can weigh against other roadmap commitments.

jobs.title: Principal Quality Engineer
jobs.summary:
Defects that slip into Vantail's checkout and payment path can cost an independent retailer revenue within minutes, which is why the quality organization reports its findings directly to engineering leadership rather than sitting downstream of it, and this principal role sets that organization's strategy.

Testing strategy across all four product groups, checkout, payments, fraud and the merchant dashboard, is set here, deciding where automation investment pays off fastest and where manual exploratory testing still catches what tooling cannot. Day-to-day scripting stays with the product teams; this seat instead designs the quality architecture, chooses the frameworks teams standardize on, and builds the dashboard that surfaces defect trends to the VP of Engineering monthly. An early task is merging three automation stacks into one shared library.

Required: deep test strategy and automation architecture experience, strong Python, and hands-on experience designing CI/CD pipelines, plus the team leadership to influence engineers who don't report to you directly. Eight or more years leading quality organizations through a scaling period is what this role expects. Writing test scripts day to day is not part of the job, so recent hands-on scripting speed isn't what this role is evaluated on.

In-office days in Berlin run three a week, in a full-time hybrid role. A quarterly quality review happens with each product group's engineering lead, and success is measured by a sustained reduction in production incidents traced back to insufficient test coverage rather than by raw ticket volume alone.

jobs.title: Order Management QA Analyst
jobs.summary:
Merchants depend on the order management system to reconcile what a shopper paid against what actually ships, and small discrepancies there turn into support tickets and refund disputes fast, which is what this entry-level role inside the Order Management team exists to catch first.

Clear test cases in Jira come first, executed against each release candidate, with bug reports detailed enough that an engineer can reproduce the issue without follow-up questions, covering order-state transitions from created through paid, fulfilled and refunded, plus edge cases like a shopper cancelling mid-fulfillment. Over the first few months, the team's emerging automation suite becomes part of the job too, pairing with a senior QA engineer to convert repeated manual checks into scripted tests, alongside sitting in on sprint planning.

Required: careful test-case design and manual testing discipline, comfort working in Jira, and enough exploratory-testing instinct to find the edge case a written test case missed. This is an entry-level seat: up to two years of QA experience, including coursework or a bootcamp project, is enough. Prior automation-scripting experience is not required, since that's something you'll pair on and learn in the role.

Based onsite in Berlin, working alongside the order management engineers five days a week rather than remotely, this full-time role reports to the order management team's dedicated QA lead daily, and the team values careful, methodical documentation over raw speed through the first full year on the job.

jobs.title: API Test Engineer
jobs.summary:
Postman collections and contract tests are the backbone of how Vantail Systems verifies its public developer API before every release, and this six-month contract is focused entirely on strengthening that layer ahead of a major API version upgrade, timed so partner integrations don't quietly break.

You will build and maintain automated contract tests using Postman and Newman, wired into the CI pipeline so a breaking change to a request or response schema fails the build immediately rather than surfacing in a partner integration weeks later. Working alongside the API platform team, you will audit existing endpoints for undocumented behavior, write the missing test coverage, and flag inconsistencies to the engineering lead before they become public contract commitments.

Required: real Postman and Newman skill, contract-testing experience, and enough CI/CD fluency to wire test failures directly into a release gate rather than a report nobody reads. Three to five years in API testing, most of it on a public-facing API with real external consumers, is what this contract expects. Prior experience with Vantail's specific API is not required, since auditing existing endpoints from scratch is part of the first few weeks.

Europe-wide and remote, this six-month contract allows a possible extension if the migration's scope grows beyond what's currently planned. The team expects overlap with Central European working hours for daily standups, and the role runs through the end of the version-migration window, reporting to the API platform team's engineering lead.

jobs.title: Payments API Developer Advocate
jobs.summary:
External developers integrating Vantail's Payments API are often building their first checkout flow, and this role exists to make that first integration go smoothly rather than turn into a support escalation that eats into the platform engineers' week.

You will write and maintain the getting-started guides, sample applications and reference implementations most developers touch before their first successful test transaction, working closely with API platform engineers to keep documentation accurate as endpoints evolve. Part of the role is proactive: monitoring developer forums and support tickets for recurring points of confusion, then fixing the documentation or sample code rather than repeating the same answer. You also represent the developer's perspective in API design reviews.

Required: strong technical writing and API documentation skill, comfort producing sample code developers will copy directly, and enough public-speaking comfort for the occasional meetup talk. Three to five years in developer advocacy or a closely related technical role gets you to where this seat starts. A background in payments specifically is not required, provided the writing and empathy for a first-time integrator are strong.

Full-time and fully remote within North America, with travel to developer meetups and partner workshops roughly four to six times a year. This posting is open to internal transfer candidates first, reflecting a preference for growing the role from people who already know the platform, and it reports to the senior developer advocate owning integrations.

jobs.title: Senior Integrations Developer Advocate
jobs.summary:
Time to first successful API call is the metric this role is judged against, and lowering it across Vantail's growing base of platform integrators, the point-of-sale and storefront builders whose customers rely on Vantail's checkout underneath their own branding, is the mandate.

You will lead the technical relationship with Vantail's largest platform partners, building reference integrations for the three most common partner tech stacks, running technical enablement sessions for partner engineering teams, and escalating platform gaps directly to product management when a partner hits a wall the current API can't solve cleanly. You will also mentor two more junior advocates on public speaking and technical writing, and maintain a scorecard tracking integration health across the partner portfolio.

Required: real experience writing SDKs and integration guides, solid Git fluency, enough community-management instinct to keep partner engineers engaged between launches, and enough backend background to read and critique another engineer's integration code. Five to eight years in developer relations or a closely related engineering role is roughly what this seat needs. Extensive conference-speaking history is not required on day one, since the team is growing its conference presence together this year.

Quarterly travel for partner summits is part of this full-time, fully remote role within North America, with integration-health metrics reviewed together every two weeks. The role reports into the head of developer relations rather than into engineering, and sits alongside two other senior advocates covering different partner segments.

jobs.title: Staff Developer Advocate
jobs.summary:
Setting the multi-year developer experience strategy for Vantail's public API surface falls to this staff-level role, which sits one level above individual advocacy work and closer to product strategy than to day-to-day content production, even though content still matters.

You will decide which developer segments the advocacy team prioritizes each year, merchants, platform partners, or independent marketplace developers, and defend that call to the VP of Product when resources are tight. This means owning the annual developer experience roadmap, running research that finds where developers abandon integration attempts, and partnering with the API platform team to fix the underlying friction rather than only documenting around it. You are also the final editorial reviewer for major documentation work.

Required: real content strategy and program management skill, open-source fluency, and enough stakeholder collaboration experience to be credible in a room of staff engineers. Eight or more years in developer relations or developer experience work is what the role calls for. A single-industry background is not required, since the role spans merchants, platform partners and marketplace developers alike.

Two or three major industry conferences a year come with this full-time, fully remote North America role, as a featured speaker. Team health is tracked through a quarterly developer satisfaction survey rather than raw content output, and the role reports directly to the VP of Product overseeing developer experience company-wide.

jobs.title: Developer Community Lead
jobs.summary:
Independent developers building tools and plugins on top of Vantail's platform have grown into a real but fragmented community, scattered across side channels, and this lead role exists to give that community an actual home rather than a scattering of half-watched chats.

You will run Vantail's official developer community spaces, moderate discussions, organize a recurring virtual meetup, and identify the most active contributors for a formal partner-recognition program launching next year. Managing two community coordinators, you will set the editorial calendar for community content, decide which community-built integrations get featured in official documentation, and triage community-reported bugs into the right engineering queue with enough context that they get picked up rather than lost.

Required: real community-building and event-planning experience, comfort running Discord or Slack communities at scale, and enough content-calendar discipline and feel for developer feedback loops to keep both the newsletter and the bug-triage queue moving. Scope defines this seat far more than years on a resume: you should already have grown and moderated a technical community of meaningful size. A background specifically in payments is not required, since the role is about community craft rather than the underlying product domain.

Full-time and hybrid, split between Vantail's Berlin and Amsterdam offices, roughly three days a week in whichever location you're based. Community engagement metrics are reviewed with marketing leadership every month, with the reporting line running to the head of developer relations, who also owns the wider advocacy program.

jobs.title: API Documentation Writer
jobs.summary:
Vantail Systems is rewriting the weakest sections of its API reference before a public developer conference, and the freelance technical writer taking this on works directly against the checkout and fraud APIs rather than a generic style guide.

The work starts with auditing existing checkout and fraud API docs against actual current endpoint behavior, then rewriting the sections that leave developers guessing and adding working code samples in at least three languages for the most-used endpoints. Scoped to roughly twelve weeks, the engagement tracks closely with the API platform team, since endpoint details keep shifting until days before the conference.

Required: comfort reading OpenAPI specifications directly rather than working from a secondhand summary, fluency in Markdown, and a Git workflow for submitting documentation changes through pull requests like an engineer would. Three to five years of technical writing experience, ideally on developer-facing API references, is the level this engagement is scoped for. Prior experience with payments or fraud systems specifically is not required; the API platform team briefs contributors on the domain.

Open to writers anywhere as a project-based freelance engagement, paid hourly with no fixed office or timezone requirement. Weekly video check-ins with the API platform team track progress against the documentation backlog, and the twelve-week scope ends at the conference date rather than rolling forward automatically.

jobs.title: Merchant Support Engineer
jobs.summary:
Every merchant support ticket at Vantail Systems starts as an unknown: a misconfigured webhook and a genuinely broken payment path look similar until someone digs in, and the merchant support engineer joining this team makes that first call under time pressure.

Reproducing merchant-reported checkout and payments issues where possible comes first, followed by routing confirmed platform bugs to the right engineering team with clear steps to recreate them. Reading application logs and API traces daily is what separates a merchant configuration mistake from an actual platform defect, and you will maintain the troubleshooting playbooks the wider support team relies on plus join a monthly review with checkout and payments engineering leads.

Required: working SQL for querying transaction and merchant records, hands-on Zendesk ticket triage experience, and enough comfort with application logs to distinguish a configuration error from a genuine bug. This seat is built for someone with two to four years in a technical support or merchant onboarding role. Prior experience specifically in payments is useful but not required, since the team trains new hires on the domain.

Three days a week in the Amsterdam office and the rest from home make up the hybrid schedule here. The team runs a rotating on-call rotation that adds evening coverage during peak retail seasons, and the role reports to the merchant support team lead.

jobs.title: Checkout Customer Success Engineer
jobs.summary:
Twenty or so merchants on Vantail's payments platform get a named technical contact instead of a general support queue, and that relationship is what this senior customer success engineer owns across a portfolio spanning several European markets.

Quarterly technical reviews with each merchant's engineering team anchor the role, alongside flagging checkout performance issues before the merchant notices them and coordinating early access to upcoming platform features when a merchant's roadmap calls for it. Accounts span different regions and payment method mixes, so working knowledge of the regional payment landscape behind each one matters, and you will represent merchant feedback at the checkout team's quarterly roadmap review.

Required: Salesforce fluency for account management, hands-on checkout troubleshooting skills, and the data analysis habit of pulling account health trends rather than relying on anecdote. The seniority bar sits at five to eight years in a technical customer success or account management role, ideally with payments exposure. Direct sales negotiation experience is not required, since account executives own the commercial side of renewals.

Working hours flex around overlapping availability across European merchant time zones when a critical issue demands it, based from Berlin or elsewhere on the continent. This role's manager is the head of customer success for the payments product line, and account health scores alongside renewal rates are what gets reviewed.

jobs.title: Technical Sourcer
jobs.summary:
Backend and platform engineering roles at Vantail Systems take longer to fill than the rest of the company, since the payments domain narrows the qualified candidate pool considerably, and the technical sourcer joining the recruiting team builds a deeper pipeline specifically for those harder searches.

Partnering with hiring managers across payments and checkout engineering comes first, translating vague role requirements into concrete sourcing criteria before running outreach campaigns across LinkedIn, GitHub and niche fintech engineering communities. Reviewing inbound applications for technical fit, building longlists through Boolean search, and tracking which outreach messaging underperforms so it can be rewritten rather than repeated round out a typical week.

Required: fluency with Boolean search construction, daily working use of LinkedIn Recruiter, and comfort managing candidate pipelines inside an applicant tracking system without hand-holding. Three to five years of technical sourcing is what the work assumes, ideally with exposure to backend or infrastructure hiring. Closing or offer negotiation experience is not required, since that responsibility sits with the recruiting manager.

The hybrid schedule runs three days a week in the Berlin office, with the rest remote. Weekly pipeline health metrics go to the recruiting manager, and the role suits someone who enjoys the research and outreach side of recruiting more than closing and negotiation.

jobs.title: Payments Sales Engineer
jobs.summary:
Enterprise merchants evaluating Vantail's payments platform almost always want a working proof of concept before they sign, and the senior sales engineer who owns that process carries it end to end, from the first technical call through a functioning pilot integration.

Account executives on the largest deals in the pipeline get direct partnership here, translating a prospect's existing checkout architecture into a realistic integration plan and then building the demo environment that proves it against the prospect's actual payment methods and currencies. Configuring demos across multiple card schemes within a single sales cycle, writing technical responses to security questionnaires, and keeping the shared demo library current as the platform adds payment method support round out the work.

Required: hands-on experience with payments APIs at a platform of comparable complexity, fluency building technical demos and proofs of concept, daily comfort keeping opportunity and demo activity current in Salesforce, and enough solution design judgment to map a prospect's existing stack onto a realistic integration plan. Five to eight years in a sales engineering or solutions architecture role focused on payments puts you in range for this seat. Formal RFP writing experience is not required, since the security team supplies template answers to build from.

Twenty percent travel for onsite prospect meetings comes with an otherwise remote role based anywhere in North America. The position sits inside the payments go-to-market team, and technical win rate on qualified opportunities is the primary measure of success rather than a fixed quota of demos delivered.

jobs.title: Detection Rules QA Tester
jobs.summary:
New detection rules at Ironvale Security have to survive a library of simulated attacks before they ship, since a rule that is too loose floods analysts with noise and one that is too strict lets a real attack through, and the entry-level tester who validates them works inside the detection engineering team itself.

Executing test attack scenarios against staged detection rules inside the SIEM test environment is the daily work, comparing the alerts that actually fire against expected outcomes and logging discrepancies in enough detail for engineers to fix the underlying rule logic. Learning the query language detection rules are written in, taking on a growing share of the regression suite run before every release, and shadowing the team's weekly rule review meeting round out the role over time.

Required: methodical manual testing habits, comfort navigating a SIEM interface daily, and disciplined bug tracking in Jira with enough detail that engineers can reproduce a discrepancy without follow-up questions. This entry-level seat suits one to two years of testing or security-adjacent experience, sometimes even a strong first role out of a bootcamp or degree program. Writing production detection rules yourself is not required or expected in this seat.

Five days a week onsite at the Austin office puts the tester directly alongside the detection engineering team that owns the rules under test. The team hires a meaningful share of its future detection engineers from within this function, so the office proximity is deliberate rather than incidental.

jobs.title: Security Research Technical Writer
jobs.summary:
Ironvale's threat research team keeps uncovering attacker techniques worth publishing, but the researchers writing the first drafts are stretched thin, and the freelance writer joining this engagement turns those notes into finished threat intelligence reports and blog posts.

Preserving technical accuracy while making each report readable to a security practitioner, not only to fellow researchers, is the central skill, alongside standardizing the report template so future pieces need less editorial back-and-forth. Helping researchers think through responsible disclosure timing matters too, since a report published too early can tip off the attackers it describes before vendors patch.

Required: strong technical writing skills, working familiarity with security terminology, comfortable authoring and editing in Markdown, and a portfolio of published technical writing that demonstrates it. Three or more years of professional writing experience, ideally with some security research exposure, is the level this engagement calls for. Hands-on penetration testing or malware analysis experience is not required, since the researchers supply the technical substance for you to shape.

A rolling queue of write-ups drives the schedule rather than a fixed weekly commitment, and the engagement is fully remote, open to writers anywhere. Pieces move at the pace research findings are ready, with the working relationship sitting directly with the research team rather than through a separate editorial layer.

jobs.title: Security Escalations Team Lead
jobs.summary:
Confirmed false negatives, meaning attacks the platform should have caught but did not, escalate to this team the instant they are verified, and how quickly the case moves from report to root cause often decides whether Ironvale keeps that customer's trust. The lead who owns this team carries the heaviest of those escalations personally.

Owning the on-call rotation for critical customer incidents comes first, including personally taking the most severe escalations and coaching the four engineers on the team through the ones delegated instead. Building the postmortem process for detection misses with the detection engineering team, briefing customer-facing leadership on active incidents without inducing panic, and running quarterly tabletop simulations against a worse scenario than the team has actually faced fill out the rest.

Required: hands-on incident response experience, fluency navigating SIEM tooling under time pressure, and a track record leading a small technical team through high-stakes situations. This lead seat is scoped to owning escalation strategy for a team of four rather than pegged to a specific year count, and the posting favors internal candidates first given how much it depends on Ironvale's specific detection stack. Prior formal people-management certification is not required.

Weekend coverage shared evenly across the team is part of the hybrid Austin on-call rotation, and the lead additionally carries a pager for the most severe incidents even outside the standard weekly schedule, reflecting the accountability that comes with the title.

jobs.title: Tier 1 Support Specialist
jobs.summary:
Ironvale's support queue opens with everything from license activation questions to a customer unsure why a specific alert fired, and the tier 1 specialist who triages that queue is the first real filter keeping complex issues from clogging the escalation path unnecessarily.

Triaging incoming tickets through Zendesk and resolving straightforward configuration and account questions directly make up most days, along with writing clear handoff notes whenever a ticket needs to move to a specialist team. Real time in the first weeks goes toward learning to read platform logs well enough to tell a genuine bug from a misconfiguration, since that judgment call is the core skill the role builds, and tracking recurring question patterns to suggest knowledge base additions continues after that.

Required: clear written customer communication, comfort learning a new ticketing system quickly, and the patience to triage a high volume of varied questions without losing accuracy. This entry-level seat does not require prior security industry experience, though one to two years in any customer support role helps. Deep SIEM or log-analysis experience is not required going in, since the role is where that skill gets built.

A standard weekday shift onsite at the Krakow security operations office is the default, with occasional weekend coverage during major incident response events. The role reports to the tier 1 support team lead and works a fixed schedule rather than a rotating one.

jobs.title: Enterprise Technical Account Manager
jobs.summary:
Ironvale's largest enterprise customers run security operations centers that never stop, and each one gets a single technical account manager who knows their detection tuning, integration setup and escalation preferences well enough to be useful during a live incident. This twelve-month contract covers roughly eight such accounts.

Quarterly technical reviews anchor the account relationship, alongside coordinating custom detection rule requests with the detection engineering team and acting as each account's advocate when a platform limitation affects their specific environment. Becoming fluent in every account's unique deployment matters here, since generic advice carries little weight with customers this sophisticated, and documenting configuration decisions in enough detail that a colleague could step in during a handoff without starting from zero is part of the job.

Required: enterprise account management experience carrying at least a handful of high-touch accounts logged and tracked in Salesforce, working incident response knowledge, and comfort writing technical documentation precise enough for a colleague to act on unsupervised. The engagement is scoped for someone five to eight years into technical account management or a similar customer-facing security role. Direct experience with Ironvale's specific detection stack is not required, since the role trains that in over the first accounts assigned.

A fixed twelve-month term, remote within North America, comes with the possibility of conversion to a permanent role depending on business needs once the contract ends. Direct exposure to security leadership at major enterprise customers carries correspondingly high expectations for responsiveness, including outside standard hours during a live incident.

jobs.title: Threat Escalation Engineer
jobs.summary:
Alerts a customer flags as suspicious sometimes need deeper investigation than the first-line support team can provide, and those escalations land with the threat escalation engineer who sits at the boundary between customer support and the detection engineering organization inside Ironvale's Krakow office.

Investigating escalated alerts using the platform's own log analysis tooling comes first, determining whether the underlying detection logic behaved correctly and either closing the loop with the customer directly or filing a detailed engineering ticket when a genuine rule gap turns up.
