Spotting patterns across tickets matters too: three similar false positives in a week should get flagged as a trend rather than treated as isolated cases, and onboarding newer support engineers onto the log analysis tooling rounds out the role.

Required: strong log analysis skills, working knowledge of SIEM tooling, and enough API debugging ability to tell a client-side integration mistake from a platform defect. Three to five years of technical incident response or escalation work marks the experience threshold here. Prior customer-facing support experience is not required, since log analysis ability matters more here and the role trains the communication side.

A rotating shift that includes some evening coverage comes with the hybrid Krakow schedule, since security incidents do not confine themselves to business hours. The role reports into the escalations team lead and sits between the support queue and detection engineering day to day.

jobs.title: Customer Success Manager
jobs.summary:
Renewal conversations for security software tend to hinge on whether a customer's security team actually trusts the platform rather than on contract terms alone, and building that trust over the life of an account is what this senior customer success manager owns within Ironvale's Europe-based success team.

Owning a portfolio of mid-market and enterprise accounts comes first, running onboarding through to renewal, tracking adoption of key detection features, and flagging early signs of disengagement before they turn into churn risk. Close coordination with the technical account management team on larger accounts and with product when feedback across the portfolio suggests a real roadmap gap continues day to day, alongside building quarterly business reviews that translate usage data into a narrative customer leadership finds useful.

Required: Salesforce fluency for pipeline and account tracking, hands-on renewal management experience, and the account health judgment to spot disengagement before a customer raises it themselves. Five to eight years in customer success or account management, ideally in security or another trust-sensitive software category, is roughly the tenure this seat assumes. Direct technical troubleshooting skill is not required, since the technical account management team handles that layer.

Krakow or elsewhere in Europe both work for this fully remote role, as long as working hours overlap with the team's core hours. The role reports into the senior manager of customer success, and account health scores alongside renewal rates are the metrics reviewed each quarter.

jobs.title: Security Sales Engineer
jobs.summary:
Prospective customers evaluating Ironvale almost always want to watch the platform catch a simulated attack in their own environment before they trust it with real production traffic, and running that demonstration convincingly is the core skill the sales engineer joining this Austin-based team builds.

Supporting account executives through the technical stages of the sales cycle comes first, configuring proof-of-concept environments and building demo scenarios that map to a specific prospect's threat model rather than a generic script. Answering architecture and deployment questions, responding to security questionnaires alongside the security and legal teams, and shadowing senior sales engineers on the first several proof-of-concept engagements before running one independently round out the growth path.

Required: comfort building and running technical demos under time pressure, working knowledge of security architecture concepts, the Salesforce discipline to keep opportunity stages accurate for the account executives you support, and enough solution design instinct to translate a prospect's environment into a believable proof of concept. Three to five years in a technical, customer-facing role is the level this growth-track seat is set at, with room to grow into more senior sales engineering responsibility. Prior formal sales engineering title experience is not required, since the team runs a structured shadowing period before solo ownership.

Part of the week in the Austin office defines the hybrid schedule, working alongside account executives and senior sales engineers who review demo scripts together monthly to keep them current against the product roadmap. The role reports to the sales engineering manager.

jobs.title: Solutions Engineer
jobs.summary:
Every enterprise prospect arrives with a different existing security stack already in place, and the senior solutions engineer responsible for designing a realistic integration architecture has to fit Ironvale into that stack without asking the customer to rip out tools they already trust.

Leading technical discovery calls and producing architecture diagrams and integration plans for the largest opportunities in the pipeline comes first, alongside writing formal RFP responses with the deal desk team. Partnering with product management matters too, since patterns across enterprise deals are often the clearest signal of where the platform's integration story has real gaps, and mentoring two junior sales engineers while maintaining a shared library of reusable architecture patterns rounds out the work.

Required: solid grounding in common security frameworks, strong technical presentation skills in front of skeptical enterprise buyers, and enough cross-functional collaboration instinct to get product management's attention on a real gap. Five to eight years in a solutions engineering or architecture role, ideally security-adjacent, is what this role expects. Direct people-management experience is not required despite the mentoring component, since it is informal rather than a reporting relationship.

Onsite architecture workshops with the largest prospects pull in roughly twenty-five percent travel, on top of a remote position based anywhere in North America. Day-to-day management comes from the head of solutions engineering, and technical win rate on supported opportunities is the metric that matters most.

jobs.title: Sales Operations Manager
jobs.summary:
Sales processes that worked when Ironvale had twenty account executives start to break down at eighty, and the sales operations manager brought in to redesign them sits within the revenue operations function reporting up through the sales organization.

Owning the sales technology stack, including Salesforce configuration, CPQ-driven quote generation, and the deal approval workflow, comes first, with changes driven by direct feedback from account executives rather than a top-down mandate. Rebuilding the territory assignment model is a current priority, since it has not kept pace with the shift toward larger enterprise deals, and running the systems and process portion of onboarding for new sales hires before handing off to enablement rounds out the role.

Required: hands-on Salesforce administration experience, working knowledge of CPQ tools for quote configuration, and forecasting discipline precise enough that sales leadership can plan headcount against it. Expect to bring three to five years in sales operations or a related revenue operations role. Direct people management experience is not required, since the role is an individual contributor position for now.

Three days a week in the Austin office rounds out the hybrid schedule, partnering closely with finance on compensation plan design and with the VP of Sales on quarterly planning. Success is measured by how little process friction shows up in quarterly rep feedback surveys.

jobs.title: Partner Solutions Engineer
jobs.summary:
Ironvale sells a meaningful share of its enterprise business through managed security service provider partners, and the partner solutions engineer joining the global partner organization gives those partners the technical enablement they need to sell and deploy the platform without pulling in Ironvale's own sales engineering team every time.

Building partner-facing technical training materials and running enablement sessions for new partner engineers comes first, alongside acting as the escalation point when a partner's deployment hits an issue their own team cannot resolve. Joining partner-led customer calls directly when a deal is large enough to warrant it and maintaining the technical certification program partner engineers complete before deploying Ironvale independently round out the work.

Required: solution architecture fluency explainable to engineers who do not work at Ironvale, comfortable technical presentation skills, and direct deal support experience joining live customer calls under pressure. This role sits at the three-to-five-year mark for someone coming from a partner-facing or sales engineering background. Direct MSSP operations experience is not required, since the certification program is designed to close that specific gap.

Occasional shifts in working hours to cover partner time zones outside North America come with this globally open, flexible arrangement. On the org chart, this rolls up to the head of partner solutions engineering, and success is measured by how independently enabled partners become after each certification cohort.

jobs.title: Talent Sourcing Coordinator
jobs.summary:
Filling specialized detection engineering and threat research roles at Ironvale requires sourcing candidates who rarely respond to generic outreach, and the part-time coordinator building those harder pipelines works inside the technical recruiting team specifically for that purpose.

Researching candidates across LinkedIn, security conference speaker lists and open-source security tooling contributors comes first, then coordinating initial outreach and scheduling first-round conversations for the recruiting team. Administrative precision matters just as much: keeping the applicant tracking system current, logging interview feedback promptly, and flagging candidates who have gone quiet so nothing falls through unnoticed.

Required: sourcing research skills that go beyond a basic LinkedIn search, working fluency with applicant tracking systems, and the scheduling discipline to coordinate interviews across a recruiting team's shifting calendars. Two to four years of recruiting coordination or sourcing puts you in range for this one. Prior specifically technical or security-domain sourcing experience is not required, since the recruiting team supplies the domain context.

The schedule runs roughly twenty-five hours a week, fully remote across Europe, with flexibility on which days those hours fall as long as there is overlap with the recruiting team's core hours for coordination. The role reports to the technical sourcing lead based in Krakow.

jobs.title: Network QA Engineer
jobs.summary:
The platform team behind Lumenbridge's network analytics product owns an ingestion pipeline that has to stay accurate no matter how much carrier telemetry a customer throws at it, and the senior QA engineer joining that team keeps pace as data volume keeps growing, since most testing tools were never built for traffic at carrier scale.

Designing and maintaining automated test suites in Python that validate the ingestion pipeline against real, anonymized carrier traffic samples is the core of the job, catching data quality regressions before they reach a customer's operations dashboard. A recurring project this year is building load tests that simulate a full regional carrier's traffic volume, since the current test environment tops out well below what the largest customers actually push through, alongside working with data engineering on new ingestion formats before they ship and contributing fixtures to the shared library other product teams draw from.

Required: solid Python test automation skills, working knowledge of CI/CD pipelines for running suites automatically, and familiarity with core networking concepts like NetFlow or SNMP. Five to eight years in a QA or test automation role, ideally with some exposure to high-volume data systems, is the calibration point for this seat. Deep carrier-specific protocol expertise is not required going in, since the team trains that layer on the job.

Dublin is available as an office base, though the role is remote within Europe by default. The team shares an on-call rotation covering ingestion pipeline incidents, and the role reports to the QA lead for the analytics platform.

jobs.title: Staff SDET
jobs.summary:
Shared test infrastructure that every one of Lumenbridge's five product teams can adopt without rewriting their existing suites is the deliverable for this staff SDET seat. Each team built its own automation stack, CI configuration, and definition of a passing build over several years, and closing that gap at the architecture level, not one team at a time, is the mandate.

Designing a shared test infrastructure platform covering a common CI orchestration layer, shared test data fixtures for carrier network simulations, and a unified flaky-test detection system comes first, built so no team has to start from scratch. Cross-team negotiation follows naturally, since asking five teams to migrate onto shared infrastructure means convincing each one the short-term disruption is worth it, and serving as final technical reviewer for any new automation framework a team proposes rounds out the role.

Required: deep hands-on test automation experience plus genuine platform engineering ability, since the deliverable is infrastructure other engineers build on rather than test scripts for one product. Strong Java skills and fluency designing CI/CD systems at scale matter here. Eight or more years in test engineering, with several of those years in an architecture or staff-level capacity, is the experience this staff opening was built around. Direct people-management experience is not required, since the mentoring here is technical rather than a formal reporting line.

The role runs fully remote within North America, with the Boston office available for anyone who wants an on-site base rather than working from home. Progress gets tracked through a quarterly reduction in average CI run time across all five product teams, with the chain of command leading to the director of quality engineering.

jobs.title: Performance Test Engineer
jobs.summary:
When a regional network outage spikes traffic, Lumenbridge's analytics platform is exactly what carriers lean on to understand what is failing, and this six-month contract exists to prove the platform holds up under that kind of load before it happens for real.

Designing and running performance test scenarios in JMeter that simulate sudden traffic surges into the ingestion pipeline comes first, identifying which components degrade first and documenting findings in enough technical detail that the platform engineering team can prioritize fixes without a live walkthrough. Building a repeatable performance testing framework the team can rerun before each major release is a core deliverable, since performance testing currently happens only when someone remembers to schedule it.

Required: hands-on JMeter scripting experience, comfort reading network monitoring dashboards to trace where a bottleneck originates, and SQL skills for querying the data the ingestion pipeline produces under load. Three to five years in performance or load testing is the bar for this contract. Building the test framework from scratch is expected, so prior experience with Lumenbridge's specific stack is not required.

Fixed through the end of the current fiscal year with possible extension, the contract runs remote across Europe with Warsaw as the team's anchor point. The role reports directly to the engineering lead for the ingestion pipeline, with findings presented at the end of each testing cycle rather than filed and forgotten.

jobs.title: Mobile QA Engineer
jobs.summary:
Field technicians at Lumenbridge's carrier customers diagnose network issues through a mobile app, often from basements or remote cell tower sites with unreliable connectivity, and the senior QA engineer responsible for that app makes sure it behaves correctly under exactly those difficult conditions.

Building and maintaining Appium-based automated tests covering both the iOS and Android versions of the app comes first, with particular focus on offline mode behavior and sync reconciliation once connectivity returns. Manual exploratory testing on physical devices under simulated poor-connectivity conditions makes up a significant part of the role too, since automated tests alone miss flakiness that only shows up on real hardware, and quarterly user research sessions with field technicians directly round things out.

Required: hands-on Appium automation experience across both iOS and Android, comfort with exploratory testing methodology on physical devices, and enough mobile platform knowledge to reproduce a connectivity-dependent bug reliably. You should be carrying five to eight years in mobile QA or test automation to be a fit here. Prior field-service or telecom industry background is not required, since the field technicians themselves supply that context during research sessions.

A device lab onsite in Dublin handles the physical testing that cannot be done remotely, three days a week as part of the hybrid schedule. The role reports to the mobile QA lead and includes upkeep of the lab's device inventory as older hardware falls out of step with what field technicians actually carry.

jobs.title: Accessibility QA Engineer
jobs.summary:
Network operations dashboards at Lumenbridge run around the clock for carrier staff, some of whom rely on screen readers or high-contrast modes, and keeping accessibility from degrading as new dashboard features ship is the job of the accessibility QA engineer inside the dashboard product team.

Auditing new features against WCAG standards before release comes first, testing with actual screen reader software rather than relying on automated scanners alone and filing detailed remediation tickets when a component misses the bar. Maintaining the internal accessibility checklist designers and engineers reference before starting new dashboard work, running periodic training sessions on accessibility pitfalls specific to data-dense interfaces, and coordinating with an external auditor who reviews the platform twice a year through to remediation round out the role.

Required: working knowledge of WCAG success criteria, hands-on testing experience with at least one major screen reader, and disciplined manual testing habits logged clearly in Jira. The team is sizing this at three to five years in accessibility or QA work, with some of it specifically on accessibility. Front-end coding ability to fix flagged issues yourself is not required, since remediation is handled by the design and engineering teams you file tickets to.

Five days a week onsite at the Warsaw office keeps the role working closely with the dashboard product team in person. The role reports to the QA lead for the operations dashboard and tracks remediation of external audit findings through to actual completion twice yearly.

jobs.title: Principal Developer Advocate
jobs.summary:
Carrier engineering teams evaluating Lumenbridge's network analytics APIs are a narrow, technically sophisticated audience, and reaching them looks nothing like typical developer marketing aimed at a broad consumer API crowd. The principal developer advocate hired for this sets the entire developer relations strategy for that niche audience.

Deciding which telecom industry conferences merit Lumenbridge's presence, which carrier engineering communities deserve direct outreach, and which content formats actually land with network engineers rather than general software developers comes first. Personally building the flagship reference integrations that showcase the API against real carrier use cases like fraud detection and capacity planning, representing the developer's perspective directly to the VP of Product during quarterly roadmap planning, and maintaining relationships with a small number of technical champions inside major carrier customers round out the mandate.

Required: a track record of developer advocacy that includes public speaking to technical audiences, hands-on ability to write API documentation and sample code personally, and enough networking domain credibility to be taken seriously in rooms full of network engineers. Think in terms of eight or more years split across developer relations and hands-on engineering. Formal telecom industry certification is not required, since credibility here comes from the integrations shipped, not a credential.

Global and fully remote by default, the role still carries quarterly travel to major telecom industry conferences. Impact is measured through qualified pipeline the advocacy program contributes rather than raw content metrics, and this seat hangs off the VP of Product, who leaves significant day-to-day autonomy over strategy and priorities.

jobs.title: Developer Relations Manager
jobs.summary:
Two individual contributors currently make up Lumenbridge's entire developer relations function, and growing that into a fuller team is the primary mandate for the manager hired to lead it, reporting into the VP of Marketing.

Hiring and managing a small team covering technical content, community and developer advocacy comes first, setting quarterly priorities that balance long-term community building against nearer-term conference deadlines. Taking over editorial planning responsibilities that currently sit informally with individual advocates gives the function a coherent content calendar for the first time, and representing developer relations in marketing leadership meetings, defending budget and headcount requests with concrete engagement metrics, rounds out the role.

Required: program management skills that hold together content, community and advocacy work as one coherent function, hands-on event planning experience, and enough cross-team collaboration credibility to defend a budget request in front of marketing leadership. The target profile is six or more years in developer relations or technical marketing, including some direct people-management experience. Deep personal expertise in the telecom domain is useful but not required, since the team's individual advocates supply that depth.

This posting favors internal candidates first, given the specialized telecom industry knowledge the role benefits from, with a hybrid schedule of three days a week in the Dublin office. Day-to-day work includes negotiating speaking slots and booth placement directly with external conference organizers.

jobs.title: Technical Content Strategist
jobs.summary:
Lumenbridge's technical content library grew unevenly over several years: some topics have three overlapping articles, while the newer fraud detection API is barely documented at all. The freelance content strategist brought in for this engagement exists to fix that imbalance.

Auditing the existing content library against actual product usage data to find the highest-impact gaps comes first, then building a content calendar and either writing or commissioning the pieces needed to close them. Close collaboration with product marketing keeps the calendar aligned to upcoming feature launches rather than an outdated roadmap, and establishing basic content performance tracking plus a recurring quarterly audit that retires pieces no longer reflecting the current product rounds out the scope.

Required: demonstrated content strategy experience, strong technical writing skills applied to a technical or infrastructure product, and working SEO knowledge to prioritize gaps that actually drive search traffic. Three to five years across content strategy and technical writing is the level this engagement calls for. Deep prior telecom or networking domain knowledge is not required, since the product marketing team supplies that context during the audit.

A rolling twelve-week initial scope structures this remote, hourly engagement, open to candidates anywhere. Work happens on a self-directed schedule coordinated with the product marketing team rather than fixed office hours, with the possibility of extension once the initial content gaps are closed.

jobs.title: Carrier API Technical Writer
jobs.summary:
Lumenbridge Networks builds network analytics tools that carrier engineers wire into their own operations software, and this part-time role sits inside the developer relations team that maintains the API documentation those integrations depend on. Telecom data formats and terminology diverge enough from general-purpose APIs that generic documentation templates fall short here.

Maintaining and expanding the carrier-specific reference docs is the core of the job, done in close coordination with the API platform engineers, who confirm accuracy against actual endpoint behavior before anything publishes. Worked examples draw on realistic, anonymized carrier data rather than toy inputs, since this audience notices the difference immediately. Each month you scan support ticket themes for documentation gaps that, closed earlier, would have stopped the ticket from being filed at all.

Required: strong technical writing ability, comfort producing API reference docs and carrier integration guides in Markdown, and enough Git fluency to manage documentation as code alongside the platform team. Three to five years writing developer-facing documentation is the level this seat targets, ideally with some carrier, telecom or networking exposure, since the domain vocabulary takes real time to absorb. Prior hands-on experience with this specific analytics API is not required.

The role runs roughly twenty hours a week on a flexible schedule rather than fixed daily hours, remote within Europe, with the wider documentation and platform teams based out of Dublin. It reports to the developer relations lead, who reviews published updates but otherwise leaves day-to-day scheduling and prioritization to whoever holds the seat.

jobs.title: Network Operations Success Engineer
jobs.summary:
Carrier operations teams running their network uptime monitoring through Lumenbridge's platform have little patience for that platform having problems, and this success engineer role exists to keep the relationship healthy through proactive technical partnership rather than reactive ticket handling. It sits inside customer success, not engineering, since fixes here are usually process calls.

You will run technical health checks against assigned accounts' platform configuration on a regular cadence, catching misconfigurations or underused features before they turn into frustration. Expect to lead onboarding for new carrier customers through their first ninety days, coordinating with professional services on any custom integration work required. You will also build the technical case for renewal and expansion conversations alongside each account's salesperson.

Required: hands-on experience with Zendesk for case management, working SQL for pulling usage and configuration data, and enough network troubleshooting background to diagnose what a carrier customer is actually seeing. Five to seven years in a technical, customer-facing operations role gets you to this seat's experience bar. Direct telecom industry experience is useful but not required, provided the networking fundamentals are solid.

Hours are full-time, with flexible working arrangements across Europe and no fixed office requirement, though the wider customer success organization is anchored in Dublin. Success is tracked through account health scores and the technical adoption rate of key platform features across the portfolio. The role reports to the manager of customer success engineering, who reviews portfolio health monthly.

jobs.title: Senior Carrier Account Manager
jobs.summary:
Twelve or so of Lumenbridge's carrier accounts generate a disproportionate share of total revenue, and this senior account manager role owns the technical and commercial health of that concentrated group. The carrier account management team in Dublin runs this relationship, and the role is one of its most senior seats.

Quarterly business reviews anchor the job, combining platform usage data with a clear-eyed read of account satisfaction; from there you coordinate custom feature requests with product management and manage renewals well ahead of contract expiration to avoid last-minute pressure. Carrier procurement cycles move slowly and involve multiple stakeholders, so keeping a renewal moving through legal and procurement without losing momentum is a real part of the job. Occasional travel to carrier sites for major reviews is expected.

Required: solid Salesforce fluency for pipeline and account tracking, proven account management experience with enterprise or carrier relationships, and comfort producing the technical documentation that supports a renewal case. Five to eight years in account management or a related carrier-facing commercial role is what the seat calls for. A background specifically in telecom is helpful but not required if enterprise account experience is strong.

Expect a hybrid schedule out of the Dublin office, with in-person days used mainly for account strategy sessions and renewal planning. Compensation includes a component tied to renewal and expansion revenue across the portfolio. You'd work for the director of carrier accounts, who stays closely involved in the largest renewal negotiations.

jobs.title: Recruiting Coordinator
jobs.summary:
Interview scheduling across five hiring teams and three time zones is more complex than it sounds, and this entry-level coordinator role keeps Lumenbridge's hiring process moving without candidates slipping through administrative cracks. Five separate hiring managers currently rely on this one coordinator to keep their pipelines moving in sync.

Day to day, you schedule interviews, prepare interviewer packets with candidate background and structured feedback forms, and make sure feedback lands in the applicant tracking system before the next stage is booked. You also serve as a candidate's main point of contact throughout the process, answering logistics questions and keeping them informed on timeline, since a slow or confusing process is a common reason strong candidates drop out. Sourcing support work grows into the role over time.

Required: organized, comfortable use of ATS tools and calendar scheduling under real time pressure, plus clear written and verbal communication with candidates and interviewers. This is an entry-level seat: under a year of office, coordination or customer-facing experience is enough to start. Prior recruiting-specific experience is not required, since the role is designed as a first step into the function.

The coordinator role is based onsite at the Warsaw office, full time, and open to internal candidates first under Lumenbridge's internal mobility program. It works alongside five hiring teams and reports to the recruiting operations manager, who sets weekly scheduling priorities during high-volume hiring pushes.

jobs.title: Enterprise Account Executive
jobs.summary:
Closing a new carrier logo is a long game at Lumenbridge, often twelve to eighteen months from first conversation to signed contract, and this senior account executive role on the enterprise sales team carries a quota built around that reality rather than shorter software sales cycles. North America is the territory, split across a handful of named account executives.

Owning the full sales cycle for enterprise carrier accounts in your territory is the center of the job, from initial outbound through technical evaluation, working closely with a dedicated solutions engineer on every serious opportunity. Carrier buying committees typically span network operations, security and procurement stakeholders with different priorities, so building a coalition of internal champions matters more than relying on one relationship. You also coordinate with product marketing on competitive positioning against rival vendors.

Required: proven Salesforce-driven pipeline management, experience running enterprise sales cycles that stretch well beyond a single quarter, and comfort negotiating contracts and forecasting against a long-cycle quota. Plan on five to eight years in enterprise or carrier-facing sales to be a realistic fit. Prior experience specifically inside telecom is useful but not required if long-cycle enterprise sales experience is strong.

Territory coverage is fully remote within North America, with the sales team anchored in Boston and regular travel to carrier customer sites and industry conferences. Compensation includes a meaningful commission component tied to closed annual contract value, with accelerators for exceeding quota. This account executive seat sits under the VP of enterprise sales.

jobs.title: Deal Desk Analyst
jobs.summary:
Custom pricing terms and non-standard contract structures come up constantly in carrier deals, since large telecom customers rarely accept Lumenbridge's standard order form untouched, and this deal desk role processes those exceptions quickly without exposing the company to unnecessary risk. Revenue operations owns this seat, built to move fast between sales, legal and finance.

You will review deal terms against approval policy, route exceptions to the right internal stakeholder for sign-off, and maintain the pricing and discounting guidelines sales reps reference when structuring a proposal. Auditing closed deals against originally approved terms, to catch discrepancies before they cause revenue recognition problems later, is a recurring piece of the job. You also train new account executives on deal desk process during their onboarding.

Required: working knowledge of CPQ tools and Salesforce for deal configuration and tracking, solid deal structuring and contract review skills, and the cross-functional collaboration to keep exceptions moving without stalling a close. The seat assumes three to five years in deal desk, sales operations or contracts work, comfortable reading a contract redline without legal supervision. Direct telecom industry background is not required.

Office days are hybrid out of Boston, roughly three days a week, with the closest partnership to legal, finance and revenue operations landing in the final week of each quarter, when deal volume spikes and turnaround time matters most. The analyst reports to the manager of deal desk operations, who signs off on any exception outside standard policy.

jobs.title: Test Automation Architect
jobs.summary:
Matchmaking and session-management services at Northfen Interactive have to hold up under sudden concurrent-player spikes whenever a new title launches or a major update drops, and this senior architect role owns the automated test strategy that catches problems before millions of players do. Central quality engineering runs this seat, positioned to catch problems other teams find later.

Designing the test automation architecture for the multiplayer backend is the mandate, choosing Python frameworks that can simulate realistic concurrent player load against staging environments before every major release. A significant piece of the role is building chaos-style tests that deliberately fail individual backend services mid-match to verify the client degrades gracefully rather than disconnecting players outright. You also embed test hooks directly into new services alongside the backend engineering leads as they are built.

Required: deep test strategy and automation architecture experience, strong Python skills, and working CI/CD fluency to wire automated suites into the release pipeline. Distributed systems intuition for multiplayer systems matters as much as testing skill, since the failure modes worth testing rarely show up in the API surface alone. Five to eight years in test automation or backend quality engineering is where this seat is pitched. Prior game industry experience is not required.

Five days a week onsite at the Montreal studio is the working pattern, alongside the backend platform team. You also run a quarterly architecture review with automation leads from each product team, keeping shared test infrastructure from drifting apart as teams evolve their own needs. Accountability for this seat runs to the director of quality engineering.

jobs.title: Lead QA Engineer
jobs.summary:
Launch day for a new Northfen title is when the quality team's work either holds up under real player load or does not, and this lead role makes sure QA is genuinely ready well before that day arrives. Quality engineering in Montreal is where this lead role sits, one layer below the director who sets studio-wide strategy.

Managing a team of six QA engineers across automated testing and structured playtesting is the daily job, setting the test plan for each release and deciding where limited time is best spent between automation, exploratory testing and organized playtest sessions. Running the go or no-go readiness review before each release, presenting known issues and risk directly to production leadership, sits with you. You also mentor two engineers moving from manual testing into automation.

Required: hands-on test automation experience in C# against Unity projects, a working CI/CD setup for automated suites, and real team leadership experience managing other QA engineers day to day. This is a lead-level seat, scoped to owning a team of six and the release readiness call rather than a fixed years threshold, though prior people-management experience is expected. Specific game QA background is preferred but not required if the leadership and automation experience is strong.

The schedule shifts around major launch weeks, which can include weekend coverage, but the base arrangement is full-time and onsite at the Montreal studio. You own the team's budget for device farms and load-testing infrastructure and report monthly quality metrics up to the director of quality engineering, who leaves day-to-day team decisions to you.

jobs.title: Director of Quality Engineering
jobs.summary:
Northfen Interactive ships live-service titles that players expect to keep working around the clock, and the quality organization this director role leads owns testing strategy across every studio team, from the multiplayer backend through individual game clients. Engineering leadership in Montreal is who this director answers to, and four separate QA teams answer to the director in turn.

Setting quality standards and budget priorities across four QA teams, consolidating them under one shared strategy for the first time as the studio scales past its original single-title structure, is the immediate mandate. A major initiative this year is building a dedicated live-ops testing capability that validates in-game events and seasonal content without a full regression pass each time. You also chair the studio's cross-team quality guild, where QA leads calibrate severity definitions consistently.

Required: a track record setting quality metrics and automation strategy across multiple teams, strong stakeholder management with engineering and production leadership, and experience running release management at studio scale. This is a director-level seat, scoped to leading roughly twenty QA engineers across four teams and executive release-readiness discussions, rather than defined by a years threshold. Direct hands-on coding is not required, though technical fluency to challenge automation strategy is.

Based onsite at the Montreal studio, the role is open to internal candidates first, reflecting the studio's preference to promote leaders who already understand its live-service challenges. You report directly to the VP of Engineering and represent quality risk in executive release-readiness discussions ahead of every major launch.

jobs.title: Playtest QA Intern
jobs.summary:
Spending a summer testing unreleased multiplayer game builds before anyone outside the studio has touched them is what this internship offers, working directly alongside Northfen's QA team on a current in-development title. Northfen's Montreal quality team hosts the internship, currently deep in testing for a title still months from launch.

You will run structured playtest sessions following detailed test scripts, log bugs with clear reproduction steps in Jira, and take part in daily bug triage meetings where you will see how the team decides what gets fixed before launch versus what ships as a known issue. As the internship progresses you take on small pieces of exploratory testing with less structure, building the judgment needed to find bugs a script would not catch. You will also sit in on a few production meetings, seeing how playtest findings change what ships.

Required: careful attention to detail, clear written communication for bug reports, and comfort following a structured test script for hours at a stretch. This is an entry-level internship: no professional QA experience is required, only curiosity about how live multiplayer games get tested before launch. Prior Jira experience is helpful but will be taught on the job if you have not used it before.

Twelve weeks, paid, and onsite at the Montreal studio: that is the shape of the internship, working full time alongside the permanent QA team. It is intended as a genuine entry point into a QA career in games rather than administrative work, and reports to the lead QA engineer on the assigned title, who checks in daily during the first few weeks and weekly after that.

jobs.title: Live Ops QA Analyst
jobs.summary:
Seasonal in-game events at Northfen's flagship title ship on a tight two-week cadence, and this analyst role exists to test each one thoroughly within that window without becoming the bottleneck that slows live-ops down. This seat belongs to Helsinki's live-ops quality team, the smallest of the studio's QA groups relative to how much ships through it.

Testing new event content, limited-time modes and in-game store changes against a checklist tuned for live-ops releases is the daily work, since these move faster and carry different risk than the studio's larger quarterly updates. Verifying that in-game economy changes, like new currency sinks or reward tuning, behave as designed rather than accidentally breaking game balance is a meaningful part of the role. You work directly with live-ops production, often testing content still being finalized right up until deployment.

Required: solid manual and regression testing skills, working knowledge of Jira for tracking test coverage and bugs, and enough familiarity with matchmaking systems to spot when an event change affects them unexpectedly. Three to five years in QA, with some live-service or live-ops exposure, is about the experience level this seat assumes. Prior experience specifically with this title's economy system is not required.

Two to three days a week in the Helsinki studio covers the hybrid split, on a schedule aligned to the event release calendar rather than a standard weekly sprint, with occasional evening coverage the night an event goes live. The analyst reports to the live-ops QA lead, who sets test priorities each cycle alongside the live-ops producer.

jobs.title: Game SDK Developer Advocate
jobs.summary:
Third-party studios building on Northfen's multiplayer backend SDK need working reference implementations and responsive technical support to succeed, and this senior freelance advocate role focuses on exactly that developer-facing relationship. Developer relations is who commissions this engagement, fielding integration questions from partner studios across North America.

You will maintain and extend the SDK's sample game project across common game engines, keeping it current as the underlying backend API evolves, and respond directly to integration questions from partner studio engineers in a dedicated developer forum. Writing migration guides whenever a backend API version changes is a recurring piece of the engagement, since partner studios often lag several versions behind and need clear upgrade paths. You also organize partner feedback into structured input for the platform team's roadmap discussions.

Required: experience shipping and maintaining SDK sample code across at least one major game engine, strong developer advocacy or community management background, and comfort supporting other engineers directly rather than through a ticket queue. Five to eight years in developer relations or backend game engineering is the rough tenure this engagement assumes. Public speaking experience is a plus but not required.

Remote and project-based, the engagement is open to candidates across North America, with the developer relations team anchored in Montreal, where occasional in-person planning happens around major releases. It runs on a rolling six-month scope with the possibility of renewal, reporting to the head of developer relations.

jobs.title: Live Ops Support Engineer
jobs.summary:
When a live multiplayer title goes down, or a critical bug affects paying players mid-event, this senior support engineer role is one of the first technical responders, working with backend engineering to diagnose and mitigate the issue while communicating status to the studio. Vancouver's live-ops support team is home base here, the group paged first when a live title misbehaves.

Runbooks for common failure patterns are yours to maintain and improve, alongside a share of the rotating on-call schedule covering live titles and leading post-incident reviews that produce concrete follow-up actions rather than vague lessons-learned notes. You also partner with the community team during major incidents so player-facing communication stays accurate as the technical picture develops, and help design the severity framework the studio uses to decide how aggressively to communicate during an outage.

Required: hands-on experience with Zendesk and structured troubleshooting under pressure, live-ops monitoring tools, and clear customer communication when the technical picture is still incomplete. Five to eight years in a technical support or incident response role is the experience window this seat targets. Deep game development background is not required, though comfort making judgment calls without perfect information is.

Onsite at the Vancouver studio, full time, with an on-call rotation that includes evening and weekend coverage during major launches and live events, shared across a team of four support engineers. The role reports to the live-ops support manager, who leads the post-incident review process alongside you.

jobs.title: Studio Implementation Consultant
jobs.summary:
New partner studios adopting Northfen's multiplayer backend need real implementation support during their first integration, not just documentation, and this consultant role provides that hands-on guidance through a studio's first several months on the platform. Helsinki's partner implementation team is behind this seat, usually the first technical face a newly signed studio meets.

Technical kickoff sessions with new partner engineering teams open each engagement, followed by a review of their integration architecture for common pitfalls before they build too far in the wrong direction, and continued involvement through their first live launch on the platform. Translating what you learn from each implementation into improvements for the standard onboarding documentation is a meaningful part of the role, since patterns that trip up one studio usually trip up the next.

Required: experience running technical onboarding or implementation projects, comfort writing and maintaining technical documentation, and the project coordination skill to keep a multi-month implementation on schedule across two organizations. Three to five years in implementation consulting, technical account management or a related customer-facing technical role gets you to this seat's bar. Game industry background is useful but not required.

The consultant works onsite at the Helsinki studio, full time, with occasional travel to partner studio offices when a relationship warrants an in-person start. You also maintain a running log of integration mistakes across studios for the SDK team's roadmap discussions, and report to the manager of studio implementation.

jobs.title: Player Support Operations Analyst
jobs.summary:
Player support ticket volume at Northfen spikes unpredictably around content launches, live events and the occasional server incident, and this six-month contract role builds the operational visibility support leadership currently lacks into those patterns. Support operations in Vancouver commissioned this contract, the team's first time bringing in outside help for a reporting project.

Dashboards tracking ticket volume, resolution time and category trends across the player support queue are the backbone of the job, feeding a weekly report that leadership uses to staff shifts around predictable demand spikes. Modeling expected ticket volume ahead of the next major content launch, using historical data from comparable past launches, is a specific project this contract will tackle. You also audit the support team's tagging taxonomy, which has drifted over time and now makes trend analysis harder than it should be.

Required: strong SQL for pulling and shaping support data, solid data analysis and reporting skill, and process improvement experience applied to a support or operations queue under real time pressure. Three to five years in support operations, business operations or analytics is the rough tenure this seat targets. Prior experience specifically in games is not required, though comfort with unfamiliar ticketing systems helps.

Six months, remote, and fixed-term: the contract is open to candidates across North America and runs through the end of the studio's current live-ops season. The analyst reports to the support operations manager and works closely with support leadership, most heavily during weekly reporting cycles and the monthly leadership review.

jobs.title: Engineering Technical Recruiter
jobs.summary:
Backend and multiplayer systems engineering roles are consistently the hardest to fill at Northfen, since the pool of engineers with real distributed systems experience in games is small, and this recruiter role owns that hiring pipeline end to end. Montreal's talent acquisition team owns this seat, the one recruiter role dedicated entirely to backend and multiplayer hiring.

You will partner directly with backend engineering leads to build accurate role scorecards, manage candidates through the full interview process, and negotiate offers for the roles you own. Building sourcing strategies that go beyond job postings, including outreach at developer conferences and within specific online communities where backend engineers tend to gather, is a core part of the job. You also track and report time-to-fill and pipeline health metrics to the recruiting manager weekly.

Required: hands-on Boolean search and sourcing skill, working fluency with LinkedIn Recruiter and standard ATS tools, and experience managing candidate pipelines for technical roles end to end, including offer negotiation. Three to five years in technical recruiting is what qualifies for this seat. Prior recruiting experience specifically in games is not required, provided backend or distributed systems hiring experience is solid.

Three days a week in the Montreal studio covers the hybrid pattern here, working closely with the studio's employer branding efforts around major hiring pushes and alongside two other recruiters covering different engineering teams. The recruiter reports to the recruiting manager, who reviews pipeline health weekly.

jobs.title: Senior Studio Recruiter
jobs.summary:
Full-cycle recruiting for the Vancouver studio's growing live-ops and player support teams falls to this senior recruiter role, covering everything from initial intake conversations with hiring managers through offer negotiation. Vancouver's talent acquisition team carries this seat, one of the busier requisition loads on the team most quarters.

Running a full requisition load independently anchors the role, coaching less experienced hiring managers through structured interviewing and spotting where the current process creates unnecessary drop-off among strong candidates. Reworking the studio's technical interview loop for support and operations roles, which currently mirrors the engineering process despite assessing different skills, is a specific initiative this year. You also represent the studio at regional hiring events.

Required: strong interview coordination and offer negotiation experience, comfort managing multiple candidate pipelines at once, and stakeholder management skill to coach hiring managers who are new to structured interviewing. Five to eight years in full-cycle recruiting is the tenure this seat is benchmarked against. Games industry background is useful but not required if full-cycle recruiting experience is strong.

The hybrid schedule keeps you at the Vancouver studio part of the week, and success is measured through both time-to-fill and new-hire retention past the first year. The recruiter reports to the engineering recruiting lead and works alongside one coordinator who handles scheduling and offer logistics day to day.

jobs.title: Engineering Recruiting Lead
jobs.summary:
Coordinating hiring priorities across Northfen's Montreal, Helsinki and Vancouver engineering teams takes someone who can see the whole picture rather than just one studio's immediate needs, and that coordination is the core of this recruiting lead role. Northfen's central people team is home to this seat, sitting one level above the individual studio recruiting teams.

Four recruiters report into this seat, each aligned to a specific studio location; the job is setting shared standards for interview process and candidate experience while allowing enough local flexibility for each studio's hiring culture. Personally handling the most senior and sensitive searches, including engineering leadership roles, while your team covers individual contributor hiring, is expected. You also own the recruiting team's own hiring and onboarding as the function keeps growing.

Required: recruiting operations experience spanning multiple locations, real team leadership managing other recruiters, and process design skill to standardize practice without erasing local differences. This is a lead-level seat, scoped to managing four recruiters and the most senior searches directly, rather than defined by a years threshold, though prior people-management experience is expected. Fluency in a language beyond English is a plus but not required.

Travel to each studio location roughly once a quarter comes with the job, otherwise working arrangements are flexible across North America. The lead reports directly to the VP of People, sits in on final-round interviews for engineering leadership searches, and is based out of Montreal when not traveling.

jobs.title: Business Development Representative
jobs.summary:
Independent game studios evaluating multiplayer backend providers rarely respond to a first cold email, and this role builds the outbound pipeline that eventually turns into qualified conversations for Northfen's account executive team. Montreal's sales development team owns this seat, the entry point every lead passes through before an account executive sees it.

Researching target studios by genre, team size and current backend provider comes first, followed by structured outreach campaigns across email and relevant developer community channels. Qualifying inbound interest from the developer relations team's content, to separate real integration timelines from casual browsing, is a meaningful part of the role. You track every touchpoint in the CRM and hand off qualified opportunities to account executives with enough context that the first sales call does not start from zero.

Required: comfortable, persistent cold outreach ability, working knowledge of CRM tools such as Salesforce, and sound judgment for lead qualification under a steady volume of inbound and outbound activity. Call it a year or two of prospecting, sales or customer-facing experience, enough to handle rejection without losing momentum. Prior experience specifically selling into game studios is not required.

The representative works onsite at the Montreal studio, full time, closely alongside both the sales and developer relations teams, and shares a weekly pipeline review with two other representatives. The role reports to the sales development manager, who reviews call recordings weekly and helps refine outreach scripts that stop converting.

jobs.title: Platform Partner Engineer
jobs.summary:
Larger partner studios integrating Northfen's backend platform sometimes need custom integration work that goes beyond what standard SDK documentation covers, and this senior engineer role is the technical bridge between those partners and Northfen's platform engineering team. This seat lives inside Vancouver's platform engineering group, near the backend teams partners build against.

Custom integration solutions for the platform's largest partners are scoped, and sometimes built directly, alongside a review of partner integration architecture for scalability concerns before they become production incidents. Representing partner technical requirements in internal roadmap discussions and building internal tooling that makes future integrations faster to scope and support are ongoing threads of the role. You also run a quarterly partner advisory session gathering structured feedback for the roadmap.

Required: solution architecture experience across partner or third-party API integrations, strong technical presentation skill for partner-facing work, and enough backend engineering depth to review architecture for scalability concerns credibly. Five to eight years in backend or partner engineering is the tenure this seat is built around. Prior experience specifically in the games industry is not required.

Occasional travel to partner studio offices aside, the role is onsite at the Vancouver studio and full time, for deeper technical work sessions when email and video calls are not moving a partnership fast enough. The engineer reports to the head of platform engineering and works alongside two other partner engineers covering different regions.

jobs.title: Claims Systems QA Engineer
jobs.summary:
Miscalculated payouts in Stonebrook Assurance's claims automation engine are not just bugs, they are money that either leaves the company incorrectly or leaves a policyholder underpaid, and this senior QA role exists to catch those errors before a single claim processes incorrectly in production. Claims quality engineering owns this seat, standing between a code change and a policyholder's payout.

Automated regression suites in Java cover the claims calculation engine, with particular attention to how policy terms, state-specific insurance regulations and payout rules interact as they change more often than most software teams expect. Expanding test coverage ahead of each quarterly regulatory update cycle, when claims logic often needs adjustment across multiple jurisdictions at once, is a recurring project. You work with actuarial and compliance teams to translate regulation into concrete test scenarios.

Required: strong Java test automation experience, a working CI/CD setup for regression suites, and enough familiarity with claims workflows to write scenarios that reflect how a claim actually moves through the system. Five to eight years in test automation or QA engineering is the rough experience window for this seat. Insurance-specific domain background is useful but not required, provided the automation fundamentals are strong.

Fully remote within Europe, the team runs an especially thorough release process around regulatory deadline dates given the financial and compliance stakes involved. You maintain a shared library of jurisdiction-specific test fixtures for the wider engineering team, and report to the claims quality engineering lead.

jobs.title: Underwriting API Developer Advocate
jobs.summary:
Insurance carriers and brokers integrating Stonebrook's underwriting API are typically working within their own legacy policy administration systems, and this freelance advocate role exists to make that often-awkward integration path smoother. This engagement is commissioned by developer relations, the team fielding integration questions from carriers and brokers worldwide.

Sample integrations covering the most common carrier core systems Stonebrook's customers use are yours to build and maintain, alongside onboarding guides that account for the compliance documentation carriers typically require before connecting a third-party API. Answering technical questions in the developer support forum is a steady part of the work. Joining onboarding calls for larger carrier prospects, to answer technical questions the sales engineering team cannot fully address alone, is a recurring piece of the engagement.

Required: experience writing API documentation and sample code that a carrier's own engineers can adapt quickly, developer advocacy background, and comfort presenting technical material on onboarding calls. Three to five years in developer relations, integration engineering or a related technical role is the tenure this engagement expects. Insurance industry background is helpful but not required if API integration experience is strong.

Hourly and remote, the engagement is open globally and structured around a rolling monthly scope tied to the current onboarding pipeline, with hours concentrated around live onboarding calls rather than a fixed schedule. The advocate reports to the head of developer relations and coordinates directly with sales engineering on active prospect calls.

jobs.title: Policy Platform Customer Success Engineer
jobs.summary:
Insurers running their policy administration on Stonebrook's platform depend on it for something as basic as issuing a new policy correctly, and this senior customer success engineer role owns a portfolio of mid-size insurer accounts navigating that dependency day to day. London's customer success team holds this seat, one of several portfolios split across the region's insurer accounts.

Quarterly technical reviews covering platform adoption and configuration health anchor the job, alongside proactively flagging accounts using outdated policy templates that create unnecessary manual work and coordinating with professional services when an account needs a larger configuration change. Insurance products vary significantly by line of business, from auto to property to specialty lines, so developing genuine fluency in how each account's products are configured matters more than general platform knowledge.

Required: solid Salesforce fluency for account and case tracking, hands-on experience with policy administration systems, and customer success planning skill applied to a technical, configuration-heavy product. Five to eight years in customer success engineering or a related technical account role is the experience level this seat is built around. Specific insurance underwriting experience is not required, though comfort reading a policy schedule is.

London office attendance is hybrid, and success here is measured through account health scores and a reduction in configuration-related tickets across the portfolio. You also work closely with the renewals team, providing the technical narrative behind expansion conversations, and report to the manager of customer success engineering.

jobs.title: Claims Technical Account Manager
jobs.summary:
Large insurer accounts route their highest-value claims through Stonebrook's automation engine, and this senior technical account manager role is the named point of contact those accounts rely on when something in that critical path needs attention. A small claims technical account team in London is responsible for this seat, covering only a short list of the largest accounts.

Deep technical familiarity with each assigned account's claims configuration is the foundation here, paired with coordinating custom rule requests with the claims engineering team and leading quarterly reviews that walk stakeholders through platform performance and upcoming regulatory changes relevant to their jurisdictions. Expect to be pulled into escalations directly when a claims issue affects live payouts, since these accounts expect an owner who already understands their setup rather than a generic support queue.

Required: strong Salesforce and claims systems fluency, escalation management experience under real time pressure, and the technical documentation discipline to record configuration decisions that later interactions depend on. Five to eight years in technical account management, ideally with claims or insurance systems, is about the tenure this seat assumes. Fluency in a second European language is a plus but not required.

Remote within Europe, the role calls for comfort working occasionally under real pressure when a claims issue is actively affecting policyholders. You also maintain a shared regulatory calendar across accounts, since one jurisdiction's rule change often affects several insurers in the portfolio at once, and report to the director of claims technical accounts, based out of London.

jobs.title: Support Operations Analyst
jobs.summary:
Support ticket data at Stonebrook has historically lived in three disconnected systems, making it hard for support leadership to answer basic questions about where the team's time actually goes, and this analyst role exists to fix that visibility gap. Keeping that gap closed falls to Dublin's support operations team, the group every other department calls when response-time numbers get questioned.

Consolidating reporting across the ticketing system, the phone support platform and the internal escalation tracker into one operational dashboard is the first project, reviewed weekly by support leadership. Building a staffing model that accounts for the seasonal spike in claims-related tickets following major weather events, since current staffing reacts to volume rather than anticipating it, is a further piece of the job. You also benchmark response times against the contractual SLA commitments for the largest enterprise accounts.

Required: strong SQL for pulling data across disconnected systems, solid reporting and data analysis skill, and process improvement experience applied to a support queue under contractual deadlines. Three to five years in support operations, business operations or analytics is the window this seat targets, comfortable pulling clean numbers from messy source systems. Insurance industry background is not required.

The busiest stretch of the month lands in its first week, when reporting is due; otherwise the role runs full time onsite at the Dublin office. You also flag any account trending toward an SLA breach before it happens, and report to the manager of support operations, who reviews the dashboard with you each Monday before it goes to wider leadership.

jobs.title: Enterprise Escalation Engineer
jobs.summary:
Stonebrook Assurance's policy administration platform serves large insurer accounts, and this senior role sits at the boundary between first-line support and engineering, taking on the escalations that first-line cannot resolve alone. It exists because those escalations need someone who can read the platform's internals, not just relay a customer's description of the symptom.

Escalated tickets are yours to own: you dig into the platform's diagnostic tooling to tell a genuine defect apart from a customer-side configuration issue, then loop in engineering to push a fix through. You write plain-language status updates for account teams, since insurer stakeholders need clarity, not engineering detail, and log cases in a shared knowledge base so nobody rediscovers the same root cause twice. Monthly, you run a retrospective with first-line support to catch patterns earlier.

Required: five to eight years in escalation management, incident response, or senior support engineering, with enough SQL to query production data yourself instead of waiting on someone else to pull it. You should be able to turn a technical root cause into a status update a non-technical account manager can repeat to a client verbatim, and be comfortable being the person teams call when a fix is running late. Prior insurance experience is not required; the diagnostic habits transfer, and the domain specifics come with time.

London-based and hybrid, with a few days a week in person expected rather than a fixed schedule. Escalations do not wait for business hours, so occasional availability outside the standard day comes with the seat when something high-severity is live. You report to the escalation team lead and work daily alongside first-line support and the engineering groups that own the platform's core services.

jobs.title: Insurance Tech Sourcer
jobs.summary:
Engineers who understand both software and the regulatory weight of insurance technology are hard to find, and this six-month contract sourcing role exists to build Stonebrook a deeper pipeline for its hardest engineering searches. The seat sits inside the recruiting team but is scoped narrowly: pipeline-building for roles that have stayed open the longest, not full-cycle recruiting.

Most of your week goes to direct outreach: finding engineers with insurtech or fintech backgrounds across LinkedIn and niche industry communities, qualifying their interest and fit, and handing warm candidates to the recruiting team rather than running the interview process yourself. Boolean search and a tidy ATS keep the pipeline from going stale. The current focus is claims engineering, the team's longest-open search, and you report weekly on pipeline volume to the recruiting manager.

Required: three to five years of technical sourcing experience, fluency with Boolean search strings, and daily comfort in an ATS and LinkedIn Recruiter. You should be able to read an engineering job description well enough to identify adjacent, transferable backgrounds rather than sourcing keyword matches only. Insurance industry experience is a plus, not a requirement; general fintech or regulated-industry sourcing background is an acceptable substitute.

The engagement is remote and fixed-term, running through the end of the current hiring cycle, open to candidates anywhere in North America. There is no office requirement and no fixed hours beyond overlapping enough with the Hartford-based recruiting team for a weekly pipeline review. You report to the recruiting manager and coordinate closely with the two recruiters covering claims engineering.

jobs.title: Executive Search Recruiter
jobs.summary:
Stonebrook's engineering leadership team is expanding to support two new insurance lines, and this senior contract role is scoped entirely to those director- and VP-level searches rather than the broader hiring pipeline. It sits apart from the individual-contributor recruiting team by design, since confidential leadership searches need a different pace and a different level of discretion.

Longlists come from direct outreach and executive network research; you carry candidates through an extended process that, for the most senior roles, includes the CEO and board members. Some searches involve restructuring leadership before that is public internally, so discretion matters. You also coach hiring executives on assessing candidates against Stonebrook's scaling challenges, and brief the CEO before each finalist interview to keep the panel aligned.

Required: five to eight years of executive search experience, ideally within technology or financial services, including confidential searches and offer negotiation at the director level or above. You should be comfortable managing stakeholders as senior as a CEO without needing close supervision on how to run the conversation. A background specifically in insurance is not required; general regulated-industry executive search experience covers the gap.

Remote and fixed-term, the contract runs for the length of the leadership expansion rather than a fixed calendar term, open to candidates across North America. There is no office requirement, though most searches originate from and report back to Stonebrook's Hartford-based executive team. You work independently between check-ins with the CEO and the head of talent.

jobs.title: Engineering Recruiting Manager
jobs.summary:
Six recruiters now report into Stonebrook's engineering recruiting function with no manager above them, and that gap is what this role is created to close. You would be the first person to give the team consistent process and real leadership rather than six people independently improvising their own approach to the same hiring targets.

Day-to-day management covers setting hiring priorities with engineering leadership, running the team's recruiting operations, and personally taking the most senior or sensitive searches while the team covers the rest. A first project is standardizing the interview process across engineering, which varies enough to create an inconsistent candidate experience. You also own headcount planning for the team and track whether the quarterly diversity review shows real pipeline change.

Required: five or more years in technical recruiting with direct people-management experience, fluency administering an ATS, and enough process design instinct to turn six different personal styles into one team standard without flattening what works. You should be comfortable representing capacity constraints honestly to engineering leadership rather than overcommitting on timelines. Prior experience specifically in insurance or financial services is not required.

The role runs hybrid out of the London office, three days a week rather than fully remote. This posting is open to internal candidates first as part of Stonebrook's internal mobility program before opening more broadly. You report to the VP of Talent, manage a team of six recruiters directly, and coordinate closely with engineering leadership on hiring priorities each quarter.

jobs.title: Talent Operations Analyst
jobs.summary:
Recruiting data at Stonebrook currently lives mostly in individual recruiters' heads, and this senior analyst role exists to turn that into structured, reportable process as the recruiting function professionalizes. It sits inside talent operations, working across the ATS, quarterly planning reports, and the compensation data recruiters use to build offers.

You own the ATS configuration and data quality, build the reporting leadership relies on for quarterly planning, and design process changes based on where candidates drop out of the pipeline. A current project is building a time-to-fill benchmark by role type and seniority to replace a blended metric that hides real gaps between engineering and go-to-market hiring. You also train recruiters on consistent ATS use to fix reporting's biggest obstacle.

Required: five to eight years in recruiting operations or a similar analytics role, hands-on ATS administration experience, and enough data analysis skill to build a benchmark report from scratch rather than only update an existing template. You should be comfortable training recruiters on process without formal authority to enforce it. Deep insurance industry knowledge is not required; the reporting and data problems here are generic to any scaling recruiting function.

Working arrangements are flexible within Europe, based from Dublin. The role works most closely with the wider recruiting team during the final weeks of each quarter, when planning reviews are due, and otherwise sets its own schedule around the reporting calendar. You report to the head of talent operations.

jobs.title: VP of Revenue Operations
jobs.summary:
Sales, customer success, and renewals data at Stonebrook live in systems that do not talk to each other cleanly, and fixing that fragmentation while the company expands into new insurance lines is the mandate behind this executive seat. The VP of Revenue Operations owns the systems, process, and analytics underneath the entire go-to-market organization.

You lead a team of eight across sales operations, deal desk, and revenue analytics, and personally own the forecasting process the CRO presents to the board each quarter. The first-year mandate is consolidating CRM, billing, and renewal systems that grew up separately across the company's original and newly acquired insurance lines into one coherent data model. You also partner with finance on compensation plan design and with product on usage-based pricing as the company's offerings expand.

Required: prior experience building or running a revenue operations function at a scaling B2B software company, hands-on Salesforce administration knowledge, and the executive presence to present forecasts directly to a board when asked. This is a scope-defined leadership seat rather than a years-of-tenure one: what matters is having already built this function once, not a specific year count. Deep insurance-sector background is not required, provided the go-to-market systems experience is real.

London-based on a hybrid basis, the role reports directly to the Chief Revenue Officer and sits on the executive leadership team. Success is judged against forecast accuracy and the operational efficiency of the broader go-to-market organization, not a fixed set of weekly deliverables.

jobs.title: Sales Engineering Manager
jobs.summary:
Insurance carrier evaluations of Stonebrook's platform almost always come down to a technical proof of concept run against real anonymized claims data, and this manager role leads the five sales engineers who build and run those evaluations across the company's largest opportunities.

Part of the job is setting technical qualification standards for which deals get full sales engineering support, alongside coaching the team through complex proof-of-concept design and stepping into the most strategic deals when needed. You also work closely with product, since that feedback signals where the platform's gaps sit against carrier requirements. Elsewhere, you own the onboarding curriculum, a near six-month ramp you are expected to shorten, and represent the team in quarterly roadmap reviews.

Required: five or more years in sales engineering with direct team-leadership experience, working knowledge of CPQ and Salesforce, and enough sales process design background to set qualification standards rather than just follow them. Hiring is a recurring part of the role as the team grows alongside new insurance lines, so comfort running a structured interview loop matters. Insurance-specific proof-of-concept experience is useful but not required; strong general enterprise sales engineering background is an acceptable substitute.

Out of the Hartford office on a hybrid basis, with regular travel to carrier customer sites for the largest proof-of-concept engagements. Compensation includes a team-performance-linked bonus component on top of base salary. You report to the VP of Sales Engineering and manage a team of five directly.

jobs.title: Sales Engineering Intern
jobs.summary:
