Most internships do not put you inside a real enterprise sales cycle, and that direct exposure is the point of this summer placement on Stonebrook's sales engineering team. You sit alongside the team preparing demo environments and researching prospect accounts rather than observing from a separate training track.

Early weeks are spent supporting senior sales engineers: preparing demo environments, building slide decks that translate platform capabilities for a carrier's business stakeholders, and researching accounts ahead of discovery calls. As the internship progresses you take on a small proof-of-concept project under close supervision, and sit in on live customer calls to see how the team handles objections. A capstone project closes the summer: presenting a mock proof-of-concept plan to the team for feedback.

Required: familiarity with Salesforce or a comparable CRM from coursework or a prior internship, comfort presenting to a room, and genuine interest in enterprise software sales rather than pure engineering. No professional sales engineering experience is expected or required; this is an entry point, not a role that assumes prior industry time. Insurance knowledge specifically is not required and will be picked up on the job.

Twelve weeks, paid, and based onsite at the Hartford office, full time alongside the sales engineering team for the whole term. A structured mentorship program pairs you with a senior engineer for the duration, and the schedule follows standard business hours, with no travel required and no prior internship experience assumed going in.

jobs.title: Pre-Sales Solutions Consultant
jobs.summary:
Carriers evaluating a new claims or policy administration platform almost always want a working proof of concept configured against their own product lines first, and this senior contract role exists to run those engagements for Stonebrook's largest active opportunities over the next six months.

Most engagements start with configuring demo environments around a prospect's actual policy structures and rating rules, then move into leading technical discovery sessions and building the business case materials an account executive uses to justify the deal internally. Each engagement is paired one-to-one with an account executive rather than run independently. You also debrief every proof of concept with the product team, since patterns across engagements often reveal where the configuration tools still need manual workarounds.

Required: five to eight years in pre-sales, solutions consulting, or a similar technical customer-facing role, ideally with exposure to underwriting or policy administration systems, and demonstrated RFP support experience. You should be able to build a credible business case document without a template handed to you. Direct insurance carrier experience is helpful but not required if the underwriting systems background is otherwise solid.

Remote across North America for a six-month contract term, with the possibility of extension based on deal timing. Occasional travel is expected for onsite proof-of-concept kickoffs at the largest prospect accounts. You work under an account executive on each engagement and report progress to the pre-sales team lead.

jobs.title: Booking Platform QA Analyst
jobs.summary:
Double-booked hotel rooms caused by a race condition in the reservation engine are exactly the kind of bug this QA role exists to catch before they reach a front desk. The role sits with the team testing Aldercrest's booking platform, the reservation and availability engine every property depends on.

Testing focuses on the booking platform's reservation and availability logic: overlapping date ranges, last-minute cancellations, and rate changes mid-booking, worked manually against staging. Bug reports go into Jira, and you work directly with booking engine engineers to verify fixes before each release. You maintain the regression checklist the team runs before every release, updating it as new scenarios surface, and join the monthly bug bash ahead of major releases.

Required: a couple of years of hands-on manual testing experience on a transactional or booking-style system, comfort designing test cases for edge conditions rather than only following a script, and daily fluency in Jira. Exploratory testing instinct matters more here than test automation experience, which this particular role does not require at all. Prior hospitality industry background is not expected, since the testing skills transfer directly from any booking, ticketing, or transactional platform.

The role is full-time and fully remote within North America. The team ships booking engine updates on a biweekly cadence, with a release freeze around major holiday booking windows when testing focus shifts to stability over new coverage. You report to the QA lead and coordinate daily with the booking engine team.

jobs.title: Release Quality Engineer
jobs.summary:
Aldercrest ships its property management and point-of-sale products on a regular release train, and this freelance role exists to strengthen the regression testing that happens in the days before each release reaches hotel and restaurant customers. The engagement sits alongside the permanent QA team rather than replacing it.

Executing the release regression suite across both products is the daily work, prioritizing testing time toward whatever changed most recently, and coordinating with engineering on whether a newly discovered issue should block the release or ship with a documented workaround. Part of the assignment is turning the currently ad hoc release checklist into a repeatable process a permanent hire can eventually take over. You work inside the team's CI/CD pipeline to see what changed in a given build rather than testing blind.

Required: three to five years of regression testing or release-management experience, familiarity with CI/CD pipelines well enough to trace a build's changes, and bug triage judgment sharp enough to call a blocking issue correctly under time pressure. Test automation scripting is not required, since this engagement is scoped around structured manual regression rather than building new automated coverage. Hospitality software experience is a plus, not a prerequisite.

Structured as a rolling three-month freelance engagement, remote and project-based, open to candidates across North America. Availability is expected to concentrate in the specific days immediately before each release, with lighter demands between release cycles. You report into the QA lead alongside the permanent regression team.

jobs.title: Developer Educator
jobs.summary:
Hotel and restaurant technology teams integrating Aldercrest's property management API typically have less dedicated engineering support than a typical software customer, and this senior role exists to teach them what documentation alone cannot. The seat sits within developer relations, building structured training rather than one-off answers.

Designing and delivering training, including live workshops and self-paced video courses, is the core of the job: walking partners through patterns for booking sync, POS integration, and guest data. Curriculum development means turning patterns from onboarding calls into proactive content instead of repeating the same explanation. You also build the advanced certification track from scratch and revise it using attendee feedback after every workshop.

Required: five to eight years combining technical writing, developer advocacy, or a similar teaching-adjacent engineering role, with demonstrated experience designing curriculum rather than only delivering existing material. You need to be comfortable presenting live to a mixed room of engineers and less technical operations staff, since Aldercrest's partner base spans both. Deep hospitality industry knowledge is not required going in.

Fully remote within North America and full-time, with occasional travel to run in-person training sessions at partner conferences. Success is measured by a reduction in basic integration support tickets from trained partners, not a fixed number of workshops delivered. You report to the head of developer relations.

jobs.title: Integration Sample Code Engineer
jobs.summary:
Partner developers copy working sample code far more than they read prose documentation when integrating Aldercrest's booking and POS APIs, and this freelance engineering role is scoped entirely around building and maintaining that sample code library. It sits inside developer relations.

Writing reference implementations for the most common integration patterns, in whichever languages Aldercrest's partner base uses most, takes up most of the work, along with keeping those samples current as the underlying APIs evolve. You also answer sample-code-specific questions in the developer support forum, telling genuine sample bugs apart from partners misapplying a pattern to their own architecture. Git fluency matters here since samples live in version control and partners reference specific commits.

Required: three to five years writing production-quality integration or sample code, comfortable API integration experience across REST-style services, and daily Git fluency. Practical coding ability matters more than polished technical writing for this particular role, and long-form documentation writing is not required beyond clear code comments. Prior hospitality-sector experience is not expected, since the integration patterns here are generic across booking and point-of-sale APIs alike.

Hourly and remote, open globally, structured around a rolling scope tied to the current API roadmap rather than a fixed end date. Hours flex with roadmap demand, with no fixed daily schedule beyond reasonable overlap with the developer relations team for questions. You report into the developer relations lead.

jobs.title: Property Success Manager
jobs.summary:
Independent hotels and boutique restaurant groups using Aldercrest's platform typically have no dedicated IT team of their own, which makes this senior success manager role the closest thing many properties have to ongoing technical guidance. The seat sits in customer success, managing a defined portfolio rather than a rotating queue.

You manage roughly thirty properties, running quarterly check-ins covering both platform adoption and the broader operational questions of running the system day to day. Spotting properties underusing features like automated guest messaging or integrated POS reporting, and guiding them toward adoption rather than waiting to be asked, is a core part of the job. You also coordinate renewal conversations with each account's salesperson and share seasonal playbooks with two regional peers for challenges like holiday staffing or booking surges.

Required: five to eight years in customer success or account management, working knowledge of Salesforce, and enough comfort with property management systems to speak credibly about day-to-day hotel or restaurant operations. You should be able to build a renewal case from operational evidence rather than relationship goodwill alone. Direct hospitality operations experience is useful but not required if the account management background is strong.

The position runs hybrid out of the Miami office. Success is measured through portfolio retention and feature adoption rates across your properties rather than a fixed call quota. You coordinate closely with two other regional success managers and report to the director of customer success, who reviews portfolio health with the group each quarter.

jobs.title: Support Engineering Manager
jobs.summary:
Aldercrest's support team fields everything from a front desk terminal that will not connect to a genuine data sync bug between the booking engine and a property's channel manager, and this manager role leads the eight support engineers who triage that entire range. The seat owns the escalation boundary between support and engineering directly.

Setting team priorities, owning the escalation process, and personally stepping into the rare situations sensitive enough to need management involvement, like a major property considering churn over an unresolved issue, are core to the job. A first project is rebuilding the on-call rotation, which leans too heavily on two senior engineers today, into something more evenly distributed. Weekly one-on-ones, hiring for two open positions this quarter, and aligning with customer success on a shared escalation definition round things out.

Required: five or more years in technical support with direct people-management experience, daily fluency in Zendesk, and enough process improvement instinct to redesign an on-call rotation without burning out the two engineers currently covering it. You should be comfortable managing a team supporting properties across many time zones. Prior hospitality-sector support experience is not required, since the escalation and Zendesk skills transfer directly from any high-volume support desk.

Based onsite at the Miami office, full-time, and open to internal candidates first. You manage a team of eight support engineers directly and report to the director of support, coordinating closely with the customer success organization on shared escalations, and sitting in on the quarterly service-quality review the two teams run together.

jobs.title: Director of Customer Success
jobs.summary:
Customer success at Aldercrest has grown from a handful of account managers into a function spanning onboarding, ongoing success management, and renewals, and this director role exists to give it coherent strategy and leadership for the first time. The seat reports into the executive team rather than up through a single sub-team lead.

The job centers on managing each sub-team's lead, setting the shared metrics the function is measured against, and representing customer success in executive planning alongside sales and product leadership. A major initiative this year is redesigning onboarding for new hotel and restaurant customers, since the current program runs long and creates avoidable early churn. You also own the customer success budget and headcount planning, and chair a monthly cross-functional review to surface systemic issues before they become renewal risk.

Required: demonstrated experience leading a multi-team customer success function, including account health tracking and renewal forecasting at scale, ideally at a B2B software company serving operationally lean customers. This is a scope-based leadership role rather than a specific years-of-tenure one: what matters is having run a function like this before, not a year count. Hospitality-specific experience is not required if the underlying customer success leadership background is solid.

Lisbon-based on a hybrid schedule, full-time. Success is judged against net revenue retention and onboarding time-to-value across the customer base rather than a fixed set of monthly deliverables. You report to the Chief Customer Officer and manage the leads of each customer success sub-team directly.

jobs.title: Guest Support Intern
jobs.summary:
Understanding how hotel front desk staff actually use Aldercrest's platform under real pressure, mid check-in rush or a system hiccup at the worst moment, is something this internship is built around rather than picked up by accident. The placement sits directly on the support team, not in a separate training track.

Handling a queue of straightforward support tickets under close supervision is the daily baseline, alongside shadowing senior support engineers on more complex cases to see how escalation decisions actually get made. Helping maintain the internal knowledge base article library the wider team references daily is an ongoing responsibility. As confidence builds you take on a growing share of tickets independently, with a mentor checking your resolutions before they close.

Required: comfort communicating clearly with frustrated customers, willingness to learn Zendesk and the product from scratch, and genuine interest in technical support as a career path. No professional support experience is expected or required; this internship is designed as a first entry point, not a role assuming prior ticket-queue time. Hospitality industry background is not required, since the troubleshooting and communication skills carry over from any customer-facing job you may already have held.

The internship runs twelve weeks, paid and onsite at the Miami office, full time alongside the support team for the whole term. A mentor is assigned for the duration, and the schedule follows standard business hours with no travel expected. Strong performers are considered first for a full-time support engineer opening at the end of the term.

jobs.title: Employer Brand Specialist
jobs.summary:
Aldercrest's engineering employer brand is close to nonexistent outside job postings themselves, and this entry-level role exists to start building it deliberately as the company competes for technical talent against better-known hospitality technology names. The seat sits inside recruiting, working closely with marketing on tone and channels.

Day to day, you manage the company's presence on employer review platforms and create social and careers-page content showcasing engineering's work, and coordinate logistics for a few regional tech recruiting events. Interviewing engineers about their work and turning that into content that reads as genuine, not generic, is what makes the rest credible. You track basic engagement metrics on published content to lean into formats candidates actually respond to, and work with a handful of volunteer brand ambassadors on the team.

Required: up to two years of experience in marketing, recruiting, or communications, comfort writing for social platforms, and basic event coordination skills. Formal employer branding experience is not required or expected at this level; a strong instinct for what reads as authentic versus generic is what matters most. Design or video editing skills are useful but not necessary, and the recruiting manager will teach the platform-specific tools on the job.

Miami-based with flexible working arrangements across North America, full-time. This is a good entry point into either recruiting or marketing career paths, and you report to the recruiting manager while coordinating with a handful of engineer volunteers and the wider marketing team on shared campaigns, messaging, and timing.

jobs.title: Hospitality Tech Recruiter
jobs.summary:
Aldercrest is hiring across engineering, support, and customer success at once to support its expansion into two new geographic markets, and this six-month contract recruiter role exists specifically to help the permanent team absorb that temporary surge. The seat covers full-cycle recruiting rather than sourcing alone.

You carry a full requisition load across multiple departments, running structured interviews and coordinating offer approvals with hiring managers and the compensation team. Ramping quickly on the company's interview process and candidate scorecards matters here, since the contract timeline does not allow for a long onboarding period. You also feed candidate experience observations back to the permanent recruiting team, flagging process friction as a relatively fresh set of eyes on the pipeline.

Required: three to five years of full-cycle technical or operational recruiting experience, daily fluency in an ATS, and demonstrated offer negotiation experience across multiple department types. You should be able to run a structured interview loop from a scorecard you did not design yourself. Hospitality-sector recruiting experience is a plus but not required, since the departments hiring right now span engineering, support, and customer success alike.

Remote across North America on a fixed-term contract, running through the end of the expansion hiring push. There is no office requirement, though the role coordinates daily with the Miami-based permanent recruiting team. You report to the recruiting manager for the duration of the engagement, with no direct reports of your own.

jobs.title: Property Systems Solutions Engineer
jobs.summary:
Hotel groups evaluating Aldercrest's property management platform usually run a patchwork of existing systems for booking, POS, and guest messaging, and this senior solutions engineer role designs the migration plan that does not require ripping everything out on day one. The seat sits in sales engineering, working opportunities from discovery through technical close.

Most weeks start with technical discovery calls for prospective hotel and restaurant group customers, mapping their existing systems against Aldercrest's integration capabilities, and building phased migration plans that respect a hotel's inability to simply pause operations to switch systems. Writing technical responses to procurement questionnaires, particularly around data security and PCI compliance for payment handling, is a recurring part of the largest deals. You work each opportunity from first discovery call through technical sign-off.

Required: five to eight years in solutions engineering or a similar pre-sales technical role, hands-on experience with property management or comparable operational systems, and enough API integration knowledge to scope a realistic migration rather than a theoretical one. Comfort writing detailed procurement and security responses is expected. Direct PCI certification is not required, though working knowledge of the compliance requirements is.

North America-wide and fully remote, full-time, with occasional travel for onsite discovery at the largest prospective accounts. Success is measured by technical win rate on supported opportunities. You report to the head of solutions engineering and coordinate closely with account executives on each deal.

jobs.title: Customer Onboarding Solutions Engineer
jobs.summary:
Migrating a hotel's existing booking and guest data onto Aldercrest's platform without disrupting live operations is a genuinely technical problem, and this senior solutions engineer role owns that migration process for the company's larger new customers. The seat sits between sales and customer success, picking up once a deal closes.

Scoping data migration requirements during the sales process, building the implementation plan once a deal closes, and leading the cutover alongside the customer's operations team, timed to their slow season, are the core of the work. Legacy data quality issues that only surface mid-migration come up often, and reconciling them takes judgment about what to automate versus fix by hand. You also train the customer's staff during final onboarding weeks and maintain a running checklist of migration pitfalls, updated after every cutover.

Required: five to eight years in solutions engineering, implementation, or a similar technical onboarding role, hands-on data migration experience, and strong technical documentation habits, since the pitfall checklist depends on what you write down. Project coordination skill across a customer's operations team matters as much as the technical migration work itself. Direct hospitality-sector experience is not required.

The role is hybrid out of the Miami office. Success is measured through onboarding timeline accuracy and post-launch support ticket volume rather than a fixed number of migrations completed. You hand off to the ongoing customer success team once a property goes live and report to the head of solutions engineering.

jobs.title: Enterprise Account Solutions Engineer
jobs.summary:
Large hotel chain accounts occasionally need a level of technical customization and integration depth that goes well beyond Aldercrest's standard onboarding process, and this senior contract role is dedicated to exactly those enterprise-scale opportunities for the next eight months. The seat works multi-property rollouts rather than single-site onboarding.

Each engagement starts with technical scoping for a multi-property rollout: designing integration architecture for chains running centralized reservation systems across dozens of properties, and coordinating with engineering when a chain's requirements push past the platform's current capabilities. Direct exposure to chain-level IT leadership brings rigorous procurement and security review, and contract negotiation skill matters once enterprise legal terms enter the conversation.

Required: five to eight years in enterprise solutions engineering or technical account management, working knowledge of Salesforce, and demonstrated experience navigating enterprise procurement and security review cycles. You should be comfortable being the technical counterpart in contract negotiation conversations. Hospitality-sector experience specifically is not required if the enterprise integration background is strong.

Open globally on a flexible contract running roughly eight months, with travel expected for the largest enterprise accounts when in-person technical workshops are needed to keep a deal moving. There is no fixed office or standard working hours beyond overlap with the account teams on active deals. You report to the head of solutions engineering for the duration.

jobs.title: GTM Systems Analyst
jobs.summary:
Go-to-market tooling at Aldercrest, spanning Salesforce, the marketing automation platform, and the billing system, has accumulated enough small inconsistencies that basic reporting questions take longer to answer than they should. This part-time analyst role exists to clean that up incrementally rather than in one large project.

Maintaining data hygiene across the core go-to-market systems, building and updating the dashboards sales and marketing leadership rely on for weekly reviews, and investigating specific data discrepancies flagged by the revenue operations team make up the work. A recurring project is standardizing how leads get tagged by source, which currently varies enough between marketing and sales to make attribution reporting unreliable. You write the SQL queries behind most of the dashboards rather than relying entirely on prebuilt reports.

Required: three to five years combining revenue operations and data analysis work, comfortable SQL for querying and joining data across systems, and hands-on Salesforce administration experience. Marketing automation platform experience is useful but not required if the Salesforce and SQL fundamentals are solid. Deep hospitality-sector knowledge is not necessary, since the reporting problems here look like any scaling go-to-market team's.

Part-time at roughly twenty hours a week, fully remote within North America. The schedule is flexible around the weekly reporting cadence rather than fixed to specific days, and suits someone looking for a lighter weekly commitment. You report to the revenue operations lead and coordinate occasionally with marketing on lead-source tagging.

jobs.title: Senior Search Relevance Engineer
jobs.summary:
Two zero-result search queries in the same week traced back to the same normalization bug not long ago, and catching that pattern faster is a large part of why this senior search relevance role exists on Jobbbler's own demo catalog. The team treats the catalog's search experience as a real product surface, not an afterthought behind the listings.

Improving full-text ranking, location and salary filtering, and deterministic result ordering across a TypeScript service backed by PostgreSQL is most of the work. Offline evaluation pairs with product judgment: a change that raises an aggregate relevance score only matters if an ordinary job seeker can tell results actually improved. You build relevance fixtures, chase zero-result and broad queries to root cause, and work with product and accessibility specialists to keep filters usable for keyboard, screen-reader, and agent clients alike.

Required: five to eight years of backend engineering experience with TypeScript and relational databases, hands-on full-text search or information retrieval work, and enough relevance evaluation background to build a fixture set rather than eyeball result quality. You should be able to trace a search from public tool input through normalization, storage, and rendered output, then document the tradeoffs clearly enough for the next contributor. Prior recruiting-industry domain knowledge is not required.

Full-time and fully remote, open across Europe and the United Kingdom, with a small overlap window set aside for collaborative review rather than fixed daily hours. There is no office to report to. You work closely with product and accessibility specialists and report to the engineering lead for the demo catalog.

jobs.title: Product Manager, Candidate Workflows
jobs.summary:
During an early pilot, a candidate approved a prepared answer without noticing it referenced the wrong employer, and that near miss is why consent and review checkpoints matter so much in the workflow this senior product role now owns end to end. Jobbbler Demo Systems is refining the fictional journey showing how a browser agent drafts answers while the candidate keeps control.

Mapping the smallest useful workflow, from discovering a role through reviewing prepared answers, and resolving ambiguity before it becomes interface clutter, is the center of the job. Success measures are built around saved effort, not superficial engagement metrics. Day to day, you work with design, engineering, privacy, and developer-relations partners to turn protocol capabilities into language an everyday job seeker understands, and you review agent traces from weak and strong models to find where tool descriptions cause mistakes.

Required: five to eight years of product management experience, including workflow design and direct user research, ideally with some exposure to privacy-by-design principles or consent-heavy flows. You should be able to prioritize improvements that help both human and automated clients without maintaining two separate products. Prior experience specifically with AI agent protocols is not required, and can be picked up from the traces themselves.

Full-time and hybrid, based between Berlin and Amsterdam, with remote collaboration filling most of the gaps between the two. There is no fixed in-office schedule beyond what the two-city split naturally requires. This position falls under the head of product.
